rwan was convinced the ring was cursed. At first, the proof came in small doses. There were bad streaks at the card table, sudden pain in her tooth, and stale bottles of mead. Soon, the proof took on a larger, more dangerous form. Her blade would miss its mark. Potions would cure too slowly. Or she'd step on a rune that her barbarian companion, Skjol, had no business skipping over. Then there was the greater proof, the instances that threatened their livelihood. There was the coin drying up, new guard patrols at the usual haunts, and word that the East Empire Company had taken notice of their works. All told it augured a slow, tumbling march toward the end of the Crimson Dirks. Knowing this, a smart person might've cast it out; tossed the foul ring into the heart of Illiac Bay and let the waves ferry it to forgotten shores. A wise person might've taken it a step further, destroying the artifact and its ill-fated magic, so that no person, past or present, would ever come to harm. Erwan, of course, decided to wear it around her neck. With regard to the ring's nature, she told only the barbarian. Her brother Edward would refuse to believe her. The others would demand she get rid of it, in whatever manner best fit their inclinations. Skjol, on the other hand, would neither object nor disapprove. Whenever she confided in him, Skjol would simply stare at her blankly and let out a guttural snort before chewing on the nearest piece of meat. Skjol, after all, was not just a barbarian, but one who wore that label like a badge, or an honor bestowed upon him by the High King. Of words he knew few, and when he wrote them down, rarely did he put them in the right order. The only thng that spared him from further ignominy was the fact he couldn't speak. As the story goes, the leader of the Crimson Dirks, Tyra Blood-Fire, found him in a cage with his tongue removed, and upon freeing him gained his axe. To this day it was never clear if Skjol was loyal to her or the crew, or whether that distinction had any meaning to him. If Tyra asked him to back Erwan on a job, he would do so without question, and absorb whatever secrets, insults, and curses the Breton decided to fling in his general direction. That theory would be tested the moment she stepped on that rune. Earlier that week, they had received a tip. A new crew had set up a smuggler's operation in one of the old ruins outside the capital. It was supposed to be a simple task. They were to meet with the clan leaders, flex their muscle, and come home with new members or a percentage of the take. It all would've gone according to script, Erwan thought, had the ring not been cursed. "This is all your fault," she said to no one in particular, while glaring at her disobedient hands. Moments earlier, the Breton had awoken to the sound of chanting - a low and ominous moan floating through the chamber. The rune had blurred her sight, but it was the haunting refrain that seemed to dull her focus, unable to cast a spell. Regardless, it was clear their captors were more than smugglers. Erwan didn't need to see the source of the chanting to know it was bad business, no matter how long Skjol mindlessly pointed in that direction. "Well, at least it isn't cannibals," Erwan sneered, "although you being a choking hazard might've worked in our favor." Skjol wasn't the brightest Nord, but he knew when he was being insulted. In a past life, he would've simply crushed Erwan's skull and taken a nap. Moreover, cages were nothing new to him, and Erwan's noisy jests were to him, signs of panic. But he had sworn a vow to protect the charges of the one they called Blood-Fire, and so rather than kill the Breton for looking at him oddly, Skjol continued to point, much to Erwan's confusion. The shrine behind her was Daedric in origin - large, twisted and barbed, its stems ugly and misshapen. Blood dripped from its ebony thorns, spilling past the cage and down the stone steps like shifting roots. At the base of the steps stood robed cultists, lost in their supplication, flanked by guards dressed in Daedric armor and mail. Despite an open roof, the air in the ruins was thick and noxious, and the shrine seemed to throb in the blood moon's light. As the light shone on the altar, the cultist chants began to turn more vehement and forceful. The voices continued to rise, louder and louder, until one of the guards broke from his stance, climbing the steps toward the cage. Seeing this, Erwan bared her teeth and snarled at him like an animal, but he continued his approach undeterred. As the chants hit a crescendo, Erwan could no longer hear her own thoughts, seeing nothing save the cold, black gauntlet split through the bars and reach for her neck. With a thrust the guard grabbed her by the head and slammed her into the bars, drawing his weapon with his other hand. With spit bubbling from her mouth and her body pressed against the iron, Erwan screamed at Skjol every manner of insult she could contrive. But the oaf continued to sit in place, his finger still extended, even as the cultists' chant drummed against their ears. Only now the finger was pointed to the ground, tracing a circle. Erwan looked down and saw the ring, glowing hotly on her chest. Skjol didn't need to tell her what to do next. She wrung herself free of the guard's grasp, and not knowing what would happen, placed the ring on her finger. The chanting stopped. And in its place, the shrill cry of weapons drawn from their scabbards. The Daedric warrior turned his attention to the cultists, but it was too late. Erwan's spell of hysteria had taken hold, her focus restored by the power of the ring. One by one the cultists turned on each other, their rage driven by hers. And when the clangs of metal faded and the screams turned to silence, Erwan collapsed, having exhausted all of herself and the ring. As the hours passed into the day, Erwan lay there on the floor of her cage, letting the sun splash through the bars. Skjol snored softly in his corner, shifting on occasion to scratch himself. Outside, ravens picked at the flesh of the dead, sharpening their beaks on the bones and paying no mind to the living. The others would come looking for them eventually, and fetch M'Sharra to pick the lock. But for now Erwan was content as she was. She held the ring up against the sky, circling the area where the moon once stood. Perhaps she had made a mistake, and the ring wasn't cursed after all. But Erwan still held out hope.

埃文确信这枚戒指是被诅咒了。 刚开始，迹象并不明显。无非是打牌抽到烂牌，突然牙疼，喝到变质的蜜酒，后来，迹象就变得越来越明显而且危险了。她的剑砍不中目标，喝药恢复缓慢，甚至会踩上连她的蛮子队友斯科卓都能躲过的符文。 再往后，还有甚至更大的迹象，都是些能在瞬间让她命悬一线的险情：手头的钱逐渐耗尽，更多的卫兵出现在本不该出现的地方，还有传言说，东帝国公司已经注意到了他们的行动。一切都预示着，猩红长匕的末日要不远了。 一般的聪明人意识到这些后，或许会设法自救，把这枚该死的戒指扔进骸骨湾深处，让海浪将其带向无人知晓的地方。有大智慧的人可能还能更进一步，摧毁这枚戒指和其中的厄运魔力，这样无论是现在还是以后，都不会再有人受害。 当然了，埃文是打算继续把它戴在脖子上。 关于戒指的真相，她只告诉了那个野蛮人斯科卓。因为她的同胞兄弟埃德华压根不会相信她，其他人则会不惜一切手段让她丢掉它。但斯科卓却不会表示支持或反对。 每次她对斯科卓讲什么时，斯科卓都只是空洞地盯着她，喉咙哼几声，然后去找块肉嚼。毕竟，斯科卓不止是一个野蛮人，他还把这个标签当做荣誉，好像是至高王授予他的一样。他不认识几个字，写词时也很少能写对字母顺序。还好，他没法说话，使他免于进一步因文盲而受到羞辱。 正如故事所讲的，猩红长匕的首领“血火”提拉在一个笼子里找到了被割掉舌头的斯科卓，并在释放他后得到了他的效忠。没人知道斯科卓到底是只忠心于提拉，还是整个团伙，或者对他来说这俩其实是一码事。如果提拉让他支持埃文的工作，他会毫不质疑地执行，并无视所有那些埃文工作之外搞出来的秘密，侮辱或者诅咒之类的。 当埃文一脚踩进这个符文时，上述理论就要受到检验了。 这周早些时候，他们收到消息，有一伙人在城外的一个古废墟里新设了一个走私站点。这本来是个简单的任务。与团伙首领会面，秀秀肌肉，然后就能带着个新人或者分成回来。埃文想：要是没有这个被诅咒的戒指，一切本应照计划进行。 “这都怪你。”她注视着自己不听使唤的双手，自言自语道。几分钟前，她被吟诵声惊醒，那低沉而不详吟诵声回荡在整个大厅里。那个符文模糊了她的视力，但真正要命的是那吟诵声削弱了她的注意力，让她无法施法。 无论如何，埃文不去看那吟诵声的源头也已明白：囚禁他们的人肯定不是什么一般走私者。她也懒得理会斯科卓朝着声音来源一通乱指了。 “唉，至少他们不是食人族。”埃文冷笑道：“不过你要是被呛死了，倒是帮了我们个大忙。” 斯科卓是个不怎么聪明的诺德，但也知道自己被羞辱了。换在以前，他会直接打烂埃文的脑袋，然后打个盹。此外，囚笼对他来说并不新鲜，而埃文的玩笑在他听起来满是惊慌。但他曾向那个被称为“血火”的人发誓要服从她的指挥。所以他不顾埃文疑惑的视线，继续坚持向吟诵声的方向指着。 她背后的祭坛是典型的迪德拉风格：庞大，扭曲且满是丑陋畸形的尖刺。鲜血从那黑檀尖刺上滴下，像扭动的根须般流过囚笼和石阶。在石阶底部站着一群穿长袍的教徒，正沉浸于祷告中，周围还有一群穿着迪德拉盔甲或链甲的守卫。尽管没有屋顶，可废墟里的空气还是浑浊而有毒，整个祭坛似乎都在血色月光下跳动着。 随着月光的照耀，教徒们的吟诵声越来越响亮有力，声音越来越大，直到其中一名守卫离开位置，爬上阶梯向囚笼走来。埃文像野兽似的露出牙齿低吼，但守卫不为所动。随着吟诵声的影响变强，埃文已经无法思考，除了寒冷以外，只能看见黑色的腕甲伸过栏杆抓向她的脖子。 守卫一手拔出武器，一手猛地一把抓住埃文的头，重重地撞在了囚笼的栏杆上。埃文身子贴在铁栏上，口吐白沫，用她能想到的一切话语咒骂着斯科卓。但即使教徒吟诵的声音在他们耳边声浪汹涌，斯科卓依旧呆若木鸡地坐在原地，伸着手指。只是现在他的手指画着圈，指向了地面。 埃文向下看，发现那枚戒指正在她胸前发出强烈的光芒。 不需要斯科卓再提醒下一步该怎么做。她从守卫手里挣脱，不管三七二十一地把戒指戴到手指上。 吟诵声戛然而止，取而代之的是一片武器出鞘的哀嚎。迪德拉战士把注意力转向了教徒们，但为时已晚，埃文的狂乱术已经在手，她的注意力被戒指的力量恢复了。教徒们在她的驱使下自相残杀。待到武器相交的叮当声和惨叫声终于沉寂，埃文精疲力竭，耗尽了自己和戒指的所有能量。 几小时过去了，埃文瘫倒在囚笼里，任由阳光穿过栏杆洒在身上。斯科卓在笼子里打起了鼾，不时抓挠一下。外面，乌鸦正在尸体上大快朵颐，对活人毫无兴趣。 其他人最终会来找他们的，并让玛’莎拉撬开笼子。但暂时，埃文很满足于现状。她抬起戴戒指的手指，向天空中月亮曾在的位置比划着。或许这次她错了，这枚戒指并没有被诅咒。 但埃文宁愿自己是对的。

<font face="$HandwrittenFont" size="17">
My dearest sister Erwan,

I see your way with words remains as elegant as a falling boulder. I am indeed alive, and no, I haven't forgotten my promise to you, which I remind you again was never literal. 

You see, when someone says, "You'll be the death of me," it's not an invitation to murder. It's more of a loving expression of one's exasperation, but I know nuance has never been your strong suit.

I must warn you, however, that correspondence like this endangers us both. So if you truly wish to keep this promise, it's best you don't respond. When the time is right, I will come to you.

Oh, and be kind to our merchant friend Gunther, will you? Consider him my gift to you, along with this book on our past life.

I'm sure you know by now, but it seems one of us has taken to writing about our adventures. I assure you, it isn't me. But I'm glad his depiction of you is as honest as you are incorrigible.

--Edward</font>
traduit:
<font face="$HandwrittenFont" size="17">
我最亲爱的姐妹埃文：

看到你的话语仍旧如同大石头下落一般优雅我就放心了。我确实还活着，而且没错，我还记得对你的承诺，再提醒你一次，我的承诺从来都不是字面上的。

你看，当某人说：“你会让我死的。”这可不是在邀请我去杀人。这更像是一种愤怒着表达爱的方式，但我知道感知这些细微差异从来都不是你的强项。

不过我得警告你，这样通信只会害了咱俩。所以如果你真想履行那个承诺，最好不要回信。等时机到了，我就去找你。

对咱们的商人朋友冈瑟尔好点。把他当做我给你的礼物，还有这本关于我们过去生活的书也送给你。

我相信你现在已经知道，似乎咱们中有人开始写咱们的冒险经历了。我保证不是我。但我很高兴他如实地描述了你的不可救药。

——埃德华</font>

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
My new friend Gunther and I are getting along quite well. The other bandits are already getting jealous. He really was a fine gift. I should thank my brother Edward before I slit his throat.

The thing I like best about my good friend Gunther? He can keep a secret. I tell him all sorts of juicy tidbits and he never says a thing. He reminds me of my old companion Skjol, and the time we nearly got murdered by a Daedric cult. There was a ton of good loot in that place. Haunted artifacts, blood sacrifices, things that make lesser men want to hug their priest. 

Nothing that would frighten off Gunther though. He's quite stoic, sitting in his chair. On top of that, he gets along with everyone. It doesn't matter if they're short people, fat people, tall people, or cat people. That's the thing about my old friend Gunther, he doesn't judge.

Anyways, when I got to Skyrim, I sold most of the loot we piled up over the years, seeing as wanted men have to travel light. The heaviest piece I sold was a set of Daedric mail, to a caravan Khajiit named Ma'dran. I liked that armor, but in the end I had no choice but to get rid of her. She knows what she did.

Besides, if I wanted to get her back, I could always trade something of equal value, like the Ring of Masser I ripped off the merchant at the Crescent Moons Inn way back when. Me and the furballs, we have history.

The ring is worth at least two sets of armor, or twenty pairs of boots. It can fortify your illusion magic, just like the books say. The books get a lot right, even the parts about me, except I'm much prettier and taller in real life. 

Either way, I don't need to cast spells to run this new crew. So I'll let my best friend Gunther wear the ring. I think it looks really good on him.</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
我和新朋友冈瑟尔相处得很好。其他强盗开始嫉妒了。他真是个好礼物。我应该在割断我兄弟喉咙前好好谢谢他。

我最喜欢我好朋友冈瑟尔什么？他能保守秘密。我告诉他各种花边新闻，他却一言不发。他让我想起老伙计斯乔卓，还有那次差点被迪德拉邪教徒杀害的经历。那地方有好多好东西。可怕的器物、血淋淋的祭品，这些东西足以吓得那些普通人抱紧他们的祭司。

不过没什么能吓退冈瑟尔。他坐在椅子上，非常镇定。最重要的是，他和所有人相处得都不错。不管是高的矮的、胖的瘦的还是猫人。我的老朋友冈瑟尔就是这样，从不评判别人。

无论如何，当我到达天际时，我卖掉了我们多年来积累的大部分战利品，身为通缉犯必须轻装上路。我卖掉的最贵的就属那套迪德拉链甲了，卖给了一个叫玛’德兰的卡吉特商人。我很喜欢那套盔甲，但最后我别无选择，只能摆脱她了。她会明白的。

再说了，如果我想她回来，我可以用同等价值的东西去交换，就像我从前在新月旅店从商人那里抢的那个马瑟尔之戒。我和那群毛团还是有段历史的。

不管怎么样，我不需要法术才能管理新团队。所以我会让我最好的朋友冈瑟尔戴着戒指。我觉得和他很配。</font>

4E 201, 18 Sun's Height
I've been asked to investigate rumors that one of the inns to the west is providing refuge for bandits. Several carriages traveling to Windhelm have gone missing as of late and the captain feels it may be related to the Crimson Dirks. I have some business to finish in Solitude but it shouldn't take longer than a week.

4E 201, 25 Sun's Height
While the patrons at Nightgate Inn were uncooperative and brusque, I don't believe any of them are bandits. I've asked our informant to travel to the inn to confirm, but in the meantime I will continue monitoring their behavior.
[pagebreak]
4E 201, 16 Last Seed
The Bosmer did not recognize the Nord, although I vacillate on whether I trust his opinion. I pointed out that it has been months since he has provided any actionable intelligence on his former cohorts. In response, he conveniently gave up the location of the Argonian bandit, Pale-Eyes, information I feel he has been holding on to for some time.

For now, the Bosmer remains an asset, but any information he provides should be vetted thoroughly. Supposedly, the Argonian is camped on the shoreline, west of Northwatch Keep. We can alert our Thalmor friends to take care of the matter. They won't like having a wanted criminal loitering so close to their stronghold.

In the meantime, I will leave my documentation here in the event further surveillance is needed on the inn patrons. </font>

<font face="$HandwrittenFont" Size="20">
The water does not lie. Every morning I stare at my reflection, and feel myself returning to the Hist. 

When the smoke is thick, ours is to think back to the day I met Ehlhiel for the first time, when Peladius tried to make warriors of the new recruits.

With no coin for armor, I covered myself in pots and pans I found lying around the campfire, determined not to fall behind. But while the others laughed, the Bosmer thought me clever, and from that day on, the two of us were inseparable.

Years later, on my hatch day, Ehlhiel gave me my first set of armor. He had the Orc forge one out of iron, in honor of the cast iron pot I wore on my head the first time we sparred. In return, I made the Bosmer an egg-brother, and vowed that I would protect him as if he were my own kin. 

Thus when Ehlhiel confessed to what he had done, I did not tell a soul. I will protect my egg-brother until the end.

水是不会说谎的。每天早上我凝视自己的倒影，能感觉到自己就要回归希斯特了。

当烟雾弥漫，我们的回忆是第一次见到埃利赫的那天，当时佩拉迪乌斯正试图把新人们培养成合格的战士。

没钱买盔甲，我就在营火边捡来锅碗瓢盆把自己裹起来，也不打算落后。但是当其他人都笑起来时，波斯莫却觉得我很聪明，从那天起，我们俩就形影不离了。

多年后，当我的孵化日到来，埃利赫送了我第一套盔甲。他让那个兽人铁匠用铁锻造了一套，以此纪念我们第一次决斗时我脑袋上顶的铸铁锅。作为回报，我把波斯莫当做了自己的卵生兄弟，并发誓会像保护亲人一样保护他。

因此在埃利赫亲口承认自己所做的一切前，我不会告诉任何人。我会保护卵生兄弟直到最后。

traduit: 夜扉旅店顾客的纸条

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='20'>
I just want to talk about this amazing inn, and how great the service is. The innkeeper is a kind, helpful host, who is so effortless in his laziness that he didn't bother to read past this point.

That's right, this inn is the worst. The literal worst. Of course, even if you can get past the bad service, the garbage food, and the ghost living downstairs, they're also bloody traitors! 

Not only do they rent to filthy Elves, I spotted one of them hide something in a barrel out back. I'd grab it myself, but it's probably covered in some disgusting Elven disease that would take nine of the world's greatest alchemists and a human sacrifice to cure. 

If I weren't a wanted man, I'd burn down the barrel along with this sorry excuse for an inn. For now, this letter will have to do.</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='20'>
我只是想谈谈这家棒极了的旅店，还有这里的服务有多好。老板善良又热情，他的懒惰也是如此毫不费力，以至于他肯定不会费心读这东西。

没错，这家旅店糟透了。糟糕至极。当然，即使你能忍受糟糕的服务、垃圾般的食物和住在楼下的幽灵，他们也是该死的叛徒！

他们不仅租房间给肮脏的精灵，我还发现其中一个精灵在后面的桶里藏了什么的东西。我也想自己去拿，但上面可能有某种恶心的精灵疾病，需要找一群世界上最伟大的炼金师和活人献祭才能治得好。

如果我是通缉犯，我早就用这桶酒把这破旅店点了。现在，留封信也就够了。</font>

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
"Asset." 

That's what the dossier called him. It took a while before I got past that word and found a way to stomach the rest of it. At the time, I was hurt. Now, I'm just mad.

It all started when I killed this officer on a lark. It probably wasn't the smartest thing. They're like cockroaches, you can't kill them all. But I'd be lying if I said it didn't feel good to try.

So it wasn't like I knew what he was up to when I confronted him. I didn't expect to find anything useful on his corpse either. But then I found the dossier, and now I know the truth. Ehlhiel betrayed us. 

Finding the traitorous bastard won't be easy, but I've got a plan. The dossier says they arrange meetings with him by placing a note at the Temple of the Divines, underneath a vase of tundra cotton. I'll place one there and have him meet me at Lost Echo Cave. Then I'll gut the lying little weasel and show him just how much of an asset he really is.</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
“有利用价值”

档案里是这么描述他的。我花了一段时间才忘记这个词，并找到了方法来忍着阅读下面的部分。当时我很受伤。现在，我只是疯了。

一切都是从我开玩笑杀了一个官员开始的。这不明智。他们就像蟑螂一样，杀不完。但如果我说这样干感觉不好，那也是撒谎。

所以我找他对质不是想知道他的想法。我也没想从他的尸体上找到什么有用的东西。但我后来找到了档案，知道了真相。埃利赫背叛了我们。

找到那个叛徒混蛋不容易，但我有计划。档案里说，他们安排会面时，会在圣灵神殿一个带有苔原棉花的花瓶下面放一张纸条。我会去那里放一个，让他到失落回声洞穴见我。到时候我再把这个撒谎的小黄鼠狼开膛破肚，让他看看自己多有价值。</font>

original: Ehlhiel's Journal
traduit: 埃利赫的日记

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
Tyra was too stubborn to realize it. The Crimson Dirks were done. They knew our names and our faces. If the city guard didn't catch us, it'd be The East Empire Company, or any of the other guilds and Great Houses we pissed off along the way. The way I see it, I just gave them a head start.

My job was to set the hideout ablaze, and let the Legionnaires pick off the bandits while they burned. Just goes to show how cowardly the tin men in uniform really are. They were never one for a fair fight or a fair deal, but hey, neither was I.

The guard captain was too busy smelling his own wind to realize we were burning long dead corpses. The Crimson Dirks were already gone. 

It was an even trade. A head start for a head start. So long as I kept my part of the bargain, they wouldn't find out about theirs. 

Still, it was only a matter of time before they caught on. And while they weren't aware of my part in the escape, now they want me to help with their capture. They've put everything I've told them into neat little dossiers, which they can pass around to the captains. I wonder if they even have one on me.

I only told Pale-Eyes about the cost of our freedom. The rest of them wouldn't understand. They couldn't deal with the guilt. But I had to tell somebody, because as it turns out, neither could I.</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
提拉太固执了，没有意识到猩红长匕已经完蛋了。他们已经知道了我们的名字和长相。如果城市卫兵没有抓住我们，那东帝国公司也会出手，也可能是我们这一路上惹过的其他公会或者大家族。在我看来，我只是给了他们一个先机。

我的任务是烧毁藏身处，让军团兵一边烧一边杀。这就说明这些披着官皮的东西有多胆小。他们从来不会公平决斗或者公平交易，但是，嘿嘿，我也不会。

卫兵队长忙于闻身边的风，没有意识到我们烧着的是早已死去的尸体。猩红长匕早已远走高飞。

这是个公平的交易。先机换先机。只要我遵守了承诺，他们就不会发现他们。

不过他们追上来只是时间问题。他们之前不知道我参与了逃亡，现在还想让我帮忙抓他们。他们把我提供的情报编撰成了整齐的档案，然后发给队长们。也不知道里面有没有我的那份。

我们自由的代价我只告诉了苍白之眼。其他人是不会理解的。他们无法处理负罪感。但我必须和别人聊聊，因为事实证明，我也没法处理。</font>

original: Guard's Dossier: Ehlhiel
traduit: 卫兵档案：埃利赫

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
Status: Asset (cooperative), Active

Description: Male, Bosmer, late 30s

Background:
Ehlhiel was adopted by the Crimson Dirks at a young age and trained at their hideout in the Heartlands of Cyrodiil. Some intelligence suggests his parents may have been killed by the bandits, and the child taken in as hostage.

Operational Notes:
Originally identified as a possible mole due to his background, Ehlhiel was fed the information regarding his parents and recruited as an asset. In the years following, he proved to be a valuable source of information in identifying bandit groups, as well as helping the Imperial City guard expunge the Crimson Dirks from Cyrodiil.

Currently, Ehlhiel continues to serve both the East Empire Company and the guard captains in Skyrim by providing information on fugitives that fled north after the purge. Meetings can be set up by placing a note behind the Shrine of Akatosh in Solitude. Any additional contact should be arranged through the appropriate channels.</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
状态：有利用价值（合作的），存活

描述：男性波斯莫，年龄30多岁

背景：
埃利赫很小的时候就被猩红长匕收养，并在他们位于希罗帝尔腹地的藏身处接受训练。一些情报显示，他的父母可能是被这群强盗杀害，而孩童时期的他则被劫为人质。

对策说明：
由于他的背景，他最初就有成为内线的可能性，他得到了与父母有关的消息，并接受招募成为线人。在接下来的几年里，他确实是个有价值的信息来源，帮助帝国城市卫兵识别强盗组织并从希罗帝尔清除猩红长匕。

目前，埃利赫继续为东帝国公司和天际的卫兵队长们服务，提供清洗后逃亡北方的要犯信息。如需会面可在独孤城的圣灵神殿阿卡托什祭坛后安放纸条。应通过适当渠道安排额外的接触活动。</font>

original:

Status: Active (Capture or Kill), High Priority

Background:
Yakhtu gra-Orkulg was a former blacksmith at the Stash 'N Slash in the Imperial City, a shop she inherited from her father. She was contacted by the Crimson Dirks and recruited to forge arms for the bandits as well as launder sacked goods through her shop. When the Imperial City guard issued a warrant for her arrest, she fled the city with another member of the bandit gang.  

Operational Notes:
Yakhtu was originally thought to have fled to High Rock and taken refuge in an Orc Stronghold. However, according to our informant, she actually traveled with another agent to Skyrim. Reports of unusually well made weapons and armor being peddled out of Embershard Mine may be related. This information should be forwarded to Commander Caius in Whiterun as the mine falls under his jurisdiction.</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
状态：存活（应抓捕或击杀），高优先级

描述：女性兽人，年龄40岁左右

背景：
亚克图·格拉-欧库格曾是名铁匠，从父亲手里继承了帝都的“贮藏与劈砍”店铺。后来猩红长匕联系了她，招募她为强盗们打造武器装备，并通过她的商店洗货。当帝都卫兵发出逮捕令时，她与团伙另一名成员逃离了帝都。

对策说明：
亚克图起初被认为是逃到了高岩，并前往某兽人要塞避难。然而据我们的线人说，她实际上是和另一名成员一起逃到天际了。有消息称，从碎火矿场流出的精良装备可能与她有关。矿场隶属白漫管辖范围，这一情报应传达给凯尤斯指挥官。</font>

original: Yakhtu's Journal
traduit: 亚克图的日记

original:
<font face="$HandwrittenFont">
I nearly turned around and went back to Cyrodiil because Bjormund wouldn't shut up. From dawn to dusk it was Skyrim this and Skyrim that. We hadn't even crossed the mountains yet, and I felt like I'd spent an eternity in the place. But by Malacath, he kept going.

He went on about all the different legends and the hundreds of Ragnars involved in them. He talked for hours about his family, and for days about his mead. Sometimes he even sang about them. Silence was not an option. Perhaps if they put that on my bounty, I might have been okay with the rest of it. 

But as a blacksmith, there was one story I didn't get tired of. The one about the Skyforge.

"It's an ancient relic, watched over by a great stone eagle," he said. "Come spring, you will be forging weapons under its wings," he said.

I ate it up, even though I knew it was a lie. The Skyforge was for legendary smiths, and I was a wanted criminal. Unless the guard decide to quit looking for us, I was going to spend the rest of my life crafting Orcish Plate for bandits, idiots who didn't deserve my work and lacked the brains to value it.

Maybe that's what pissed me off the most about Bjormund's tales of hearth and home. We weren't going to be welcome in Skyrim, or anywhere for that matter. We were Crimson Dirks. We had a home, and now it was gone.</font>
traduit:
<font face="$HandwrittenFont">
因为布乔蒙德一直叽叽喳喳，我差点扭头回希罗帝尔。从黎明到黄昏，天际这，天际那。我们还没翻过山脉。但玛拉凯斯在上啊，他还在逼逼。

他继续讲述着各种不同的传说，里面光是拉格纳我就听了几百次了。他一连说了好几小时关于自己家庭的事，又一连谈了好几天蜜酒。有时候，他甚至还会因为这些东西唱歌。沉默不是个选择。也许如果他们为此加重我的赏金，我也会接受。

但作为铁匠，有个故事却让我乐此不疲。就是关于天空锻炉那个。

他说：“那是个古老的遗迹，上面有一只巨大的石鹰守护，到了春天，你就能在它的翅膀下锻造武器了。”

尽管我知道这就是个谎言，但我还是信了。天空锻炉是为传奇铁匠们准备的，可我是个通缉犯。除非卫兵们不再搜捕我们，否则我这辈子都要给这群强盗打造兽人板甲了，这些白痴不配使用我的作品，也没有脑子去珍惜它们。

也许这就是布乔蒙德的家庭故事最令我生气的地方。我们在天际还是其他地方，都不会受到欢迎。我们是猩红长匕。我们曾经有家，现在却没了。</font>

dward taught Antonius the game he learned in Elsweyr, as Casival, Ehlhiel and Zaharia joined them at the table. A cloth, stained with every conceivable color of wine and spirit, was placed over the top of the wood, allowing the bones and tiles to slide across its otherwise splintered face. While some of the rules were lost in translation, Edward knew enough for the game to function. Moreover, if he were to bend said rules to his favor, his opponents would be none the wiser. "There are two types of games," Edward explained, laying the tiles out on the surface, "those with perfect information, and those that are imperfect. Chess, for example, is a game with perfect information. We know each other's pieces and their placement on the board. Card games, on the other hand, are of the imperfect variety. We are each dealt a hand with a set value, and must divine, through whatever means are available to us, who has the better of it." "And which type do you prefer?" asked Casival. "I prefer to know who and what I'm dealing with," replied Edward, "but at the same time, I know the more practical skill is to play games where the information is imperfect. After all, that is how the world around us is played." "I wasn't aware life was a game," said Ehlhiel, "because if so, I need to find a better way to cheat." "Don't be so modest," replied Edward, raking in another pot, "I think you're doing just fine. The same can't be said for our friend Antonius here." "I only lost because you distracted me," barked Antonius, "with that inhaling and exhaling thing you do with your nose." "Do you mean breathing?" asked Edward. "Yes, that." As a careful study of others, Casival understood the gist of Edward's speech. There were layers beyond what faces advertised. Edward, for instance, used his charm and intellect like a sword, his sly demeanor having a purpose that disarmed his opponents. Ehlhiel, on the other hand, wore his humor like armor, deflecting any inkling of emotion or motive. Zaharia, for all her straightforwardness, was also passionate and sincere, making her prone to falling victim to her temper. Even Antonius, for all his inebriation, was a skilled hedge mage, and one wondered at times if his drunkenness was merely a performance that allowed people to excuse his worst impulses. The same rules applied to the crew as a whole. The less that was known about the bandits - the more imperfect the information - the better their chance of survival. Their enemies would always hold the better cards. The only way to win was to bluff. It's for this reason Casival was uneasy about the last job. They had purchased a building near a warehouse, tunneling into it and stealing the goods. The plan was solid and the profit healthy, but it was the target that worried him still, even now after it was complete. After all, unlike some enterprises, the East Empire Company was a machine that counted every coin to its last, and weighed every commodity to the gram. Their employees were punctual, their accountants circumspect, and their ledgers pristine. They would identify precisely what goods were stolen, and investigate thoroughly the time and manner of the theft. Thus it weighed heavy on his mind when the forger who purchased the building next to the warehouse had not responded to his last letter. Casival wrote the missive posing as a concerned relative, not wishing to betray any secrets lest the forger had been compromised. Another concern was news that the Company had enlisted the help of the local guard captains, in an effort to pool their information. With the added protection, caravans had been harder to sack. And with a more watchful eye on merchants, goods had been much harder to smuggle. As it turned out, it was possible to rob from the East Empire Company, but not without revealing some of their cards. "Did you know that Pale-Eyes can sing?" Ehlhiel said, much to everyone's surprise. "Is that a joke?" asked Zaharia, somewhat surprised. "I'm being serious, he's actually better than most bards," Ehlhiel replied, for once completely sincere, "Trust me, it shocked me more than anything. I wasn't even aware Argonians could even make that kind of noise, let alone do it on key." Casival laughed at the thought of the shy Argonian melodically strumming his lute. Even after he thought he'd learned everything there was to know about the others, they were always surprising him in strange and interesting ways. Perhaps the same could be said about their current predicament. So long as they were free, it meant whatever information their pursuers had was still imperfect. The bandits had revealed much of their cards already, but hopefully, they had yet to give away their entire hand.

埃德华把他在艾斯维尔学会的游戏教给了安东尼奥斯，卡西瓦、埃利赫和泽哈瑞亚也先后坐到桌前加入。规则是把一块沾着你能想到的所有酒渍的布放在一根木头上，然后用骨片和瓦片从斑驳的酒渍中滑到布的另一边。尽管有些规则在埃德华当初翻译时就翻译丢了，但他已知的内容足够让游戏玩起来了。更妙的是，如果他按自己的喜好曲解了某些规则，他的对手们也会一概不知。 “游戏都分为两种”埃德华说着，把瓦片放到布上，“一种是信息完整的游戏，一种是不完整的。比如象棋，就是信息完整的游戏，双方都清楚对方的棋子和位置。而相反，卡牌游戏就是不完整的那种，我们每个人手里都握着一定点数的牌，必须绞尽脑汁去想自己的牌怎么打，并猜别人有没有更好的牌。” “那你更喜欢哪种？”卡西瓦问道。 “我偏好那种知己知彼的。”埃德华答道：“但我对信息不完整的游戏技巧更有心得。毕竟，我们周围的世界便是如此。” “我都没意识到世界是个游戏。”埃利赫说：“因为如果真是那样，那我得找个方法作弊了。” “别谦虚。”又赢了一把的埃德华说道，“我觉得你玩的不赖。但我们的同桌朋友安东尼奥斯就不行了。” “我输是因为你分散我注意力。”安东尼奥斯吼道，“就是你鼻孔进出气体的动作。” “你是指呼吸？”埃德华问道， “没错。” 作为一个善于洞察他人的人，卡西瓦明白埃德华的话中意思。比如说埃德华吧，将他的智慧和魅力运用如剑，以轻佻的风度来放松对手的警惕。而埃利赫则是用他的幽默当做护体盔甲，可以弹开任何情绪和动机。泽瑞哈亚，尽管坦率，但又真诚而充满激情，使她容易成为脾气的牺牲品。就算是安东尼奥斯，虽然经常醉醺醺的，但依然是个技艺高超的野法师，而且卡西瓦经常想，安东尼奥斯整日酗酒是不是只是为了让别人原谅他那最糟糕的冲动。 这套原则也适用于整个团体。强盗团伙的知名度越低——也就是信息越不完整，存活的概率也就越大。他们的敌人总是手握更好的牌，所以唯一可能胜出的办法就是虚张声势。 正因如此，卡西瓦对上一票深感忧虑。他们在仓库附近买了栋房子，在地下挖洞进去偷走了货物。计划万无一失且收获颇丰，但所选的目标却让他在得手后也担忧至今。毕竟，与某些企业不同，东帝国公司是一台数钱精确到枚，称货精确到克的机器。他们员工守时，会计谨慎，账本准确。他们会准确发现失窃的货物，并彻查失窃时间和方式。 所以，卡西瓦对之前买下那栋仓库旁房子的伪造者迟迟没有回信感到担心。为了不暴露伪造者身份，卡西瓦是以一个伪造者亲戚的身份写的信。他还注意到，东帝国公司已经向当地的卫兵队长求援，寻求更多关于他们的信息。随着车队保护的加强，抢劫更加困难，而商人中监视的增多，也使走私难度增加。最终，一切表明，虽然劫掠东帝国公司是有可能的，但不能不因此暴露团伙手里的一些牌。 “你们知道苍白之眼会唱歌吗？”埃利赫说道，让所有人都吃了一惊。 “你是在开玩笑吗？”泽瑞哈亚有些惊讶地问道 “我认真的。他其实比多数吟游诗人都唱的好。”埃利赫一脸认真地答道：“相信我，这比任何东西都更让我震惊，我从来没想到阿尔贡能发出那种声音，更不用说玩乐器了。” 一想到那个内向的阿尔贡会按旋律弹起鲁特琴，卡西瓦就忍不住笑了。即是在他自以为了解了其他人的一切后，他们还是能以奇特有趣的方式给他惊喜。或许当前的困境也是如此，只要他们依旧自由，就意味着敌人所追寻的信息依然是不完整的。 强盗们已经暴露了手中太多的牌，只能希望，他们还没有打算丢掉整副牌。

Yakhtu once told me I'd wager off my own mother if the odds were right. So it's probably no surprise to her that I lost her armor on a bet. 

What I would explain to the blacksmith, after she was done yelling at me, was that my plan was foolproof. 

I had in my coin purse a total of three hundred and twenty septims. My strategy was to wager ten pieces at a time. If I lost, my next bet would be ten pieces, to cover the last wager. If I lost again, I would wager twenty, and once again attempt to break even. If I lost a fourth time, I would wager forty, and so on. 

So unless I lost six straight times, I'd always break even in the end. Well, ten straight losses later, I not only have no gold, but no armor and bed to sleep on. I must have slept with Zenithar's mother or something, not sure why he hates me so.

Anyways, I sold the armor to some High Elf collector at the Bee and Barb. I should probably just kill her. I would kill the bandits running the pits, but then where would I get my fix.</font>

<font face="$HandwrittenFont" size="18">
亚克图曾经说过，如果机会充裕，我会连亲妈都输进去。所以她对我因为赌博输掉她的盔甲可能完全不会意外。

等她对我大吼大叫之后，我会跟铁匠解释说，我的计划绝对万无一失。

我的钱袋里一共有三百二十金币。我的策略是一次下十金币的注。如果输了，那下次还是下十金币，好弥补上一注。如果我又输了，那我就再赌二十，再次尝试收支平衡。如果输了四次，就赌四十，以此类推。

除非我连着输六场，否则最后总会平衡。可我连着输了十场，不但没了金币，连盔甲和住处都输进去了。我一定是上了泽尼萨尔他妈，不然他怎么这么恨我。

总之，我把盔甲卖给了蜂与钩的一个高精灵收藏家。也许我该杀了她。或者杀了经营斗兽赌博的强盗，但我又该上哪里领赏呢？</font>

original: M'Sharra's Diary
traduit: 麦'莎拉的日记

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
M'Sharra has a secret. 

Not a bad secret, like the Battle-Born's secret affair. Not a boring secret, like the shopkeeper who hates his sister. M'Sharra's secret is too good to be believed.

M'Sharra did not always spend her days like this, a cat who pretends to be a dog. No, M'Sharra used to be a bandit warrior, a member of the Crimson Dirks - famous rogues wanted by the East Empire Company, the Clan Mothers of Elsweyr, and lawbringers from here to the Summerset Isles. If the guards only knew, they would come kill her. That is why M'Sharra can never tell.

But her time is short. She longs for company. The other day she took to begging outside the city, and saw her litter-mate, Zaharia, walk through the gates. M'Sharra called her by name, but the Redguard ignored her. M'Sharra is sure she heard her, and it made her sad to know this.

M'Sharra does not want to die a rug. Perhaps she will do something mischievous, and get the Whiterun guards to attack. Then she will be a warrior once more.</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
麦'莎拉有个秘密。

不是坏秘密，不像战狂家的那种。也不是什么无聊的，不像店主讨厌他妹妹那种。麦'莎拉的秘密好得不得了。

麦'莎拉不是总这样活着的，像个装成狗的猫。对，麦'莎拉曾经是个强盗战士，是猩红长匕的一员，我们是被东帝国公司、被艾斯维尔的氏母们，还有从这里到夏暮岛的执法者们通缉的江洋大盗。如果卫兵知道真相，他们会来杀了她。这就是为什么麦'莎拉永远不说的原因。

但她已经没多少时间了。她渴望有人陪伴。有天她出城外乞讨，看到她曾经的同窝崽崽泽哈瑞亚走进城门了。麦'莎拉喊了她的名字，但那个红卫人不理她。麦'莎拉确定她听见了，正因如此她才很难过。

麦'莎拉不想死在垫子上。也许她该做点恶作剧，让白漫的卫兵来攻击。这样她就又能变成一名战士啦。</font>

original: M'Sharra's Confession
traduit: 麦'莎拉的供状

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
M'Sharra enjoyed her fight with the guard. Plus, her new home is better than the last. It is a very tiny cage, but she does not beg for food. It is given.

Still, M'Sharra longs to see the night sky. When she was a kitten, the elders warned her that if she stared too long at the moons, they would grow shy, and M'Sharra would never see them again. This made her sad, and so M'Sharra vowed to stop looking at the sky, and kept her head down toward the dirt where the beggars belonged.

One day, she tried to steal the silver out of the pockets of a Nord named Tyra. When she heard Khajiit's story, she took pity on the kitten, and told her that the moons were not the timid creatures she had believed. She said that as long as Khajiit held her head up high, they would shine brighter than any star.

From that day on she spent her life in service to the Crimson Dirks. And when she was ready, her new litter-mates forged her an armor made of silver, and in its heart, the piece Tyra had in her pocket so many moons ago.

M'Sharra hid the armor in a hut, northwest of Rorikstead. At times, M'Sharra has longed to retrieve it, and wear it proudly. 

But she must be careful not to let sentiment cloud her judgment. M'Sharra suspects she is being followed. So she will leave the armor for another. Besides, it is not the silver in the armor or the moonlight in the sky that M'Sharra treasures, but the friends she has lost. Perhaps in death, she will see them again.</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
麦'莎拉很享受与卫兵的战斗。而且，新家比以前好多了。笼子很小，但她不会乞求食物。那是给定的。

尽管如此，麦'莎拉还是渴望看到夜空。当她还是只小猫崽，长老们就警告她，如果她盯着月亮看太久，它们是会害羞的，那样麦'莎拉就再也见不到它们了。这让她很伤心，所以麦'莎拉发誓不再仰望天空了，要把头低向属于乞丐们的泥土上。

有一天，她打算从一个叫提拉的诺德人口袋里偷银子。当她听了卡吉特的故事，她很同情小猫咪，告诉她月亮不是她想的那样胆小。她说，只要卡吉特昂起头，月亮会比任何星星都明亮。

从那天起，她一直都为猩红长匕效劳。等她准备好时，她的新同窝崽们帮她造了一套银护甲，中心位置，用的就是许多个月前提拉口袋里那块银子。

麦'莎拉把护甲藏在了洛利克镇西北的一间小屋里。有时候，麦'莎拉也想回去找回来，自豪地穿在身上。

但她必须要小心，不能让情绪影响了自己的判断。麦'莎拉怀疑她被跟踪了。所以她会把盔甲留给别人。还有，麦'莎拉不是可惜护甲上的银子，也不是天上的月光，而是她失去的朋友。也许她死后还能见他们吧。</font>

[pagebreak]

The Crimson Dirks Book Two by Gathers-the-Coin

[pagebreak]

n the year following its inception, the Crimson Dirks had more than tripled in size, and now numbered fifteen. Tyra Blood-Fire had found her blacksmith in the Imperial City, an Orc named Yakhtu. She had recruited cunning battlemages in the Breton twins, Erwan and Edward. In Elsweyr she met M'Sharra, a street thief who had grown into a capable blade. There were the Wood Elf archers, Fathrys and Ehlhiel - one a hopeless romantic, the other cynical beyond his years. There was the Argonian Pale-Eyes, a loyal and true soul, and the Redguard Zaharia, a born leader of men. And lastly, she found her muscle in the Orc warrior Urgnok, and in the Nords Skjol and Bjormund, their bodies as unbreakable as the ice of their ancestors. Altogether it had the makings of a full-fledged organization, rivaling that of any major guild. They had members pulling off jobs from Bruma to Dune, raiding warehouses and pillaging farms. With every crate added to their coffers, Tyra hoped their influence could spider across the breadth of Tamriel, earning both fear and respect amongst those who plied their trade in the shadows. As bandits, however, they would rely first and foremost on the sacking of caravans. They would stalk the highways and thoroughfares for carriages full of goods, and quickly relieve them of their belongings. For this task the Khajiit, M'Sharra, found herself best suited. Her eyes were keen at identifying a heavy wagon, from the spin of its wheels to the tracks carving through the dirt. She could spot a weary guard by the slump of his shoulders or the pace of his gait. Her eyes saw clearly even in the dead of night, while others were slaves to the light of their torches. And what she lacked in strength, the other bandits were willing to provide. On this night, however, their victims put up little fight, their numbers comprised of monks and priests who were all too ready to unite with their makers. The wagon they plundered was destined for a temple, and its crates full of treasures that offered more tribute than gold. "Do you think Tyra would like this?" asked M'Sharra, popping her head out from behind the wagon, an Amulet of Talos dangling from her ear. "A bandit has no need for gods or prayer," grumbled Urgnok, wiping the blood from his battleaxe, "it's a terrible gift." "Nonsense," countered Bjormund, unloading a crate, "all Nords love Talos, almost as much as they love mead!" "Of course you would say that, frost licker," snarled Urgnok, "but by Malacath, Tyra is not like the rest of you idiots. She has taste." If Tyra were like any other Nord, Urgnok would have never pledged her his axe. In his mind, the Nords were pale-faced, poetry loving giants who ate with their fingers and drank from a horn. Tyra, however, did not think or feel or smell like the other Nords did, and more importantly, did not fight like them. She preferred the acrid bite of a sujamma bottle to a snowback's honeyed drink, and despised poetry in all its forms. He surmised she might've been from Morrowind, but the Orc was not the type to pry into another's business. "Oh?" said M'Sharra with a mischievous grin, the amulet swaying as her ears perked up, "and what are you planning to get her, Urgnok?" "What? Why would I get her anything?" the Orc replied coldly, "you'll all be dead in a year anyway." M'Sharra blanched at the words, unsure if the Orc was making a joke or speaking prophecy. While hardly a mage, Urgnok was known to dabble in dark magic, wearing tribal scars and marks on his body, and totems of bone around his neck. Unlike with the blacksmith Yakhtu, his anger seemed to stem not from the hardened nature of his blood, but something deeper and personal, and it colored every conversation they had. The others stewed in silence at his remarks until the young Bosmer, Fathrys, broke the ice. "Speaking of which, did you want anything for the holidays, Zaharia?" he mewled, a rose of blush affecting his soft brown skin. The Redguard, in return, paid him little heed as she examined the wagon's horses. "If you want to get me a Saturalia gift," said Zaharia, pointing at the arrows lodged in the wagon's side, "work on your aim. I'll feel better about having you at my back when you can kill more than planks of wood." "That is all well and good," interrupted M'Sharra, "but there is a far more important matter than life and death, for this Khajiit still does not have a suitable present." "If it's from the heart," Fathrys said, eyes fixated on the Redguard, "the amulet will be good enough." Two weeks later on a cold Saturalia night, Tyra Blood-Fire awoke to the sound of a crackling fire. A note was placed on her private safe, which she opened to find an amulet wrapped in cloth. The Khajiit had snuck into her room earlier and left the gift and the fire behind, as proof of both her generosity and skill. Tyra was not religious by nature, but as she stood in that warm, reddish glow, something about the Amulet of Talos resonated with her. Perhaps it was the letter she received from Peladius that morning, about an encounter with the Thalmor in Dune. In that instance, a thought crept into her mind and soon blossomed into an idea. The following day she beckoned the blacksmith to her chambers, the idea having matured into a plan. "I want you to forge me more of these amulets," Tyra said, placing the axe-shaped necklace on the table before her. The blacksmith picked up the artifact and studied its make, thumbing across the intricate patterns grooved into the piece. Unlike other amulets, it was simple yet ornate, its blades casting a neutral tone that neither reflected nor absorbed the surrounding candlelight. "This is made with dragonbone and scales," Yakhtu replied, "hard to come by these days, but a replica should be simple enough. I guess my only question is, why? Seems odd for bandits to turn to the Divines for help." "Last week, there was a trade caravan traveling on the Silver Road, torched by Thalmor Justiciars," Tyra said, "Apparently they killed the merchant on suspicion of Talos worship. And it's not just here. I've gotten word from Peladius that the Thalmor are making an effort to eliminate anyone and everyone in possession of these amulets, whether it be men in the streets or wagons on the road." "Wagons," replied Yakhtu, "like the ones we sack." "Exactly. The amulets aren't armor or jewelry or tribute," said Tyra, "they're a motive. We place one on every caravan we sack, and torch the wagons when we're done looting them. The guards blame the Thalmor, and we keep the spoils." Yakhtu nodded and took her leave, mind set on forging the amulets. Tyra knew well enough that the smith didn't need the artifact with her, having already committed it to memory. The blacksmith's genius was different from the others - quiet, removed, and matched only by her insatiable work ethic. The amulets would be done by daybreak, and there was no need for this one to be included. Tyra returned the amulet to the safe, when she noticed another item nestled amongst the piles of gold and gems. It was the tooth of an Orc chief, one typically earned by besting its owner in single combat. Tyra herself knew of one such Orc, a son who had been forced to kill his father against his will. Heartbroken, the son wore this tooth as a keepsake around his neck, fearing the day he would have to slay his future children. Until one day the son met a Nord bandit, who became Blood-Kin of the tribe and challenged him to a duel. The bandit bested the Orc in single combat, and recognizing the pain that haunted him, freed him from his duties as chief. She asked not for his tooth, but his blade when the time came. Yet it wasn't until after the Nord formed the Crimson Dirks that she returned to that Orc, and asked him to make good on his oath. Tyra smiled as she recalled the memory. She didn't know Urgnok had pulled the tooth, but it didn't surprise her in the least.

[pagebreak]

创建后的几年里，”猩红长匕”的规模扩大了三倍以上，现在足足有十五人。 “血火”提拉在帝都找到了她要的铁匠，一个叫亚克图的兽人。她还招募了一对狡猾的布莱顿双胞胎战斗法师，埃文和埃德华。在艾斯维尔她招募了麦'莎拉，一位会舞刀弄剑的街头盗贼。还有两位木精弓箭手，法斯瑞和埃利赫，一个多情到无可救药，一个愤世嫉俗到不正常。还有苍白之眼，一位忠实可靠的阿尔贡。以及红卫人泽哈瑞亚，天生具备领袖气质。最后，她找到了她要的打手，一位是兽人战士乌格诺克，另外两位是诺德人斯科卓与布乔蒙德，都如他们祖先那个年代的上古寒冰一般坚不可摧。 这些人都招齐后，组织变得羽翼丰满了，能与任何同行竞争。他们的业务北至布鲁玛，南至到沙丘城，目标从仓库到农场无所不抢。提拉希望随着掠来的物资越来越多，他们的名声能传遍泰姆瑞尔，让黑道同行又敬又怕。 不过，作为强盗，他们的主要收入还是来自抢劫商队。他们会把在交通要道上拦截那些装满货物的车队，然后快速抢光。卡吉特麦'莎拉最胜任这项工作，她眼神锐利，能根据马车转弯时留下的车辙判断出哪些是辎重货车，还能根据低垂的肩膀以及缓慢的步伐发现疲惫的车队护卫。甚至在最黑的夜中，她依然视力清晰，而其他人只能依赖火把。 至于她缺乏的蛮力，其他强盗愿意提供支援。 不过这一晚，他们的目标进行了些许反抗，多是些视死如归的僧侣和祭司。他们抢到的货车是运往神庙的，货箱中装的更多是贡品而不是钱。 “你们觉得提拉会喜欢这个么？”麦'莎拉从货车后面钻出头来，耳朵上挂着一个荡来荡去的塔洛斯护符。 “强盗才不需要什么神或者祈祷。”乌格诺克一边抱怨，一边擦拭着巨斧上的血迹，”这会是个糟糕透顶的礼物。” “胡扯。”卸箱子的斯科卓反驳道：”所有诺德人都爱塔洛斯，就像爱蜜酒一样！” “你肯定会这么说，爱舔雪的家伙。”乌格诺克咆哮道：“但是玛拉凯斯在上，提拉和你们这群白痴不一样，她是个有品味的人。” 提拉但凡其他诺德人有一点相似之处，乌格诺克都不会为她效忠。在他印象里，诺德人是一群脸色苍白、喜爱诗歌、用手抓饭、用角喝酒的大块头。但是，提拉在各方面看起来都与其他诺德人不一样。最重要的是，她的战斗方式与他们不一样。比起雪佬的蜜酒，她更偏爱辛辣的苏贾玛，还鄙夷任何形式的诗歌。他推测提拉可能来自晨风， 但兽人是不喜欢到处打听别人私事的。 “哦？”麦'莎拉不怀好意地咧嘴一笑，竖起了摇晃着护符的耳朵，“那你想给她什么，乌格诺克？” “我？我为什么要给她东西？”兽人冷酷地回答道：“反正你们都活不过一年。” 麦'莎拉掂量着乌格诺克的话，不确定他到底是在开玩笑还是做预言。尽管乌格诺克算不上什么法师，但大家确实知道他有涉猎黑魔法，身体上纹有部落标志，还戴着一条骨制图腾项链。与亚克图不同，他易怒的性格似乎不是天性使然，而是来自某种更深，更私密的东西，这种情绪影响着他们每一次的谈话。乌格诺克的言论让所有人笼罩在一股不详的沉默中，直到年轻的波斯莫法斯赫打破了沉默。 “说到这，泽哈瑞亚，你节日里想要什么吗？”法斯瑞喊着，柔软的棕色脸颊涨红了。正在检查货车马匹的红卫人瞥了他一眼。 “如果你真想给我份萨图拉利亚节礼物的话”红卫指着插在马车上的箭说道：“那就给我射准点。如果你在我身后支援时能射中木板以外的东西，我就心满意足了。” “好好好。”麦'莎拉打断了他俩。“但是现在有一件远比生死都重要的事情。那就是这位卡吉特还没有找到一份合适的礼物。” “只要是真心的，”法斯赫一边说着，一边注视着泽哈瑞亚。“护符也就足够了。” 两周后，在寒冷的萨图拉利亚节之夜，“血火”提拉被一阵火焰的噼啪声吵醒。一张纸条放在她的私人保险柜上，打开保险柜，里面是一枚用布包着的护符。那位卡吉特早些时候潜入了她的房间，留下了护符和火焰噼啪声，既表现了自己的慷慨，又证明了自己的能力。 提拉未曾信教，但是那时，站在那温暖的红色火光前，她忽的与这枚塔洛斯护符产生了某种共鸣。或许是与那天早晨她收到的一封佩拉迪乌斯寄来的信有关，信中讲述了佩拉迪乌斯与梭默在沙丘城的一次遭遇。在那一瞬，一个想法突然浮现在她脑中，当几天后她召铁匠到她房间时，这个想法已经发展为一个成熟的计划。 “我想让你制造更多这种护符。”提拉说着，把那个斧形项链放到亚克图面前。 铁匠拿起护符并研究其构造，手指抚过刻在护符不同部位表面错综的纹饰，护符简单而不失华丽，斧刃面表现出一种中性的特质，既不吸收也不反射周围的烛光。 “这是由龙骨和龙鳞制成的，”亚克图说道：“现在已经很难获得了，但用替代品仿制应该不难。我唯一的问题是，为什么？强盗会向圣灵求助可真新鲜了。” “上周在银色大道上，一个商队遭到了梭默审判者的烧毁。”提拉说：“显然，梭默杀掉了有崇拜塔洛斯嫌疑的商人。而且不止这一处。我收到佩拉迪乌斯的消息说，梭默正在努力消灭任何持有这种护符的人，无论是城市居民还是车队成员。” “车队啊，”亚克图回答道：”就像我们打劫的那个。” “没错。这些护符不是装备、珠宝或贡品。”提拉说：“它们是动机。我们每抢劫一个车队就放上去一个。拿完东西后就烧掉马车。卫兵会怪罪到梭默头上，我们则逍遥法外。” 亚克图点头离开了，投身于铸造护符的工作里。提拉知道铁匠并不需要随身带上实物，她对护符早已了然于心。这位铁匠的天赋与他人迥异，她安静，孤僻，有无穷无尽贪婪的创作欲望。黎明时，那批护符已经完工了，还不用算上这一枚原物。 提拉把那枚放回保险箱里时，注意到在成堆金币和宝石间的一个隐藏角落里，有一枚兽人酋长的牙齿。这种牙只有在与其主人一对一的决斗中胜出才能获得。 提拉认识这样的一位兽人，他是位被强迫违背自己意愿弑父的儿子。心碎之余，他把这颗牙戴在项上作为护身符，生怕有朝一日要亲手杀掉自己的后代。直到这位儿子遇上了一个诺德强盗，这个强盗是部落血亲，向他发起了决斗。 这个强盗在决斗中击败了他，并意识到了困扰他的痛苦，把他从酋长的责任中解脱出来。强盗没有要他的牙齿，而是要求他在时机到来时为她作战。但直到这个诺德强盗建立猩红长匕后，她才又找到这位兽人，要求他履行誓言。 回忆起这段往事时，提拉忍不住笑了。她不知道乌格诺克原来已经把那颗牙拔了，但对此她也不会觉得有多惊讶。

original:
<font face="$HandwrittenFont" size="20">
Tyra tell Skjol to wait, so he wait. But then he meet nice man from village, who show him magic ice. He call it stalhrim.

Skjol like stalhrim. He like way it look. He like way it sound. H is silent, just like Skjol, because Skjol have no tongue. 

But Skjol's axe is loud. It make good crunch noise in ice.

But stalhrim make different noise. Most ice go "REEEEE!" but magic ice go "UNFH!"

Skjol should be bard. 

Nice man say there island north of Cassookar...Cassookarst...he say there island all way north with much magic ice. The kind Skjol can wear.

Skjol think man very nice, he sorry he have to crush him.</font>

<font face="$HandwrittenFont" size="20">
提拉跟斯科卓说等着，斯科卓就等着。但他遇到了村里的好人，向他展示了神奇的魔冰。

斯科卓喜欢魔冰。喜欢它的样子，它的声音。它很沉默，就像斯科卓一样，因为斯科卓没有舌头。

但斯科卓的斧子很吵闹。在冰上咔咔嚓嚓地很好听。

但是魔冰的声音很不同。大多数冰块只能发出“咔咔”的声音，魔冰却是“嗡嗡”的。

那个好人说卡搜卡……卡搜卡斯塔格北面的那个岛上，有很多很多的神奇魔冰。斯卡尔可以穿的那种。

斯科卓觉得这人真的很好，要碾碎他真是很抱歉。</font>

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
<font size='18'>I should've made sure that body sunk to the bottom of the river, but in my old age I've gotten sloppy.

I guess I should come clean. My real name is Peladius. I'm a bandit. At least, I used to be, until our group was betrayed by one of our own. I started this whole charade because I wanted to know who.

But to be honest, it doesn't matter anymore. There was never any honor among thieves. I lost what little claim I had to it, the day I joined Tyra's crew. 

Then again, maybe I can still have an honorable death.

Meet me at Dragon Bridge. We can settle this there.
</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
<font size='18'>我应该把那具尸体沉到河里才对，可年纪大了，人也粗心了。

我想我应该坦白。我真名叫做佩拉迪乌斯，是个强盗。至少曾经是，直到我们的团伙出了叛徒。我这么做就是因为我想知道到底是谁叛变了。

但那说实话，已经不重要了。贼无光荣可言。从入伙提拉那天起，我就失去了最后一点主张它的资格。

话说回来，也许我还是可以光荣地死去。

到龙桥等我。我们到那里决个胜负吧。
</font>

original: Guard's Note on Aldepius
traduit: 卫兵关于阿尔德庇乌斯的笔记

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
I am beginning to suspect Aldepius is not who he claims to be.

He seemed rather old for a new recruit, but it wasn't until he started asking about our bandit informant that I began to suspect something was amiss. Still, I would've forgiven this as natural curiosity had he not asked to meet him.

So I checked with the list of the garrison, and no one by the name Aldepius is on it. I don't know who he is, but he's not a member of the guard. He's stationed at Dragon Bridge at the moment, when my shift is over I'm going to confront him about it.
</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
我开始怀疑阿尔德庇乌斯的身份了。

身为新兵，他看上去年纪过大了，但直到他开始询问有关我们的强盗线人的信息，我才开始怀疑有什么不对。不过，如果不是他主动提出要见面，我还是会原谅他这种天生的好奇心。

我检查了驻军名单，上面没有叫阿尔德庇乌斯的人。我不知道他的真实身份，但他肯定不是卫兵。现在他驻守在龙桥，等我换班，我就去找他对质。
</font>

original:
<font face="$HandwrittenFont">
At Arcwind Point, the bones of the dead rattle in their stone cages. But the old magic is strong in those mountains, and with the help of the cat who is a rat - a priest of Namira no less - the crow will set them free.

With his help, an army of bones will dance to her caw, be they warriors, shadows, or beasts. Yet the cauldron shows the bones of two others - dragons in mortal flesh, who seek to challenge her inside towers of frost and stone. 

It will be up to the crow to pick both their bones clean.</font>

<font face="$HandwrittenFont">
在弧风高点，亡者之骨在石棺里嘎吱作响。但是，古老的魔法在那片山脉中仍然强大，在那只耗子猫，一个娜米拉祭司的帮助下，乌鸦会把它们重新放出来的。

original: Bjormund's Diary
traduit: 布乔蒙德的日记

original:
<font face="$HandwrittenFont">
I remember the first time M'Sharra showed me the tunnel, the one we had been burrowing for months. At first, I didn't understand it. We were already making good coin sacking the carriages. What was the point of digging holes underground like vermin? It didn't help that the tunnel smelled like a troll's armpit.

We reached the warehouse, and walked by crates stacked upon crates like mountains of wood. M'Sharra led me to the back, where a dozen Legionnaires were unloading cargo too big for any box. And Shor's Breath, I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw it! It was a skull the size of a carriage, with fangs that touched the floor! 

For someone who winces at the sight of cliff racers, the idea of this monstrosity soaring through the sky made my heart tremble. And yet, for the first time, I felt alive.

For what better way to live than to fight a dragon! What better way to die! Now that would be a story even Tsun would lend an ear to!

"You think the bones are special, you should see what this one found yesterday," M'Sharra said to me. Her grin was as wide as the Halls of Jorrvaskr as she beckoned me further into the warehouse. Inside a crate, set apart from the others, was a cuirass of Dragonbone Mail! M'Sharra bade me to put it on, and I couldn't help but notice it was a perfect fit.

In that moment, I thought of my Da. People called him a pirate, a murderer and a thief. But he told me the Wind-Striders descended from the Dragonguard, ancient warriors who fashioned armor from the bones of the dragons they slew. 

Still, my pride as a Nord wouldn't allow it. How could I face Tsun wearing the armor of another's triumph? I could have the Orc forge gauntlets and boots from the skull, but the cuirass - that which held one's heart, must be earned in battle. 

My mind drifted then to stories I heard as a youngling, of my great ancestor who strode through fire like it was the wind, wearing an ancient cuirass made of dragonbone. It was then that I knew my destiny. In his honor I would claim it, and fight until the day I reached Sovngarde. 

It's that same spirit that resides in me now. The others may be fine living in hiding, but a Nord is at war so long as he holds breath.
traduit:
<font face="$HandwrittenFont">
我还记得麦’莎拉第一次带我去看隧道的情景，那是我们挖掘了几个月的成果。起初我还不明白。我们洗劫马车赚了不少，何必像个害虫一样在地下挖洞？隧道里闻起来就像巨魔的咯吱窝，糟糕至极。

我们抵达了仓库，看见堆积如山的木箱。麦’莎拉把我带到后面，那里有十几个军团兵正在卸货，货物太大了，任何箱子都装不下。舒尔之息啊，我不敢相信自己的眼睛！那是个马车大小的头骨，獠牙能够戳到地板！

对于看到峭壁行者都会颤抖的人来说，这怪物翱翔于天空的样子让我内心颤抖。然而，我第一次感受到了自己活着。

还有什么比与龙战斗更好的生活呢！还有比这更光荣的死法吗？这样的传奇，就算是苏恩也会侧耳倾听！

“如果你觉得这骨头很特别，你应该看看昨天发现的这个，” 麦’莎拉对我说。她示意我往仓库里面走时，笑得如同月瓦斯卡大厅一般灿烂。在一个独立放置的箱子里，有一副龙骨链甲！麦’莎拉让我穿上，我不由自主地注意到它的确十分合身。

在那一刻，我想到了我爸。人们管他叫海盗、杀人犯、盗贼。但他告诉我，风行者氏族是龙卫后人，是屠龙取骨，制成盔甲披挂在身上的古代勇士。

然而身为诺德人的骄傲，不允许自己这样做。我怎么能穿着象征他人胜利的铠甲去见苏恩？我应该让兽人用那副头骨锻造腕甲和靴子，但盔甲，那是能拴住一个人心脏的东西，必须在战斗中获得。

我的脑海里浮现出小时候听过的故事，我的祖先穿着古老的龙骨战甲，像风一般穿过烈火。就在那时，我知道了自己的命运。以我先祖的名义，我要夺取它，穿上战斗到我抵达松加德的那一天。

这种精神现在也还在我体内澎湃。其他人躲起来也许是个好选择，但诺德人，只要还活着，就是要战斗。

Referred to by locals as the "Dragon of Dawnstar," Bjormund is the son of a former pirate who frequented the northern port. 布乔蒙德人称“晨星之龙”，他的父亲是一个经常劫掠北部港口的海盗。在换了几次强盗团伙后，他最后向南前往希罗帝尔，在那边加入了猩红长匕。他这个绰号来源自一个传说，说布乔蒙德曾经杀死过一头龙，并把龙骨做成了盔甲，但这个故事似乎是杜撰的，因为时间点位于龙族回归之前。

对策说明：
据报，布乔蒙德从事雇佣兵工作以保持流动性。除此之外，人们对他的行踪知之甚少。</font>

he tavern fell into silence. Casival squinted at the young Bosmer, trying to get a read on his mood. Just hours earlier the lad had embarked on the biggest quest of his life, the kind of endeavor that turns squires into warriors, boys into men. "Well, what did she say?" he asked the young bandit. "She said she would only wed me," Fathrys said, "if I brought her the scale of a dragon." The tavern burst into laughter, patrons smacking their tankards against the wood. "What?" Fathrys replied, clearly confused, "What's so funny?" "I'm sorry lad," said Casival, "but I think that's her way of saying 'No.'" Fathrys was crestfallen. It had taken nearly all of his courage to confess his love to Zaharia. What meager defenses remained in his youthful frame, Casival could not guess, but they stood little chance against this latest assault. In fact, with each passing second Fathrys' shoulders slumped further and further into his chest, until he was more Guar than man. Taking pity, Casival decided to massage the boy's ego with a tale of his first rejection, when a familiar voice croaked at the pair from across the room. "A dragon scale, you say?" Not a soul had realized Antonius was in the tavern, mostly because the bandit mage was a permanent fixture. From dusk to dawn he teetered upon his wobbly chair, drinking all manner of spirits by his lonesome. Over time he began to blend into the scenery, like an odor that only strangers could smell. "By the Nine, do you know where I can find one?" Fathrys beamed with shoulders out, his once gloomy face resurrected with life. "I'm a wizard, am I not?" Antonius said, before letting out a dignified belch. "A bandit wizard," Casival interjected, "and with all due respect to you and your profession, I don't think you're helping." "Nonsense, Casival," scolded the mage, nearly tripping over his own feet as he sat at the table, "The boy needs a dragon scale, and I aim to help him find one." "But the dragons have been extinct for centuries upon centuries," Casival said. "You really are a bad student," scoffed Antonius, jabbing his finger into the Dunmer's forehead, "this is why Tyra favors Edward over you. At least he pays attention." "Forgive me, mage." "Only the Divines can forgive you, my son. Drink this bottle, and it'll take you to them." "What about the dragon scale?" Fathrys whined, growing impatient. "Oh right, that. Well, it just so happens, there's an old Nord legend about a warrior named Ulfnir Bone-Skin," Antonius explained, flecks of spit flying out of his mouth, "who slew the serpent wyrm Vithrelnaak and fashioned a powerful armor from his scales. When he died, instead of giving his armor away to his ungrateful pupils, he did what any self-respecting warrior would do, and buried himself with it." "Well, that's too bad," said Casival, hoping to derail this runaway carriage, "surely it would've been emptied out by grave robbers by now." "You would think," Antonius screamed, raising his voice for no reason, "but they say Ulfnir's corpse haunts the barrow near Yorgrim's Overlook, and kills anyone who dares try and take his armor." "I see! So it's a challenge!" Fathrys exclaimed, "In order to wear Ulfnir's armor, one must first best him as a warrior!" "Either that, or he just doesn't want some random stranger wearing his clothes. How would you feel if I showed up to your home wearing your undergarments? But yes, you kill Ulfnir, you get your dragon scale. You get your dragon scale, and you get your wench." "She's not a wench. She's the most amazing woman in all of Mundus, and I'm going to marry her!" "Sure, whatever." Casival breathed a deep sigh as Fathrys' heart grew ill with hope. The only saving grace was that Windhelm was thousands of leagues away, and Fathrys was still a pup. Perhaps when he was ready for the work, a word or two with Tyra could send him further away still. Yet whatever remedy he devised would be temporary. He had seen that look too many times to deny what would come next. A fortnight later, Casival returned to the tavern. It was the same as it ever was, for the most part. The wenches tended to the patrons, and the patrons to their stress. The bards sang tales old and new, and the drunkards, not knowing the lyrics, still saw fit to join them. Antonius was perched in the corner as always, a bottle in each hand and several more on the ground. It was like any other Fredas, save for the empty seat beside him. He would break the news to Tyra in the morning. The Bosmer would not return.

酒馆笼罩在一片沉寂中。卡西瓦眯着眼看向那个波斯莫，尝试解读他的情绪。就在几小时前，这个小伙子进行了人生里最大的追求。这种追求的力量能把纨绔子弟变成战士，把男孩变成男人。 “所以，她说了啥？”卡西瓦问这位年轻的强盗。 “她说，她会嫁给我的。”法斯瑞说，“只要我给她带一片龙鳞。” 酒馆顿时爆发出一阵大笑，顾客们把酒杯在木桌上砸的震天响。 “咋了？”法斯瑞显得很困惑“有什么好笑的？” “抱歉，小伙子。”卡西瓦说，“但我想她是在用自己的方式告诉你：没门。” 法斯瑞顿时垂头丧气。他几乎用上了所有勇气才对泽哈瑞亚表白。现在他那瘦削的身板还有多少支撑？卡西瓦猜不准，但显然是抗不过这次最新打击了。事实上，随着时间一分一秒过去，法斯瑞的肩膀越来越低，塌到了胸口，让他显得更像是一只瓜尔。卡西瓦颇为可怜他，决定给他讲一个自己当初表白被拒的故事来提振精神。就在这时，一个熟悉的低沉声音从酒馆另一端传来。 “你刚才说龙鳞？” 没人留意到安东尼奥斯也在酒馆里。主要是因为这位强盗法师是个固定桩子，一天到晚都在摇摆的椅子上晃荡，自斟自饮各种烈酒。时间一长，他开始融入周围的环境，就像一种只有新人才能嗅到的气味一样。 “九圣灵在上，你知道哪里有？”法斯瑞眉开眼笑，肩膀又立了起来，阴郁的脸色又焕发了生气。 “我毕竟是个巫师，不是吗。”安东尼奥斯说着，打了个尊贵的嗝。 “是强盗巫师。”卡西瓦插话道：“而且尽管我完全尊重你和你的专业性，但我认为你帮不上什么忙。” “胡说，卡西瓦。”安东尼奥斯骂道，他移到桌前，差点一脚绊倒。“这位小伙子需要龙鳞，而我要帮他找到一片。” “但是龙已经灭绝无数世纪了。”卡西瓦说道。 “你真是不学无术。”安东尼奥斯嘲弄道，拿手指猛戳卡西瓦的额头，“这就是为何比起你，提拉更青睐埃德华。因为至少他会认真听讲。” “原谅我，法师。” “现在只有圣灵才能宽恕你，小子。干了这瓶，你就能去见他们了。” “所以龙鳞到底在哪儿？”法斯瑞抱怨道，他已经开始失去耐心了。 “哦，好吧，那个啊。事情是这样：有一则关于诺德战士“骨肤”乌夫尼尔的古代传说……”安东尼奥斯口沫横飞地解释着，“他杀了一头名为维瑟瑞诺克的龙，用其鳞片做了一副刀枪不入的盔甲。当他去世时，他没有把铠甲送给他那群不知感激的徒弟，而是如其他自尊的战士一样，让它随自己下葬了。” “啊，那可是太糟了。”卡西瓦说，他希望赶紧阻止事态发展下去，“现在肯定早就被盗墓贼拿走了。” “你可能是这么想的。”安东尼奥斯尖声喊道，突然无故提高了声音，“但有人说乌夫尼尔的尸骸依然游荡在他位于约格利姆眺台附近的坟墓里。谁敢染指他盔甲，他就杀谁。” “我懂了，所以这是个挑战！”法斯瑞大喊道：“如果要想穿上乌夫尼尔的盔甲，就必须要像个战士一样在战斗中堂堂正正地击败他！” “要么是这样，要么就是他不想让陌生人随便穿他的东西。如果我穿着你的内衣到你家去显摆，你会怎么想？但是确实，你击败乌夫尼尔，你就能得到龙鳞，得到龙鳞，自然也就得到了那个小姑娘。” “她才不是什么小姑娘，她是梦达思最好的女人，我就是要娶她！” “好好好，随你便。” 看着法斯瑞陷入病态的希望中，卡西瓦长叹一声。目前唯一的好处是，风舵城距离这里足足有上千里，而法斯瑞还是个毛头小子。可能就算他做好准备后，提拉的一两句话依然把他打发的远远的。然而，他深知，无论他计划了什么补救措施都只能暂时拖延，他已经见过太多那种神情，以至于不想承认接下来一切已经注定的事。 两周后，卡西瓦回到了酒馆。一切基本如往常一样。侍女们一门心思伺候顾客，顾客们一门心思在各自的事上。吟游诗人唱着或旧或新的歌谣，有不知词的醉汉应和着伴奏。安东尼奥斯一如既往地坐在角落里，一手一个酒瓶，还有几瓶散在脚底。 这是一个没什么特别的星期五，除了卡西瓦旁边的位置是空的。 卡西瓦要把一则重要的消息带回给提拉，那个波斯莫再也不会回来了。

Over the course of his life, a man wears many faces, and goes by many names. Son, father, fugitive, bandit. I never thought I would include "Argonian writer" among those titles, but so it goes. 

When Peladius taught me how to write, I didn't think I'd take to it the way I have. Maybe if the gods had given me a pen instead of a sword, I would've spent my life writing books instead of sacking caravans. Well, too late to whine about it now. 

As for the name, it came from a conversation I had with Pale-Eyes one night at The Grey Mare in Chorrol. I asked him why Argonian names were so literal, and his reply was, "Why aren't yours?" 

I laughed, realizing I was bested. So I asked him to give me an Argonian name, one that suited someone of my ilk. 

And so from then on, I was Gathers-the-Coin.

The funny thing about an Argonian name is, I wasn't sure if it was meant to define the person I was or the one I aspired to be. I suppose the point is moot now. I'll probably die in this tower without a septim to my name. But at least if I keep writing, people will know our story, and know that we once lived.

<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='20'>
人这一生，不知有多少面孔，多少称谓。儿子、父亲、逃犯、强盗。我从没想过会把“阿尔贡作家”列入自己的头衔里，但事实就是如此。

当佩拉迪乌斯教我如何写作时，我没想到过会像现在这样热爱。如果诸神给我的是一支笔而不是一把剑，那我可能一辈子都在写书，而不是去洗劫商队。现在抱怨也晚了。

至于这个名字，是有一天晚上我在科洛尔的灰马酒馆和苍白之眼聊天得来的。我问他为什么阿尔贡的名字这么字面化，他反问：“为什么不是你们的才字面化呢？”

我笑了，意识到自己被驳倒了。所以我请他给我取个适合我这种人的阿尔贡名字。

从那以后我就成了“四方钱来”。

关于阿尔贡名字，有趣就在于，我不能确定它是用来定义我是一个怎样的人，还是说我渴望成为什么样的人。我想这个问题已经没什么意义了。我可能会死在这座塔里，名字上又没有一个塞普汀。但至少如果我继续写下去，人们会知道我们的故事，知道我们曾经来过。

yra had forgotten which heist was her favorite. Perhaps it was the time they stole a wagon's worth of silks from the desert palaces of Dune. Maybe it was when they burrowed a tunnel into the warehouse of the East Empire Company, siphoning crate after crate while the wardens stood mindlessly at the door. Or it could be she preferred the more violent raids, like the sacking of the Argonian supply caravans, or the attacks on cargo ships leaving the Imperial City waterfront. Or perhaps if she looked back far enough, her fondest memories would find her in the streets of Balmora, robbing travelers at knifepoint. For some reason it was this version of her, this long forgotten stranger, that seemed the most vivid now. Gone was the refined, thoughtful countenance of a leader, and in its place a hungry, ash-hewn child who had far more courage than sense. And if she closed her eyes, she could still feel the smooth, polished surface of the ruby the noble dropped in her palm, and how it felt like nothing of this world. Yet it was not the price or the feel, but the color of the ruby that she remembered most; the blades of crimson burned into the glass, like the fire of the Red Mountain. "Why do you think it is," she asked Aesrael, "that our thoughts turn to the past when are lives are so close to death?" "I suppose because it's pointless for a dead man to look forward," replied the bandit, his Altmer frame filling the breadth of her doorway, "but I take it you didn't summon me to talk about old times." "Ehlhiel says the city guard knows about the hideout. They plan to raid the place in three days." "So they will," Aesrael replied, his face unflinching, "What of the spoils?" "We can't take it with us," Tyra lamented, "but I'll be damned if I let them have it. We give what we can to the beggars, and toss the rest into the bay before we leave." "As you wish," said the High Elf, "and where will you go?" "Our best chance is north," Tyra said, tracing her dagger up the map, "The Jarls are fractured. It's only a matter of time before the whole province is at war. But we'll have to move in small groups, and find our own way once we cross the border. No contact." Tyra knew Aesrael would take to the news better than the rest. While Bjormund, Skjol, and Peladius were the muscle, they always made an effort to bond with the group. The High Elf, on the other hand, never felt at ease with the other bandits. If this were any other business, perhaps she would've tried to reach him, but tenderness was not a virtue for killers and thieves. Aesrael nodded and took his leave, leaving Tyra alone in the quiet. If this exchange taught her anything, she still needed a moment before telling the others. She had always been an expert at masking her emotions, but the sadness wore plainly on her face. Perhaps this situation called for that girl from Balmora, and not the weary woman who sat in her stead. Steeling herself, Tyra placed the dirk and the ruby in her pouch and stepped away from the map. They would head for the border tomorrow, leaving behind much of their past, but the future still unwritten.

提拉已经想不起来哪一票是自己的最爱。或许是从沙丘城宫殿偷来一辆价值连城的马车那次，或许是挖地道进入东帝国公司那次，他们在门外守卫的无能狂怒中把货箱一个个运走。也可能她更喜欢比较暴力的那几次，像劫掠阿尔贡补给车队，或者是袭击从帝都滨水区起航的货船。 又或许，如果她回忆的更久远一些，她最美好的记忆应该是在巴尔莫拉街头流浪时，靠一把小刀抢劫旅客。不知为何，这段本已几乎遗忘的陌生的回忆，如今想起来却最为历历在目。那个文雅深虑的领袖面容已然模糊，只剩下一个饥饿、灰尘满面、勇气远胜于理性的孩子。而如果她闭上眼睛，她依然能感受到贵族丢在她手心那颗光滑闪亮的红宝石，那触感仿佛不属于这个世界。 但并非那颗宝石的触感或价值让她感触最深，而是那颜色。如同被猩红的尖刀把红山的烈焰烧进玻璃中那样。 “你觉得到底是为什么，”她问艾瑟瑞：“当我们命悬一线时，思绪都会回到过去？” “我觉得大概是死人没有向前看的必要了。”艾瑟瑞答道，他那傲特莫式高大的身影遮挡住了门框，“但我猜你召我来不是为了谈论旧时光的。” “埃赫尔说城市卫兵已经知道了这个藏身处。他们打算三天内突袭这里。” “他们当然会。”艾瑟瑞说道，脸上没有丝毫惧色。“那战利品怎么办。” “我们没法带走了。”提拉叹道：“但我也绝不会让他们得到。我们尽可能把它们分发给乞丐，再把剩下的丢进海湾。” “如你所愿。”艾瑟瑞答道，“那我们接下来到哪里去？” “我们最好去北方。”提拉说着，指着地图上插着的匕首。“那里的领主们正在陷入分裂，整个省爆发战争只是时间问题。但我们必须分成小组行动，而且一旦跨过边境后就各自谋生，不再联系。” 提拉知道艾瑟瑞会比其他人更能接受这个消息。布乔蒙德、斯科卓和佩拉迪乌斯作为打手，总是努力与团队协作，但艾瑟瑞这位高精却从不喜与其他人一起行动。如果这是其他任何事，提拉之后或许可能还会去找他，但关怀他人对一群杀手和盗贼来说从来不是什么美德。 艾瑟瑞点头离开了，只剩提拉一人在一片寂静里。如果说这场会面提醒了提拉什么，那就是在把消息告诉剩下的人之前，她依然需要点时间缓缓。她向来擅长掩盖自己的真情实感，但如今脸上却写满了悲伤。或许现在这个情况更需要当年那位巴尔莫拉街头的女孩，而不是如今这个在马背上筋疲力尽的女人。 提拉把红宝石和长匕装进袋子，从地图前离开了，尽力让自己坚强起来。明天他们就将前往边境，把绝大部分过去抛在身后，但未来却依旧没有定数。

As a fan of the Imperial Arena and student of history, I was very intrigued when I discovered volume eight of the short story collection, The Crimson Dirks, at a local library in Cheydinhal. While the librarian considered it a work of fiction, I've combed over the information in the story and much to my delight, found much of it may be true!

For instance, there was indeed an Orc who fought in Dwarven mail after the Great War, who rose to the rank of Bloodletter before mysteriously disappearing! The same is true for the blacksmith, who abandoned her shop in Cyrodiil under equally unknown circumstances! 

While I have nothing on the Redguard, the name itself may be an alias. But the last sentence is most intriguing, as it implies our Orc Bloodletter went north to Skyrim, and began fighting in the underground pits! In fact, I've heard there's an Orc living in the Bthalft Ruins who matches that description right now!

I've requested the Orc meet with me in private, so I can ask him if he is indeed the one in the story. I am so excited! I know the book paints him as a bit unruly toward fans, but authors tend to exaggerate certain features. Besides, even if it were true, I'd be willing to bet time has softened his stance. He'll be more than pleased to meet a true fan of the Arena! I can't wait!</font>

比如，在浩大战争之后，确实有一个穿着矮人链甲的兽人在竞技场战斗过，还在神秘消失前升到了放血者级别！还有那个铁匠，也是在不为人知的情况下，放弃了在希罗帝尔的店面！

虽然我没有那个红卫人的资料，但这个名字也可能是个别名。但最后一句话很有趣，因为它在暗示我们的兽人放血者北上天际，并开始在深坑竞技场战斗！事实上，我确实听说有个符合描述的兽人生活在巴塔尔夫特遗迹！

我已经邀请兽人与我单独见面了，这样我就可以问问他是不是故事里的那个人。我太兴奋了！我知道书里把他写的对粉丝不太守规矩，但作者往往会夸大某些特征。此外，即使是真的，我也愿意打赌时间已经软化了他的立场。他肯定会非常高兴见到一位真正的竞技场粉丝！我都等不及了！</font>

n his time with the Crimson Dirks, Urgnok had killed countless men, and heard all manner of reaction to their deaths. He'd heard women gasp, men cry, and children scream. Yet never in his life had he heard the noise that cascaded from the archways, when he plunged his sword into the belly of his assailant. Applause. When the crew disbanded, many of the Dirks were forced into the shadows, yet Urgnok's path took a different route. He met with a face butcher, adopted an alias, and joined the arena. And for the most part, the tactic seemed to work. These days, the only pursuers the Orc feared were the adoring fans that followed him in the street. "I suggest you turn around now," Urgnok grumbled, seeing a shadow cut through the door, "the last fan who annoyed me was this baker. He offered me a pastry, and I smashed his face in. Now he eats his sweet rolls through a straw." "Funny," the shadow replied, "I seem to recall a sparring session years ago that ended with you crying back to Tyra like a newborn babe." "Zaharia. What are you doing here?" "I came to see our mutual Orc friend," the Redguard said, examining a nearby weapon," I see you've already paid her a visit, judging by that armor. Dwarven, right? Although not exactly what I pictured." Urgnok spit at the ground, acknowledging what she left unspoken. The blacksmith was a magician with a hammer and anvil, working with all types of metal. Perhaps that was how the Redguard puzzled out his identity, yet it was unlikely a Blood-Kin would betray his confidence. "You know, the funny thing about fighting styles," Zaharia said, swinging the practice blade, "is that they're almost like fingerprints. You may have changed your armor, your name, and even your face, but I recognized that clumsy top foot of yours almost immediately." "Doesn't matter," Urgnok sneered, "The guard haven't sniffed me out yet, and they won't ever. I've been able to hide in plain sight, while everyone else is dying in the shadows." "Hiding in plain sight may work in the short term," Zaharia said, sliding the weapon back onto the rack, "But over time, you know what happens to things in plain sight? They get seen." "Cut the crap, Zaharia," the Orc groused, "we both know I don't care what you think." "True," the Redguard replied, handing him a letter, "but you'll care about this." Urgnok wasn't sure how he was discovered, or who wrote the letter to the guard. Had Zaharia not killed its bearer, he would already be in chains. He stopped short of accusing Zaharia of forging the note, however. She was crafty, but not a liar. "Where." "North," said the Redguard, "Get into one of the Strongholds, or take a job fighting in the pits. Either way, you can't stay here."

在为猩红长匕效命时，乌格诺克杀过无数人，见识过各种各样的人对死亡的反应。他见识过女人的喘息，男人的哭喊和孩童的尖叫。但是当他把剑刺进对手的腹部时，那种自拱顶上倾泻而下的声音他却从未听过。 掌声。 当团伙解散时，大部分成员都被迫低调谋生，但乌格诺克不同。他得到了一位整容师的帮助，换了假名，然后加入了竞技场。总的来说，计划似乎奏效了。这些天来，乌格诺克唯一怕的跟踪者就是在街头追着他跑的粉丝。 “我建议你最好现在就调头回去。”乌格诺克对着刚刚绕到门后的人影警告道：“上一个这么惹我的粉丝是个面包师，他要送我一份糕点，我就把他的脸砸了上去。现在他只能用吸管吸自己那些甜卷了。” “有意思。”人影说道：“让我想起几年前打的一场架，那次你像个小屁孩一样哭着跑回去找提拉。” “泽瑞哈亚？你在这里干啥？” “我来找咱俩都认识的一位兽人朋友。”红卫人说着，一边检视着旁边的一把武器，“从她做的那套盔甲来看，我猜你已经问候过他了。这套是矮人？虽然和我设想的不大一样。” 乌格诺克啐了一口，默认了泽瑞哈亚的话外音。那个铁匠简直是位锤与砧的魔法师，能处理各种金属。或许泽瑞哈亚就是靠这个推出他的身份的。不过作为血亲，她应该不会出卖乌格诺克。 “关于战斗风格，你知道最有趣的一点就在于，”泽瑞哈亚一边说着，一边挥舞着练习用剑，“它几乎像指纹一样，你或许已经改变了装备，名字甚至是长相，但我立刻就认出了你那笨拙的战斗步伐。” “无所谓的。”乌格诺克冷笑道：“卫兵到现在没有认出过我，以后也永远不可能认出我。我已经藏身于明处很久了，而其他人却早已死于暗处。” “藏在明处可能藏得了一时。”泽瑞哈亚把武器放回架子，说道：“但时间长了，你觉得会怎样？最终只会被发现。” “少废话了，泽瑞哈亚。”乌格诺克抱怨道，“你我都知道我才不在乎你的想法。” “确实。”泽瑞哈亚答道，把一封信交给了他。“但你会在乎这个的。” 乌格诺克不知道他是怎么暴露身份的，又或者是谁给卫兵写了这封信。如果不是泽瑞哈亚干掉了送信的人，他早就镣铐加身了。他有想到泽瑞哈亚可能伪造了这封信，但马上排除了这个想法。泽瑞哈亚或许狡诈，但并不是个骗子。 “我该去哪。” “往北吧。”泽瑞哈亚说道：“随便找一个兽人要塞，或者去深坑角斗场工作。无论哪种，你也不能继续待在这里了。”

yra Blood-Fire didn't want just any crew. Bandits never built Great Houses. They had no structure, organization, nor legacy. They had few tactics in the field and little design for the future. Worst of all they had no loyalty beyond filling their own pockets. A bandit clan was a pack of stray dogs fighting for scraps, willing to bite the hand if it dared to feed them. Growing up in Balmora, Tyra knew that the Great Houses of Morrowind were built on blood. Yet as an orphan child and a Nord amongst Elves, her concept of family was one forged from experience. It wasn't the bandits and cutthroats, but the loners and outcasts she identified with most. So when she picked out the crew that would become the Crimson Dirks, she sought out the qualities that best defined herself. What she wanted were survivors. To find them, she would first need connections. For this, she sought the help of a Dark Elf named Reaver. The Dunmer had no real name to speak of. Some speculated he was once a noble, having abandoned his titles and claims for a new one. Others believed he was with the Morag Tong, assassins having little use for their birth name. Tyra, meanwhile, had first met the brigand as a child begging in the streets. The Dark Elf had fixed his blood red eyes upon this orphan girl, ashen and starved, and deigned to fill her alms bowl. When she looked down, she found neither food nor gold, but a knife. "This isn't a gift, little netch," the Dunmer cautioned, throat scarred with ash, "your first score belongs to me." That night young Tyra would make good on that promise, delivering a single ruby into the ashlander's palm. It glowed crimson like fire and blood, and from that day she was known as Tyra Blood-Fire, earning her name just as Reaver did from his deeds. As the years passed, the Dunmer kept a close eye on the Nord, tracking her growth from a cutpurse to a bandit. And while she considered her debt to Reaver paid, whenever their paths crossed, he would continue to demand a cut. Eight years later, and the two had gone their separate ways - not just in distance, but in spirit and mind. Tyra had matured into a tenacious warrior, her physique chiseled and rough, a body forged in a crucible of blood and ash. Reaver, on the other hand, had grown fat and lazy, content to skim off the labor of his subordinates while he spent his days in quiet repose. As Tyra stood before him, he played with a ruby in his palm, occasionally using his forearm to wipe the saliva from his greasy lips. While Tyra recognized the gem almost immediately, the Dark Elf bared little resemblance to the vicious killer she once knew. Perhaps it was Cyrodiil that changed him. He had traded his netch leather for fine silks, his dagger for a silver spoon, and his ashland cave for a highborn residence in the heart of Skingrad. His scowl was not one of rage, but irritation, chiefly at his guest for tracking mud on his freshly waxed floors. Only the eyes, scarlet and piercing, betrayed his former identity. "I'm new to Cyrodiil," she said, placing a bag of gold on the table as tithe, "and I need a crew." The Dunmer beckoned a servant to hand him the gold, as he could no longer be bothered to reach for it. He examined the bag briefly to judge its weight, before shooing the servant and the gold aside. Tyra wondered if she had been better served filling the bag with cakes. "I will help you find these men," the Dunmer croaked, finger rapping the table, "but remember, little netch, your first score belongs to me." Of men who fit her requirements, there were three. Aesrael, the High Elf hunter, had grown up in an orphanage. Peladius was a former guardsman, dismissed for beating a pickpocket to death. Antonius was a hedge mage who spent more time at the tavern than the guild. There were still others she wanted before the crew could be whole. She wanted a blacksmith to forge arms, and muscle to wield it. She wanted a thief who could stalk their prey in the shadows, and assassins to slit their throats. She wanted scouts to glean information, and sharp minds to decipher their code. And she was willing to travel the breadth of Tamriel to find them. But for this first job, three was more than enough. One was all she needed. After all, she had already cased the building, having been invited as a guest. She had seen the servant girl deposit the gold in the next room, and the piles of riches scattered throughout the house. And she had watched as their plump, horker of an owner, lost his edge and taste for the work. For it was the reaver and all his riches that they would come for first. A week later, the three sealed their pact in blood. Aesrael and Peladius, being trained warriors, made quick work of the guards. Antonius bespelled the servants with his magic, and together the crew filled the wagons with their spoils. But before all that was done, Tyra first found the once fearsome reaver in his bed chambers, helpless to stop what his greed had ordained. In the shadow of a lantern's light, the Nord approached him with arms extended. In one hand was the bag of gold she had given him the week prior. In the other was the knife he had placed in her alms bowl so many years ago. "I want you to have this," Reaver said, placing the ruby on the nightstand beside him. Tyra, for her part, never said a word. "I wasn't always a reaver," the Dark Elf continued, "I used to have a proper name. Casival, they called me. Funny story, there's a Dunmer boy, peddling for alms outside the Two Sisters Lodge with the same name." Upon hearing his words, Tyra's eyes met Reaver's for the last time, standing over him as he once did her. Perhaps in that moment another deal was made, understood but left unspoken. Seconds later, she plunged the knife into his heart. When it was done, Tyra wiped the blood-stained dirk on the bedsheet and picked up the ruby from the nighstand. In the hours that passed the crew sacked the place clean, all save the bag of gold, which she left next to her former employer's corpse. The first score, after all, belonged to him. The rest she took for herself.

“血火”提拉不打算随便就招人。 强盗从来就不会建什么大家族，他们没有组织，没有架构，也没有遗产可被继承。他们没有战略眼光或者长远打算。最麻烦的是他们除了想自己赚钱外毫无忠诚可言。强盗团不过是一群为了残羹剩饭厮杀的流浪野狗，甚至随时愿意把任何敢喂它们的手都吃干抹净。 自幼生长于巴尔莫拉的提拉知道晨风的大家族是建立在血缘之上。但作为一个孤儿和一个成长于精灵之间的诺德异类，她对家庭的概念是基于自己的经验定义的。那个家庭的成员不能是强盗和凶手，而要是她最认同的独行侠和弃儿。所以，当她招募未来将成为猩红长匕一员的人时，每个人都必须是她自己精挑细选的。 她真正想招的，是懂得如何生存的人。 为了找到这些人，她首先需要一个联系人。这次，她找到了那个叫“劫掠者”的丹莫帮忙。 没人知道这个丹莫的真名，有人猜他曾是个贵族，在放弃了原本身份后另起了个新名，也有人觉得他曾是莫拉格堂的一员刺客，以代号为名字。至于提拉，她在还是名流浪街头乞讨的孤儿时遇到了这个土匪。当时，他用血红的眼睛看着这个蓬头垢面、饥肠辘辘的孤儿，俯身在她的碗里放了个东西。 提拉低头看时，那不是食物或钱，而是一把小刀。 “这不是一份免费的礼物，小气母。”丹莫用饱经沧桑的声音提醒道：“你的第一票归我。” 那一晚，年幼的提拉信守承诺。将一颗独一无二的红宝石交到了这位灰地民的手中。那块宝石散发着像鲜血和火焰一样猩红的光芒，自那一天后，她便被称为“血火”提拉，就像“劫掠者”一样，靠自己的行径为自己赢得了一个称号。数年过去了，这位丹莫一直仔细地注意着提拉，看着她从一位扒手成长为一个匪徒。而当提拉认为自己早已还清她对“劫掠者”的债时，每次他们相遇，他还是会要一笔分红。 八年后，两人分道扬镳——不仅在实际距离上，也在思想观念上。提拉已经成长为一位坚韧的战士。她体格粗壮，在血与灰烬中练就了强健的躯体。另一边的“劫掠者”已经变得臃肿懒惰，满足于在安逸中盘剥下属。 当提拉再一次站在他面前时，他正在玩弄掌中的红宝石，不时用手臂抹去油腻的唇角淌出的涎水。提拉立刻就认出了那颗红宝石，但却很难将眼前这个丹莫与她曾经熟悉的那位危险的杀手联系起来。 或许是希罗帝尔的文化改变了他。他把自己的气母皮甲换成了华美的丝绸，拿匕首换取了银勺，拿灰地的洞穴换成了一处位于斯金格勒中心的高级住宅。他的神情不复有真正的怒意，而是充斥着不耐烦，用来针对那些让他闪亮的打蜡地板沾上泥巴的客人。只有那双猩红而又敏锐的眼睛，透露出他曾经的身份。 “我新来希罗帝尔。”她一边说着，一边将一袋金币放到桌上作为入门礼。“我还需要招募人手。” 丹莫示意仆人把钱递给他，因为他已懒得自己动手。他仔细检查袋子并掂重后，打发仆人拿走了钱。提拉觉得如果袋子里装的是蛋糕，效果可能更佳。 “我会帮你找人。”丹莫一边用手指敲打着桌面，一边用沙哑的嗓音说道：“但是记住，小气母，你的第一票归我。” 有三个人符合提拉的要求：艾瑟瑞，从小作为孤儿长大的高精猎人；佩拉迪乌斯，因将一名扒手殴打致死而被开除的前卫兵；安东尼奥斯，一位在酒馆里待的时间比公会还长的不入流法师。 要让自己的组织完整，提拉还需要招更多人。她想要一位能造武器的铁匠，搭配一个武功高强的打手；一位能在暗处追踪猎物的盗贼，搭配一个杀人于无形的刺客；一位能收集情报的斥候，搭配一个破解谜题的智囊。为了找到这些人，她愿意跑遍泰姆瑞尔。 但是对于干第一票来说，三个手下就足够了。事实上，提拉只要一个人就行。毕竟，她早已作为客人逛过那栋建筑，见过女仆把金币藏在附近的房间里，还有分布在房子周围的成堆财宝，以及那个臃肿如海象，丧失了锐意和进取心的主人。他正是“劫掠者”。他的财富将成为提拉的第一票。 一周后，三个手下歃血为盟。艾瑟瑞和佩拉迪乌斯两个训练有素的战士快速解决掉守卫，安东尼奥斯用魔法赶跑了仆人，三人将财宝装上马车。 但在这一切结束前，提拉在卧室里找到了这位曾经叱咤风云的劫掠者，他正无助地试图阻止这场因自己的贪婪带来的厄运。 在灯火下，提拉一手拿着一周前给他的钱袋，一手握着他许多年前放在她碗里的那把小刀，向他缓缓逼近。 “你收下这个吧。”“劫掠者”说着，把那颗红宝石放到了身边的床头柜上，提拉看着，一言不发。 “我并非生来就是劫掠者。”丹莫继续说道：“我曾有一个真名，叫卡西瓦。巧的是，还有一个同名的丹莫男孩现在正在‘双胞姊妹旅店’门口施舍穷人。” 听到这话，提拉的眼神与“劫掠者”最后一次相交，正如多年前一般。或许在这一刻，又一个协议在沉默中达成了。 接着，提拉把刀捅进了他的心脏。 完事后，提拉用床单擦干沾血的长匕，从床头柜上拿走了红宝石。接下来的几小时，她的部下将此地洗劫一空，只有那袋她放在前主人尸体旁的金币留了下来。 毕竟，第一票归他，剩下的所有，都归提拉。

首先，我要就测试的事抱歉。我希望这能给我打开一扇窗，让我了解你的想法，并给我带来安慰。

你给了乞丐一整袋金币。你是个把他人生命置于自身之上的高尚之人。但是，即便是一千塞普汀也不能拯救所有男女儿童的生命。

所以我给你的建议是不要成为你自己善良的牺牲品。像我这样的人会利用这样的机会。有时候，为了获得更大的收益，你必须做出艰难的抉择。力所能及地去救人，但在必须取舍的时候也要果决。

最后，告知我生前认识的人，不要哀悼我的死。就像你们曾经有人跟我说的那样，当你所作的一切都只是回顾往昔时，就该对未来合上那本书了。我是按自己的意愿做出选择的。永别了。</font>

First off, I'm sorry about the tests. My hope was that it'd give me a window into your mind, and bring comfort to mine. 

You chose to pray for the beggar, putting your faith in the Divines. After all, maybe it isn't food or water people need, but hope in something greater than themselves. But the world is not a place where hope alone will save you.

My advice to you is to seize your destiny. Don't wait for an idle god. Then you'll be a worthy judge and executioner for your enemies, just as you were for me.

Lastly, to the ones I knew in life, don't mourn my death. As one of you once told me, when all you do is look to the past, it's time to close the book on one's future. I do so on my own terms. Goodbye.</font>

original: Letter from Tyra Blood-Fire
traduit: “血火”提拉的来信

original:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
<Alias=Player>,
My name is Tyra Blood-Fire. Like Sottilde the Wet Ear before me, I am an orphan child of Balmora. Many years ago, I took a band of misfits and rogues and turned them into the Crimson Dirks. In our heyday, they called us thieves, bandits, apostates and killers. And they were right. We were all of those things. 

But so is the Jarl who taxes the poor to starvation, the soldiers who rape and pillage the towns, the Empire who would erase our gods, and the guardsman who would behead the innocent.

I know your story. If there's going to be a judge for me, I don't want it to be them. Not the Empire, not the East Empire Company, and not the guards. Just you and the Divines.

But first I want you to prove you're a worthy judge.  

Go to the docks in Windhelm. There, you'll meet a beggar in need of your aid. Some would offer him gold. Others, bread or wine. Offer him the alms you think will best serve him.

Once you have proved your measure and your mercy, you must then show your mettle. I will wait for you at the Talos shrine west of Windhelm. 

When at last we meet, I ask that you speak only with your blade. For while the tongue lies, the sword is true. 

-Tyra</font>
traduit:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'>
<Alias=Player>,
我叫“血火”提拉。如我之前的“湿耳”索蒂尔德一样，是巴尔莫拉的一个孤儿。多年前，我带了一群边缘人和流氓，把他们变成了“猩红匕首”。全盛时，他们把我们视为小偷、强盗、叛教者和杀人犯。他们说的没错。这些事我们都干过。

但同样可怕的，还有盘剥小民让他们冻饿而死的领主，在城镇烧杀掳掠的士兵，还有抹杀我们信仰的帝国，还有拿着无辜者脑袋领赏的卫兵。

我听说过你的事迹。如果要对我进行审判，那我也不想让他们动手。不管是帝国、东帝国公司还是卫兵。只有你和圣灵才行。

但首先我要你证明自己是个合格的裁决者。

到风舵城的码头去。那里有个需要你帮助的乞丐。有人会给他金币。也有人会给面包或酒。给他你觉得最合适的施舍。

等你证明完自己的方寸和仁慈，就来展示你的勇气吧。我在风舵城以西的塔洛斯祭坛等你。

等我们最后见面到时候，只用你的剑说话就好。舌头是会说谎的，但刀剑不会。

--提拉</font>
