The Monomyth

[pagebreak]

"In Mundus, conflict and disparity are what bring change, and change is the most sacred of the Eleven Forces. Change is the force without focus or origin."-Oegnithr, Taheritae, Order of PSJJJJ [pagebreak] imply put, the schism in the Human/Aldmeri worldview is the mortal's relationship to the divine. Humans take the humble path that they were created by the immortal forces, while the Aldmer claim descent from them. It doesn't seem like much, but it is a distinction that colors the rest of their diverging mythologies. All Tamrielic religions begin the same. Man or mer, things begin with the dualism of Anu and His Other. These twin forces go by many names: Anu-Padomay, Anuiel-Sithis, Ak-El, Satak-Akel, Is-Is Not. Anuiel is the Everlasting Ineffable Light, Sithis is the Corrupting Inexpressible Action. In the middle is the Gray Maybe ('Nirn' in the Ehlnofex). In most cultures, Anuiel is honored for his part of the interplay that creates the world, but Sithis is held in highest esteem because he's the one that causes the reaction. Sithis is thus the Original Creator, an entity who intrinsically causes change without design. Even the hist acknowledge this being. Anuiel is also perceived of as Order, opposed to the Sithis-Chaos. Perhaps it is easier for mortals to envision change than perfect stasis, for often Anuiel is relegated to the mythic background of Sithis' fancies. In Yokudan folk-tales, which are among the most vivid in the world, Satak is only referred to a handful of times, as "the Hum"; he is a force so prevalent as to be not really there at all. In any case, from these two beings spring the et'Ada, or Original Spirits. To humans these et'Ada are the Gods and Demons; to the Aldmer, the Aedra/Daedra, or the 'Ancestors'. All of the Tamrielic pantheons fill their rosters from these et'Ada, though divine membership often differs from culture to culture. Like Anu and Padomay, though, every one of these pantheons contains the archetypes of the Dragon God and the Missing God. [pagebreak] The Dragon God and the Missing God The Dragon God is always related to Time, and is universally revered as the "First God." He is often called Akatosh, "whose perch from Eternity allowed the day." He is the central God of the Cyrodilic Empire. The Missing God is always related to the Mortal Plane, and is a key figure in the Human/Aldmeri schism. The 'missing' refers to either his palpable absence from the pantheon (another mental distress that is interpreted a variety of ways), or the removal of his 'divine spark' by the other immortals. He is often called Lorkhan, and his epitaphs are many, equally damnable and devout. Note that Tamriel and the Mortal Plane do not exist yet. The Gray Maybe is still the playground of the Original Spirits. Some are more bound to Anu's light, others to the unknowable void. Their constant flux and interplay increase their number, and their personalities take long to congeal. When Akatosh forms, Time begins, and it becomes easier for some spirits to realize themselves as beings with a past and a future. The strongest of the recognizable spirits crystallize: Mephala, Arkay, Y'ffre, Magnus, Rupgta, etc., etc. Others remain as concepts, ideas, or emotions. One of the strongest of these, a barely formed urge that the others call Lorkhan, details a plan to create Mundus, the Mortal Plane. Humans, with the exception of the Redguards, see this act as a divine mercy, an enlightenment whereby lesser creatures can reach immortality. Aldmer, with the exception of the Dark Elves, see this act as a cruel deception, a trick that sundered their connection to the spirit plane. [pagebreak] The Myth of Aurbis Subtitled "The Psijiic Compensation," "Mythic Aurbis" was an attempt by Artaeum apologists to explain the basics of Aldmeri religion to Uriel V in the early, glorious part of his reign. It quietly avoided any blame or bias against the Lorkhan-concept, which was still held in esteem by the Cyrodiils as "Shezarr", the missing sibling of the Divines. Despite this, the Psijiici still give a nice summary of the Elder view, and it will serve our purposes here. This version comes from the archives of the Imperial Seminary from the handwritten notes of an unknown scribe. [pagebreak] Mythic Aurbis exists, and has existed from time without measure, as a fanciful Unnatural Realm. 'Aurbis' is used to connote the imperceptible Penumbra, the Gray Center between the IS/IS NOT of Anu and Padomay. It contains the multitude realms of Aetherius and Oblivion, as well as other, less structured forms. The magical beings of Mythic Aurbis live for a long time and have complex narrative lives, creating the patterns of myth. These are spirits made from bits of the immortal polarity. The first of these was Akatosh the Time Dragon, whose formation made it easier for other spirits to structure themselves. Gods and demons form and reform and procreate. Finally, the magical beings of Mythic Aurbis told the ultimate story -- that of their own death. For some this was an artistic transfiguration into the concrete, non-magical substance of the world. For others, this was a war in which all were slain, their bodies becoming the substance of the world. For yet others, this was a romantic marriage and parenthood, with the parent spirits naturally having to die and give way to the succeeding mortal races. The agent of this communal decision was Lorkhan, whom most early myths vilify as a trickster or deceiver. More sympathetic versions of this story point out Lorkhan as being the reason the mortal plane exists at all. The magical beings created the races of the mortal Aurbis in their own image, either consciously as artists and craftsmen, or as the fecund rotting matter out of which the mortals sprung forth, or in a variety of other analogical senses. The magical beings, then, having died, became the et'Ada. The et'Ada are the things perceived and revered by the mortals as gods, spirits, or geniuses of Aurbis. Through their deaths, these magical beings separated themselves in nature from the other magical beings of the Unnatural realms. The Daedra were created at this time also, being spirits and Gods more attuned to Oblivion, or that realm closer to the Void of Padomay. This act is the dawn of the Mythic (Merethic) Era. It has been perceived by the earliest mortals many different ways, either as a joyous 'second creation', or (especially by the Elves) as a painful fracturing from the divine. The originator of the event is always Lorkhan. [pagebreak] Lorkhan This Creator-Trickster-Tester deity is in every Tamrielic mythic tradition. His most popular name is the Aldmeri "Lorkhan," or Doom Drum. He convinced or contrived the Original Spirits to bring about the creation of the Mortal Plane, upsetting the status quo much like his father Padomay had introduced instability into the universe in the Beginning Place. After the world is materialized, Lorkhan is separated from his divine center, sometimes involuntarily, and wanders the creation of the et'Ada. Interpretations of these events differ widely by culture. Below are some of the better known: Yokudan, "Satakal the Worldskin" "Satak was First Serpent, the Snake who came Before, and all the worlds to come rested in the glimmer of its scales. But it was so big there was nothing but, and thus it was coiled around and around itself, and the worlds to come slid across each other but none had room to breathe or even be. And so the worlds called to something to save them, to let them out, but of course there was nothing outside the First Serpent, so aid had to come from inside it; this was Akel, the Hungry Stomach. Akel made itself known, and Satak could only think about what it was, and it was the best hunger, so it ate and ate. Soon there was enough room to live in the worlds and things began. These things were new and they often made mistakes, for there was hardly time to practice being things before. So most things ended quickly or were not good or gave up on themselves. Some things were about to start, but they were eaten up as Satak got to that part of its body. This was a violent time. "Pretty soon Akel caused Satak to bite its own heart and that was the end. The hunger, though, refused to stop, even in death, and so the First Serpent shed its skin to begin anew. As the old world died, Satakal began, and when things realized this pattern so did they realize what their part in it was. They began to take names, like Ruptga or Tuwhacca, and they strode about looking for their kin. As Satakal ate itself over and over, the strongest spirits learned to bypass the cycle by moving at strange angles. They called this process the Walkabout, a way of striding between the worldskins. Ruptga was so big that he was able to place the stars in the sky so that weaker spirits might find their way easier. This practice became so easy for the spirits that it became a place, called the Far Shores, a time of waiting until the next skin. "Ruptga was able to sire many children through the cycles and so he became known as the Tall Papa. He continued to place stars to map out the void for others, but after so many cycles there were almost too many spirits to help out. He made himself a helper from the detritus of past skins and this was Sep, or Second Serpent. Sep had much of the Hungry Stomach still left in him, multiple hungers from multiple skins. He was so hungry he could not think straight. Sometimes he would just eat the spirits he was supposed to help, but Tall Papa would always reach in and take them back out. Finally, tired of helping Tall Papa, Sep went and gathered the rest of the old skins and balled them up, tricking spirits to help him, promising them this was how you reached the new world, by making one out of the old. These spirits loved this way of living, as it was easier. No more jumping from place to place. Many spirits joined in, believing this was good thinking. Tall Papa just shook his head. "Pretty soon the spirits on the skin-ball started to die, because they were very far from the real world of Satakal. And they found that it was too far to jump into the Far Shores now. The spirits that were left pleaded with Tall Papa to take them back. But grim Ruptga would not, and he told the spirits that they must learn new ways to follow the stars to the Far Shores now. If they could not, then they must live on through their children, which was not the same as before. Sep, however, needed more punishment, and so Tall Papa squashed the Snake with a big stick. The hunger fell out of Sep's dead mouth and was the only thing left of the Second Serpent. While the rest of the new world was allowed to strive back to godhood, Sep could only slink around in a dead skin, or swim about in the sky, a hungry void that jealously tried to eat the stars." [pagebreak] Cyrodilic ""Shezarr's Song"" "This was a new thing that Shezarr described to the Gods, becoming mothers and fathers, being responsible, and making great sacrifices, with no guarantee of success, but Shezarr spoke beautifully to them, and moved them beyond mystery and tears. Thus the Aedra gave free birth to the world, the beasts, and the beings, making these things from parts of themselves. This free birth was very painful, and afterwards the Aedra were no longer young, and strong, and powerful, as they had been from the beginning of days. "Some Aedra were disappointed and bitter in their loss, and angry with Shezarr, and with all creation, for they felt Shezarr had lied and tricked them. These Aedra, the Gods of the Aldmer, led by Auri-El, were disgusted by their enfeebled selves, and by what they had created. 'Everything is spoiled, for now, and for all time, and the most we can do is teach the Elven Races to suffer nobly, with dignity, and chastise ourselves for our folly, and avenge ourselves upon Shezarr and his allies.' Thus are the Gods of the Elves dark and brooding, and thus are the Elves ever dissatisfied with mortality, and always proud and stoic despite the harshness of this cruel and indifferent world. "Other Aedra looked upon creation, and were well pleased. These Aedra, the Gods of Men and Beast Folk, led by Akatosh, praised and cherished their wards, the Mortal Races. 'We have suffered, and are diminished, for all time, but the mortal world we have made is glorious, filling our hearts and spirits with hope. Let us teach the Mortal Races to live well, to cherish beauty and honor, and to love one another as we love them.' Thus are the Gods of Men tender and patient, and thus are Men and Beast Folk great in heart for joy or suffering, and ambitious for greater wisdom and a better world. "Now when the Daedra Lords heard Shezarr, they mocked him, and the other Aedra. 'Cut parts of ourselves off? And lose them? Forever? That's stupid! You'll be sorry! We are far smarter than you, for we will create a new world out of ourselves, but we will not cut it off, or let it mock us, but we will make this world within ourselves, forever ours, and under our complete control.' "So the Daedra Lords created the Daedric Realms, and all the ranks of Lesser Daedra, great and small. And, for the most part, the Daedra Lords were well pleased with this arrangement, for they always had worshippers and servants and playthings close to hand. But, at the same time, they sometimes looked with envy upon the Mortal Realms, for though mortals were foul and feeble and contemptible, their passions and ambitions were also far more surprising and entertaining than the antics of the Lesser Daedra. Thus do the Daedra Lords court and seduce certain amusing specimens of the Mortal Races, especially the passionate and powerful. It gives the Daedra Lords special pleasure to steal away from Shezarr and the Aedra the greatest and most ambitious mortals. 'Not only are you fools to mutilate yourselves,' gloat the Daedra Lords, 'But you cannot even keep the best pieces, which prefer the glory and power of the Daedra Lords to the feeble vulgarity of the mush-minded Aedra.'" [pagebreak] Altmeri "The Heart of the World" "Anu encompassed, and encompasses, all things. So that he might know himself he created Anuiel, his soul and the soul of all things. Anuiel, as all souls, was given to self-reflection, and for this he needed to differentiate between his forms, attributes, and intellects. Thus was born Sithis, who was the sum of all the limitations Anuiel would utilize to ponder himself. Anuiel, who was the soul of all things, therefore became many things, and this interplay was and is the Aurbis. "At first the Aurbis was turbulent and confusing, as Anuiel's ruminations went on without design. Aspects of the Aurbis then asked for a schedule to follow or procedures whereby they might enjoy themselves a little longer outside of perfect knowledge. So that he might know himself this way, too, Anu created Auriel, the soul of his soul. Auriel bled through the Aurbis as a new force, called time. With time, various aspects of the Aurbis began to understand their natures and limitations. They took names, like Magnus or Mara or Xen. One of these, Lorkhan, was more of a limit than a nature, so he could never last long anywhere. "As he entered every aspect of Anuiel, Lorkhan would plant an idea that was almost wholly based on limitation. He outlined a plan to create a soul for the Aurbis, a place where the aspects of aspects might even be allowed to self-reflect. He gained many followers; even Auriel, when told he would become the king of the new world, agreed to help Lorkhan. So they created the Mundus, where their own aspects might live, and became the et'Ada. "But this was a trick. As Lorkhan knew, this world contained more limitations than not and was therefore hardly a thing of Anu at all. Mundus was the House of Sithis. As their aspects began to die off, many of the et'Ada vanished completely. Some escaped, like Magnus, and that is why there are no limitations to magic. Others, like Y'ffre, transformed themselves into the Ehlnofey, the Earthbones, so that the whole world might not die. Some had to marry and make children just to last. Each generation was weaker than the last, and soon there were Aldmer. Darkness caved in. Lorkhan made armies out of the weakest souls and named them Men, and they brought Sithis into every quarter. "Auriel pleaded with Anu to take them back, but he had already filled their places with something else. But his soul was gentler and granted Auriel his Bow and Shield, so that he might save the Aldmer from the hordes of Men. Some had already fallen, like the Chimer, who listened to tainted et'Ada, and others, like the Bosmer, had soiled Time's line by taking Mannish wives. "Auriel could not save Altmora, the Elder Wood, and it was lost to Men. They were chased south and east to Old Ehlnofey, and Lorkhan was close behind. He shattered that land into many. Finally Trinimac, Auriel's greatest knight, knocked Lorkhan down in front of his army and reached in with more than hands to take his Heart. He was undone. The Men dragged Lorkhan's body away and swore blood vengeance on the heirs of Auriel for all time. "But when Trinimac and Auriel tried to destroy the Heart of Lorkhan it laughed at them. It said, "This Heart is the heart of the world, for one was made to satisfy the other." So Auriel fastened the thing to an arrow and let it fly long into the sea, where no aspect of the new world may ever find it."

元神话

[pagebreak]

“梦达斯中，冲突与差异带来变化，而变化乃十一力中至崇高者。变化是无焦无源之力。”——PSJJJJ教团，奥格尼瑟，塔赫黎特 [pagebreak] 简而言之，人类与奥德莫世界观分歧的根源，就是神凡关系。人类心怀敬畏，自认是神灵不朽伟力的造物，而奥德莫则宣称自身源出于彼。两者看似联系不多，然而，正因如此给他们不同的神话增添了迥异的色彩。 泰姆瑞尔所有宗教都同源一处。人与莫，均出于阿努及他者的二元。这对力量有许多名字：阿努-帕多梅，阿努艾尔-西帝斯，阿克-艾尔，撒塔科-阿克尔，“是”-“非”。阿努艾尔是永恒而不可言喻的光，西帝斯是腐朽而难以言表的行为，二者交汇就是“灰色可能”（伊诺菲语里的“奈恩”）。 在绝大多数文化中，阿努艾尔因身为创世互动原力之一而备受尊敬，然而西帝斯却较之更甚，因为他是引动了反应。西帝斯因而被视为原初造物者：一个未经设计就从本质上引起变化的存在。就连希斯特也承认其存在。 阿努艾尔也被视为秩序的象征，而与之相反的西帝斯即是混沌。可能对于凡人而言，理解可预见的变化相较于保持绝对的静止更为容易，因而阿努艾尔总是沦为西帝斯神秘奇迹的神话背景板。在尤库达人那些最为生动的民间传说中，撒塔科——被称为“亨”——被提到的次数屈指可数，因为他是无远弗届却寻常可见的伟力，乃至人们往往忽视其存在。 无论如何，在这两者的相互作用下催生了“艾'阿达”，或说“原灵”。人类将艾'阿达视作神与魔；而奥德莫则称“伊德拉”/“迪德拉”，或“先祖”。虽然所有泰姆瑞尔信仰体系都源于这些艾'阿达，但其中的成员却因文化而异。但尽管如此，就如阿努和帕多梅那般，每一类神话体系都包含有“龙神”和“缺位神”这种形象原型。 [pagebreak] 龙神和缺位神 龙神通常与“时间”相关，且总被尊为“首神”。他往往被称为阿卡托什，“栖身永恒之中，创生时间昼夜”。在希罗帝尔帝国信仰中被尊为主神。 缺位神则总与凡界相关，是引发人类/奥德莫分裂的关键。“缺位”指他显然从各信仰在被隐去（另一种精神上的痛苦有更多样的解释），或者指代他的“神圣火花”被其他不朽剥夺了。他常被称作洛克汗，对他的评价也褒贬不一。 需注意，远在泰姆瑞尔乃至凡界尚未存在时，“灰色可能”仍是原灵们的游乐场。其中一部分偏爱阿努的光明，另一些则更倾心于满是未知的虚空。他们不断地流动与相互作用使得数量不断增加，但自身的个性却需要很长时间才能凝结。阿卡托什成形，时间便开始流动，而这让部分原灵更容易判明他们本身是拥有过往与未来的存在。在这些拥有意识的原灵中，最强大的那些个体陆续凝聚：梅法拉，阿尔凯，伊’符瑞，玛格努斯，卢普特迦等等。其余者则更多是以概念、灵感、情绪等形式，无形态存在着。原灵中最强大的一员，一股勉强形成的冲动，也就是洛克汗，详细诉说了创造凡界梦达思的计划。 除红卫人外，人类都将洛克汗此举视为一种神圣的怜悯，一种让低等生物也能达成超凡的启示。而除暗精灵外，奥德莫均将之视为残忍的欺瞒，一场破坏他们和原灵位面联系的诡计。 [pagebreak] 奥比斯之秘 副标题为“赛伊克赠偿”的《奥比斯之秘》是阿塔姆宗教辩护者们所做的一次尝试，目的是向正处于统治早年光辉时期的尤瑞尔五世论述有关奥德莫信仰的基础知识。这篇文章已尽可能避免展露对洛克汗（希罗帝尔称为“舍扎尔”，是圣灵缺位的同胞）的任何非难或偏见。尽管如此，赛伊克们仍然作出了一份优良的上古视角概要，有助于阐述我们的题目。此版本为一位隶属帝国神学院档案室的某位不知名抄写员的抄录本。 [pagebreak] 神秘的奥比斯有如幻想而成的非自然领域，其存在更早于时间可被度量以前。 “奥比斯”用来形容难以明确分辨的半影，象征着阿努和帕多梅的“是”和“非”黑白交融混杂所成的灰色中心。它囊括了光界和湮灭无量的领域，以及其他结构形式不如前二者那般复杂的领域。 　　 在这神秘的奥比斯中的神奇存在们寿命悠长，各自拥有言说曲折的生涯，造就了形形色色的神话。 　　 这些精魂是超凡极性的碎片凝成的。当先者是时间龙神阿卡托什，他的诞生令其他精魂更容易构建自我。神魔形成、改造，继而繁衍。 　　 最终，奥比斯中的神奇存在们，诠释了一段终极传奇——关于他们自身的死亡。于某些精魂而言，这不过是一场转化为世界上那些具象、非魔法性物质的艺术。但于另一些精魂而言，却是一场所有人都被杀害的战争，他们的身体化作世界上的物质。而对于一些而言，这是一场浪漫的婚姻和哺育；身为父母的精魂自然会逝去，把舞台让给后继的凡人种族。 　　 主导这一重大集体决策的，是被各大早期神话诋毁为骗子或欺诈者的洛克汗。对于该故事，更富同情心的版本则指出，洛克汗正是凡界得以存在的原因。 　　 神奇存在们依照自己的形象，创造了奥比斯众多凡人种族。或是他们如艺术家和工匠般有意而为，也可能是他们化为丰饶肥沃的温床，让凡人们如雨后春笋般涌现，或是以其他各式各样的类似形式诞生。 　　 随后，这些神奇存在们就此死去，化为艾'阿达。艾'阿达们被凡人们尊为奥比斯诸神、精魂、天赋来崇拜。因为他们的死亡，这些散入自然界的神奇存在自此与那些处于超凡领域的同胞们隔绝。 　　 迪德拉们亦于此时被创生，他们成为了更适应湮灭、或是更临近帕多梅虚空的领域的精魂与神。此即神话纪元的开端。然而最早的凡人们对此事的认识各有不同，或称此乃值得欣喜的“二次创造”，或（特别是精灵）被认为是与神圣相切割的痛苦。但事件的始作俑者，总是洛克汗。 [pagebreak] 洛克汗 每一篇泰姆瑞尔神话传统都绕不开这位创世神、欺诈师、考验者。他流传最广的名号就是奥德莫语的“洛克汗”，或“末日之鼓”。他说服或诱骗了众原灵去创造凡界，以打破现状，正如他父亲帕多梅曾在起源之地向宇宙注入了不稳定那样。当世界实质化后，洛克汗被迫与其神性中心分离（有些说法是非自愿的），并在众艾'阿达的造物中流连徘徊。对这些事件的解释因文化而异。以下是比较知名的版本： 尤库达：“世界之皮——撒塔卡尔” “首蛇”撒塔科，生于一切之前，所有世界都栖息于他鳞片的微光中。但他过于庞大，且外无他物，所以就一圈圈盘绕起来，众界彼此滑擦，但没有任何呼吸与存在的空间。所以众世界呼唤拯救，让他们能够解脱出来。当然，首蛇之外别无他物，援助之内来自其内，也就是——“饥饿之胃”阿克尔。阿克尔的主动显现，使得撒塔科只能想着它，想着那巨大的饥饿，只能不断地吃啊吃。很快，各世界有了足够的空间继续存在，事物开始发展。然而因为没有时间熟悉曾经的东西，这些新生的存在经常犯错。所以大多数东西转瞬即逝，或不够完美，又或直接自暴自弃。但也有一些存在刚要开始，就因为撒塔科抵达它身体的那一部分，结果被吃掉。这是一个荒蛮的时代。 没过多久，阿克尔诱使撒塔科吃下心脏，一切就此告终。但就算在死亡中，饥饿也并未停止，首蛇开始再度蜕皮重生。随着旧世界消亡，撒塔卡尔开始了，在其他存在意识到这种模式时，也明白了自己在其中的角色。他们开始给自己起名，如卢普特迦或是图瓦卡，又更进一步四处寻访同族。撒塔卡尔仍在反复自我吞噬的时候，那些最强的精魂则学会了在这种时候位移到某些陌生角落里躲避循环。他们称此过程为“漫步”，一种在世界之皮上穿越跨行的方法。其中，卢普特迦已庞大到足以布置星辰，以指引弱小的精魂更容易找到道路。方法变得简单，精魂们得以更容易前往那称之为‘远岸’的地方，等待下一次蜕皮。 卢普特迦于多次的轮回过程中诞下无数子嗣，因此被称为“大老爹”。他继续放置星辰，为他人绘制虚空的地图，但随着循环次数的增加，需要帮助的精魂也越来越多。为求解困，他自过去的蛇蜕中造出了他的帮手，“次蛇”塞普。塞普继承了饥饿之胃的大部分，各种不同的蛇蜕中也有不同的饥饿。他饿得无法正常思考，甚至会直接吃掉本该帮助的精魂，但大老爹都会把手伸进去，将他们救出来。最终，塞普厌倦了帮助大老爹的日子，把剩余的旧蛇蜕收集起来揉成一团，欺骗精魂们过来帮忙，并向他们保证，用这些旧皮做成新的，就是抵达新世界的方法。这些精魂很喜欢这种安逸轻松的方式。不用继续反复横跳。所以很多精魂加入其中，认定这是个好主意。大老爹听了只是摇头。 没过多久，蛇蜕球上的精魂开始死去，因为他们太过远离撒塔卡尔的真实世界。他们发现自己距离远岸太远，难以跳入其中。余下的精魂恳求大老爹救他们回去。但卢普特迦冰冷拒绝，他告诉这些精魂，现在他们必须学会新的方法，跟随星辰的指引返回远岸。做不到的话，就一代代继续尝试，这就是和过去的不同。当然，塞普需要更多惩罚，所以大老爹一棒把他打扁。饥饿从塞普死去的嘴里掉了出来，那就是次蛇仅剩的东西。当新世界中的其他人都被允许努力恢复神性时，塞普却只能披着死皮四处游荡，或者巡游天空，带着饥饿的空虚企图吃掉星辰。 [pagebreak] 希罗帝尔：“舍扎尔之歌” 舍扎尔向诸神描绘了全新的事物：成为父母，担负责任，在没有成功的保证下进行伟大的牺牲。但舍扎尔对他们口若悬河，触动他们超越神秘与泪水。因而，伊德拉们奉献自身孕育了世界，创生飞禽走兽、世间万物，这种随心意而进行的创生非常痛苦，伊德拉们变得不再年轻强大如初。 很多伊德拉因损失而失望痛苦，对舍扎尔和一切造物感到愤怒，他们认为舍扎尔欺骗了他们。这些伊德拉就是以奥瑞-艾尔为首的奥德莫众神，他们对自身的衰弱和导致这一切的他们的造物只觉厌恶。“万事休矣，从今往后，我们所能做的就是教会精灵高尚且有尊严地忍耐诸此一切，为自己的愚蠢惩罚自己，向舍扎尔及其盟友复仇。”因此，精灵众神阴暗且忧郁。精灵们也对凡性不满，尽管世界残酷冷漠，却总是保持着骄傲与坚忍。 其他的伊德拉看着创造的成果，深感欣喜。这些伊德拉多是由阿卡托什领导的人类与兽民的神明，赞叹呵护他们的凡人诸族。“我等历尽辛酸，神力也不断衰减，但我们所创造的凡界是荣耀的，我们的心灵与精魂充满希望。让我等教化凡人好好生活，爱惜美与荣誉，如我等爱他们那般相爱相惜。”因而人类诸神温柔且耐心，人类和兽民也是如此。他们有一颗能够直面悲喜的伟大心灵，热衷追求更广大的智慧和更美好的世界。 迪德拉君主们听说了舍扎尔的所为，他们讥讽他和其他伊德拉。“从自身剥离一部分？然后永远失去？真是蠢材！你们早晚会后悔的！我们比你们聪明多了，因为我们会创造自己的新世界，但不会像你们这样自我切离，或让它嘲讽我们。我们会创造隶属我们自己的世界，永远受我们完全掌控。” 迪德拉君主们创造了迪德拉领域，以及大大小小的各阶迪德拉生物。最令他们满意的是，他们能将信徒、奴仆、玩物牢牢掌握。但同时，他们偶尔也会嫉妒凡界。因为他们虽觉得凡人们既卑劣又弱小还粗野，但他们拥有的激情和雄心也远比迪德拉生物的滑稽举止更令人感到惊讶和有趣。因此，迪德拉君主们寻求并引诱凡人种族中某些有趣的个体，特别是那些激情而强大的人。从舍扎尔和伊德拉处偷走最伟大最具雄心的凡人们，似乎给予迪德拉君主们别样的快乐。“你们的愚昧之处不仅仅是自残，”迪德拉君主们幸灾乐祸，“你们甚至保不住自家最宝贝的东西，比起你们这些糊涂软弱的伊德拉，他们更爱迪德拉君主的荣耀和权能。” [pagebreak] 高精灵：“世界之心” 阿努包罗万物。为求能自我认知，他又创阿努艾尔，他的灵魂，也是万物的灵魂。阿努艾尔，作为万物之魂，也开始自我反省，为此须自行三等分割：形式、属性、智慧，由此诞生了西帝斯，他是阿努艾尔用于思考自身一切局限性的总和。阿努艾尔，作为万物之魂，因而化形万物，他们过去与现在相互作用形成的就是奥比斯。 起初的奥比斯动荡混乱，因为阿努艾尔的思索是在全无设计的情况下进行的。奥比斯的化身们随即要求制定秩序或规律，从而使他们可能在追寻完美知识的进取外享受余暇。为了认识自己，阿努又创造了他灵魂的灵魂——奥瑞艾尔。奥瑞艾尔于全奥比斯播下新的伟力，称为“时间”。随着时间流逝，奥比斯的方方面面开始知晓自身的性质与局限。他们为自己取了名字，如玛格努斯、玛拉、泽恩。他们的一员，洛克汗，所具有的局限远大于性质，所以他在任何地方都不能长久停留。 在他遍访阿努艾尔各灵时，洛克汗都会提出一项几乎完全基于局限性的想法。他概述关于为奥比斯创造灵魂的大计，各化身都可以在那里得到自我反思。他吸引了大量支持者，甚至奥瑞艾尔被他告知可以成为新世界的王时，也应承要帮助洛克汗。于是他们就此创造了使他们的化身亦可生存于其中的梦达思，同时化为艾'阿达。 但这是个骗局。洛克汗深知这新世界梦达思含有更多的局限性，所以并非阿努之造物，而是西帝斯的殿堂。当他们的化身渐渐崩坏，许多艾'阿达彻底消失。其中部分得以逃脱，例如玛格努斯，这便是魔法毫无局限性的原因。其余如伊'符瑞，自身化为伊诺菲（地骨），确保了全世界不至于消亡。剩下的则不断婚配繁衍后代来维持生命，他们的力量逐代变弱，最终便成了奥德莫。黑暗降临。洛克汗将最弱小的灵魂们拼凑作一支军队，赋名‘人类’，他们将西帝斯带往每一个角落。 奥瑞艾尔恳请阿努把他们带回去，但阿努已用其他事物填补了他们的位置。但他的灵魂起了恻隐之心，将弓与盾授予奥瑞艾尔，让他能从人类部落的围攻中拯救奥德莫。部分精灵已然堕落，如凯莫，服从被玷污的艾'阿达；而另一些，如波斯莫，则玷污了时间的血统，自甘堕落和人类婚配。 奥瑞艾尔无力挽救奥尔特莫拉大陆（古木大陆）并败给人类，他们被赶往东南向的古伊诺菲。洛克汗紧追不舍，他将这块大陆粉碎成无数块。最终崔尼玛克，奥瑞艾尔最强大的骑士，于两军阵前击倒洛克汗，并用双手将其心脏掏出。洛克汗就此败落。人类拖走洛克汗的遗体并歃血而誓，永远对奥瑞艾尔的后裔们复仇。 但当崔尼玛克和奥瑞艾尔尝试毁掉洛克汗之心时，洛克汗对着他们大笑：“这颗心就是为了满足世界而创造的世界之心。”奥瑞艾尔遂将心脏捆于一支箭上弯弓射出，让它远远飞落海中——一处新世界诸灵不能寻得的位置。

THE MARKSMANSHIP LESSON By Alla Llaleth

[pagebreak] [pagebreak]

elmeril Brin had very definite opinions on how things should be done. Every slave he bought on the day he bought him or her was soundly whipped in the courtyard for a period of one to three hours, depending on the individual degree of independent spirit. The whip he used -- or had his castellan use -- was of wet, knotted cloth, which regularly drew blood but very seldom maimed. To his great satisfaction and personal pride, few slaves ever needed to be whipped more than once. The memory of their first day, and the sight and sound of every subsequent slave's first day, stayed with them throughout their lives. When Brin bought his first Bosmer slave, he ordered his castellan to whip him only for an hour. The creature, which Brin had named Dob, seemed so much more delicate than the Argonians and Khajiiti and Orcs who made up the bulk of his slaves. Dob was clearly ill suited for work in the mines or in the fields, but he seemed presentable enough for domestic service. Dob did his work quietly and tolerably well. Brin occasionally had to correct him by refusing him food, but the punishment never needed to go further. Whenever guests arrived at the plantation, the sight of the exotic and elegant addition to Brin's household staff always impressed them. "Here, you," said Genethah Illoc, a minor but still noble member of the House Indoriil, as Dob presented her with a glass of wine. "Were you born a slave?" "No, sedura," Dob answered with a bow. "I used to rob nice ladies like you on the road." The company all laughed with delight, but Kelmeril Brin checked with the slave trader from whom he had bought Dob, and found that the story was true. The Bosmer had been a highwayman, though not one of any great notoriety, before he had been caught and sold into slavery as punishment. It seemed so extraordinary that a quiet fellow like Dob, who always looked respectfully downward at the sight of his superiors, could have been a criminal. Brin made up his mind to question him about it. "You must have used some sort of weapon when you were robbing all those pilgrims and merchants," Brin grinned as he watched Dob mop. "Yes, sedura," Dob replied humbly. "A bow." "Of course. You Bosmeri are supposed to be very handy with those," Brin thought a moment and then asked: "A bit of a marksman, were you?" Dob nodded humbly. "You will tutor my son Wodilic in archery," the master said after another moment's pause. Wodilic was twelve years of age and had been rather sadly spoiled by his mother, Brin's late wife. The boy was useless at swordplay, fearful of being cut. He embarrassed his father's pride, but the personality defect seemed ideally suited to the bow. Brin had his castellan purchase a finely wrought bow, several quivers of arrows, and ordered targets to be set up in the wildflower field next to the plantation house. In a few days time, the lessons began. For the first few days, the master watched Wodilic and Dob to be certain that the slave knew how to teach. He was pleased to see the boy learn the grips and the different stances. Business concerns, however, had to take precedence. Brin only had time to see to it that the lessons were continuing, but not how well they were progressing. It was a month's time before the issue was reexamined. Brin and his castellan were reviewing the plantation's earnings and expenses, and they had come to the area of miscellaneous household costs. "You might also check to see how many targets in the field need to be repaired." "I have already anticipated that, sedura," said the castellan. "They are in pristine condition." "How is that possible?" Brin shook his head. "I've seen targets fall apart after only a few good shots. There shouldn't be anything left after a month's worth of lessons." "There are no holes of any kind in the targets, sedura. See for yourself." As it happened at that hour, the marksmanship lesson was underway. Brin walked across the field, watching Dob guide Wodilic's arm as the boy took aim at the sky. The arrow flew up into an arc, over the top of the target, burying itself in the ground. Brin examined the target and found it to be, as his castellan said, in pristine condition. No arrow had touched it. "Master Wodilic, you must pull your right arm down further," Dob was saying. "And the follow-through is essential if you expect your arrow to gain any height." "Height?" Brin snarled. "What about accuracy? Unless he's been secretly racking up a high kill ratio on birds, you haven't taught my son a thing about marksmanship." Dob bowed humbly. "Sedura, first Master Wodilic must become comfortable with the weapon before he need worry about accuracy. In Valenwood, we learn by watching the bolt arc at different levels, in different winds, before we try very hard to strike targets." Brin's face turned purple with fury: "I'm not a fool! I should have known not to trust a slave with my boy's education!" The master grabbed Dob and shoved him toward the plantation house. Dob, head down, began the humble, shuffling walk he had learned in his domestic duties. Wodilic, tears streaming down his face, tried to follow. "You stay and practice!" roared his father. "Try aiming at the target itself, not at the sky! You are not coming back into the house until there is one hole in that damned bullseye!" The boy tearfully returned to practice, while Brin brought Dob into the courtyard and called for his whip. Dob suddenly broke away and scrambled to hide between some barrels in the center of the yard. "Take your punishment, slave! I should have never shown you mercy the day I bought you!" Brin bellowed, bringing the whip down on Dob's exposed back again and again. "I have to toughen you up! There'll be no more soft jobs as tutor and valet in your future!" Wodilic's plaintive yell drifted in from the meadow: "I can't! Father, I can't hit it!" "Master Wodilic!" Dob cried back as loud as he could, his voice shaking with pain. "Keep your left arm straight and aim slightly east! The wind has changed!" "Stop confusing my son!" Brin screamed. "You'll be in the saltrice fields if I don't beat you to death first! Like you deserve!" "Dob!" the boy wailed, far away. "I still can't hit it!" "Master Wodilic! Take four steps back, aim east, and don't be afraid of the height!" Dob tore away from the barrels, hiding under a cart near the wall. Brin pursued him, raining down blows. The boy's arrow sailed high over the target and kept climbing, reaching a pinnacle at the edge of the plantation house before coming down in a magnificent arc. Brin tasted the blood before he realized he'd been hit. Gingerly, he raised his hands and felt the arrowhead protruding out of the back of his neck. He looked at Dob crouching under the wagon, and thought he saw a thin smile cross the slave's lips. Just for an instant before he died, Brin saw the face of the rogue highwayman on Dob. "Bullseye, Master Wodilic!" Dob crowed.

凯尔莫瑞尔·布林是个很有办法的人。每次买下奴隶的当天，布林都会在庭院持鞭将之狠抽一到三个小时，时长取决于奴隶个人意志独立的程度。他和手下所用的鞭子都是为缠结的浸湿布条，很容易抽打出血，但极少致残。让他颇为满意及自豪的是，如此杀过威风的奴隶极少需要再度鞭笞。第一天的惨痛经历，以及往后看到每个后进奴隶的同情同景，都足以令所有奴隶铭记一生。 当布林首次购得波斯莫奴隶时，他命手下只鞭打一小时即可。这家伙被他命名为达伯。他绝大多数的奴隶是阿尔贡、卡吉特和兽人，相比之下这木精灵的体态要羸弱得多，显然不宜下矿或耕田，但看起来还是可以做家务的。 达伯办事安静，质量也不错。布林虽然偶尔断其饭食来纠正他，但也仅到此为止，从不需要更严厉的责罚。布林的种植园每有客人到来，都会因布林家举止优雅且颇具异国风情的奴仆而留下深刻的印象。 “喂，你，”珍妮塔·伊洛克说着，她是因多瑞尔的一个次要贵族。而达伯正为她端呈一杯酒，“你生来就是奴隶吗？” “不，塞杜拉，”达伯躬身答，“我以前专门在路上抢劫您这样的贵妇人。” 此言博得满堂欢笑。但凯尔莫瑞尔·布林之后咨询卖给他达伯的奴隶贩子，发现这故事所言非虚。这波斯莫在被罚为奴之前，真的是个拦路贼，只是没有什么恶名罢了。达伯平日低眉顺眼，这样安静的人居然是罪犯，这可真是出人意料。布林打定主意就此盘问他。 “你当年打劫过路的朝圣者和商人时，一定是拿着什么武器的吧。”布林看着达伯拖地时笑笑问。 “是，塞杜拉，”达伯谦卑答，“我是用弓箭的。” “肯定了，你们波斯莫都懂那个，”布林思酌良久又问，“那你是个神射手了，是不是？” 达伯恭敬地点头。 “你来教授我儿沃迪历克学习箭术。”奴隶主深思熟虑后说。沃迪历克当时十二岁，悲哀的是，这孩子被他母亲，也就是布林的亡妻给宠坏了。沃迪历克不擅长剑术，因为他害怕受伤，让他身为父亲的自豪感深为难堪。但这种性格缺陷貌似很适合当个射手。布林命手下买了一副做工精良的弓，还有几支箭筒，又令人在庄园旁的野花地里安放靶子。数日后，课程开始了。 起初数日，布林观察着沃迪历克和达伯，以确认这个奴隶是否懂得如何教学。他欣慰地看着男孩学会了弓的握持方法和各种射姿。然而他的生意也很紧要，所以布林的时间也只够确认他们的课是否在继续进行，但进展如何则无暇了解。 足足一个月过去了，这事才被重新审视。布林和手下正审查种植园的收支，他们查着查着对到家用杂费一项。 “你也给我查查，看靶场那边有多少靶子需要修复。” “我早知您会提及此事，塞杜拉。”手下说，“它们仍完好如新。” “怎么可能？”布林摇头，“我曾见过射手仅仅几发好箭命中，立靶就得烂了。何况连着上了一个月课，早该渣也不剩了。” “那堆靶子上连个眼儿都看不到，塞杜拉。您大可亲自瞧瞧。” 刚好彼时正在上箭术课。布林走过田野，看着达伯牵引沃迪历克的手臂，让男孩瞄准天空。箭矢飞出弧形划过空中，飞越立靶顶部深埋入地。布林把立靶挨个检查了一遍，发现手下所言不虚，个个完好如新，没有箭簇接触过它们。 “沃迪历克少爷，您的右手应再压低些。”达伯对沃迪历克说，“若想您的箭矢飞得足够高，少许后摇绝对必要。” “足够高？”布林咆哮，“那精准度呢？除非他背地里射下来的鸟越来越多，要不然你小子压根没教过我儿子射箭。” 达伯谦逊躬身：“塞杜拉，沃迪历克少爷须先熟悉武器的使用，其后再考虑精准度。在我们威伦森林，努力练习射中目标前，我们都需要先观察熟记各种高度和风向之下发出箭矢的弧线有何差异。” 布林脸色气得发紫：“老子不傻！我早该知道不能把孩子的教育托付给一个奴隶！” 奴隶主抓起达伯并把他狠狠地往种植园里推去。达伯仍谦卑地低头蹒跚而行，一如他在过去家事劳动时学会那般。沃迪历克泪流满面地也想一块去。 “你留下，练箭！”他父亲吼道，“给我瞄着靶子，而不是天空！除非你在该死的靶子上射出个洞来，不然你别想进家门！” 男孩只好边哭边折回练习。布林拉着达伯进了庭院，高吼着命人取鞭子来。达伯骤然挣脱，艰难地爬着躲进庭院中心摆着的几个桶中间。 “给老子乖乖受罚，奴才！买你那天就不该对你心慈手软！”布林怒咆着一下下狠鞭达伯露在桶堆外的后背，“我得敲打敲打你！你打后就别想再干家教和家政这样的肥差了！” 沃迪历克的悲呼从荒原传来：“我做不到！爸，我射不中！” “沃迪历克少爷！”达伯用尽全力高声回应，他的嗓音因剧痛颤抖，“保持您的左臂平直并稍偏向东瞄！风向变了！” “别再蛊惑我儿子了！”布林尖啸，“如果不打死你，你就给我滚去盐水稻田里去！你就配干这个！” “达伯！”沃迪历克的哀号遥遥传来，“我还是射不中！” “沃迪历克少爷！退四步并瞄向东侧，别怕射得高！”达伯拨开桶堆躲进墙边的马车底。布林疯狂追赶，鞭若雨落。 男孩的箭矢高飞越靶，仍在爬升，在种植园房舍边升至顶点始落，划成华丽的巨弧。布林突然尝到血腥味，方才意识到自己被命中了。他战战兢兢地举起双手，摸到了箭头从脖子后面扎了进来。他看向躲在马车底的达伯，确信看到奴隶的嘴角掠过一丝微笑。死前的最后一瞬，布林在他脸上看出了那拦路贼的匪气。 “正中目标了，沃迪历克少爷！”达伯欢呼道。

The Hope of the Redoran by Turiul Nirith

[pagebreak]

ne of the few magical arts the Psijics of Artaeum have kept to themselves, away from the common spells and schools of the Mages Guild, is the gift of divination. Despite this, or perhaps because of it, omens and prophesies abound in Tamriel, some of substance, others of pure folly, and still others so ambiguous as to be unverifiable. There are still other prophesies kept secret, from the prophesies of Dro'Jizad in Elsweyr and the Nerevarine in Morrowind, to the Elder Scrolls themselves. The Nord nobility have a tradition of having omens read for their children. In general, these readings are of the obscure variety. One of my acquaintances told me that her parents were told, for example, that their daughter would have her life rescued by a snake, and so gave her the name Serpentkin in a special ceremony. And this young lady, Eria Valkor Serpentkin, was indeed saved by a snake many years later, when an assassin creeping on her stepped on a danswyrm viper. Occasionally, omens seem to be almost purposefully misleading, as if Boethiah had crafted them as traps. I recall one particularly. Many, many years ago, a male child was born into House Redoran. It was a very difficult birth, and the mother was delirious and near death by the time it was over. She chanted just as her son came into the world and she passed from it. Fortune has smiled this day not frowned My child will be mighty in mind and in arm He shall bring hope to House Redoran Neither spell nor blade shall hurt the man Nor illness nor poison cause any harm His blood shall never drop on the ground The boy, named Andas, was indeed extraordinary. He never was ill and never suffered so much as a scratch all through his childhood. He was also quite intelligent and strong, which, combined with his invulnerability, caused many to call him, after his mother's omen, the Hope of the Redoran. Of course, any one who is called the Hope of the Redoran will eventually develop some taint of impertinence, and it wasn't long before he had enemies. His worst enemy was his cousin Athyn, who had borne much abuse at the hands of Andas. Primary among the grudges was that Athyn had been sent to Rihad to complete his education at Andas's insistence. When Athyn returned from Hammerfell, it was because of the death of his father, who had also been a councilor of the House. Athyn was old enough to take his seat in the Council, but Andas claimed the seat as well, saying that his cousin had been gone too long from Morrowind and didn't understand politics as he did. The majority of the House agreed with Andas, wanting to see the Hope of Redoran rise quickly. Athyn exercised his right to combat his cousin for the seat. No one thought he had any chance of winning, of course, but the battle was scheduled to commence the following morn. Andas whored and dined and drank with the councilors that night, confident that his place in the House was secured and the hopeful new dawn of House Redoran was rising. Athyn retired to his castle with his friends, Andas's enemies, and his servants he had brought from Hammerfell. Athyn and his friends were discussing the duel morosely when one of his old teachers, a warrior called Shardie, came into the hall. She had grown quite proud of her student over the years in Hammerfell, proud enough to accompany him across the Empire to his family's lands, and wanted to know why they had so little confidence in his odds in the battle. They explained to her Andas's uncommon blessings and the nature of his mother's omen. "If he can't be harmed by disease, poison, magicka, and his blood can never be spilled, what hope have I of ever besting him?" cried Athyn. "Have you remembered nothing I taught you?" replied Shardie. "Is there no weapon you can think of that will slay without blood? Are swords and spears and arrows the only items in your arsenal?" Athyn quickly realized the weapon Shardie was speaking of, but it seemed absurd. Not only absurd, but pathetic and primitive. Still, it was the only hope he had. All that night, Shardie trained him in the art and techniques, showing him the various swings and stances her people had developed in Albion-Gora; counter-attacks, feints, and blocks imported from Yokuda; the classic one and two-handed grips for the most ancient weapon in history. The cousins faced one another the next morning, and never have two combatants looked so unevenly matched. Andas's entrance brought a great cheer, for not only was he much beloved as the Hope of the Redoran, but as his victory was a foregone conclusion, most wanted to be in good standing with him. His shining mail and blade drew admiration and awe. By contrast, Athyn drew a gasp of surprise and only a smattering of polite applause. He appeared costumed and armed like a barbarian. As Shardie had suggested, Athyn allowed Andas to attack first. The Hope of the Redoran was eager to finish the battle and take the power he deserved quickly. The blade pushed by Andas's mighty arm slashed across Athyn's chest, but shallowly, and before it could be counterswung, Athyn knocked it back with his own weapon. When Athyn attacked and wounded Andas, the Hope of the Redoran was so surprised by being hurt for the first time in his life, he dropped his sword. The less said about the end of the battle, the better. Suffice it to say that Athyn, wielding a simple club, battered Andas to death without spilling a drop of blood. Athyn took his father's seat as councilor, and it was then said that the hope in the omen referred to Athyn, not Andas. After all, had Andas not tried to take the councilor seat away from his cousin, Athyn, being not very ambitious, might have never tried to get it. It can certainly be argued that way, I suppose.

阿塔姆那群赛伊克们有少数秘藏不宣、与法师公会的通常法术学派迥异的魔法技艺，其中之一，就是占卜术。虽说如此，或者说正因如此，泰姆瑞尔的征兆和预言才会这般比比皆是，有些是指向实质的，而有些纯属胡说八道，还有些含糊其辞到无可证实的程度。但仍有一类预言是保密的，艾斯维尔的德罗'吉扎德预言、晨风的尼瑞瓦因预言，乃至上古卷轴本身。 诺德贵族有项古老的传统：为他们的后代判读征兆。一般来说，该类判读都是晦涩模糊的。我的某位熟人曾和我说过，就如她的父母被告知，他们的女儿会被一尾蛇挽救生命，他们就依此举行某种特殊仪式，为她取了个叫“蛇亲”的名字。而这位年轻的“蛇亲”爱莉雅·沃客女士，多年后的确被一尾蛇所救——当一名刺客蹑手蹑脚逼近她时意外踩到了一尾丹斯温蝰蛇。 不过有时，征兆似乎完全是在故意误导，就好像是波耶西亚将它们设做陷阱。有一件我记忆犹新。在很多很多年以前，一名男婴诞生于瑞多然家族。分娩异常艰难，那位母亲在生产结束后已然神志不清，濒临死亡了。她在儿子降临世间而自己即将离世时反复吟唱这段预言： 幸运女神今日不蹙反笑 吾儿日后智明勇武俱妙 他为瑞多然氏送来希望 那奥术与刀剑皆不可创 那灾病与鸩毒皆不可伤 此子鲜血永不洒在地上 那名唤安达斯的男孩确是异乎寻常。他的整段孩提时光无病无伤，甚至连小小的擦伤都没有。他也非常聪慧壮硕，加上他表现出的刀枪不入，导致很多人都按着他母亲预兆的内容，称他为“瑞多然家的希望”。不过嘛，不管谁被别人天天称作“瑞多然家的希望”，最后都会染上一些名为“无礼”的污点，没用多久就招来了敌视。 他最大的敌人就是曾在他口中饱受谩骂的堂兄弟阿辛恩。他们间结下最大的梁子，就是当年在安达斯的极力主张下，阿辛恩被送遣到瑞哈德留学。待阿辛恩自落锤省归来后，由于他的过世的父亲曾是家族议会的议员，而阿辛恩的年龄已达到占据一席之地的条件，所以现在他有权继承它。但安达斯也宣称应该领有一席，他声称他的堂兄弟已远离晨风多年，对时下政局的了解不及他。而家族绝大多数成员也站在安达斯这边，期待看到“瑞多然家的希望”更快崛起。 阿辛恩行使了他的权利：为了席位和堂兄弟展开一场决斗。当然，没人觉得他有机会获胜，但决斗还是被安排在次日清晨开始。当夜安达斯与议员们嫖娼吃喝，确信他在家族议会中的地位已然稳固，瑞多然家的新曙光正在冉冉升起。而阿辛恩则和他的朋友、安达斯的敌对派还有从落锤省带回的随从一同回到了他的城堡。 正当阿辛恩和他的朋友们正为次日决斗闷闷不乐地讨论时，他旧日的一位老师，一位名叫莎蒂的战士走进了大厅。在落锤省度过的这些年里，她深深地为她这名出色的学徒感到骄傲，乃至肯陪伴阿辛恩横跨帝国抵达他的家乡。她想知道为何众人如此低估他这场比试中的胜算。他们便向她解释了安达斯那异乎寻常的赐福及其母亲所述的预兆内容。 　　 “如果他不会被灾病、毒药、魔法伤到，还永不流血，我还有什么战胜他的希望啊？”阿辛恩喊着。 　　 “你已将我往日所授尽数忘却了吗？”莎蒂答，“你就想不到一类杀人不见血的武器么？难不成你的军械库里只有枪剑弓吗？” 　　 阿辛恩很快意识到莎蒂说的武器是什么，可那貌似很荒谬。不只是荒谬，还悲哀又原始。可这是他仅存的希望了。当晚整夜，莎蒂一直在训练他的战斗技巧，对他展示了她的族人在阿尔比昂-戈拉发展出来的各种挥舞、站立的姿势；发源自尤库达大陆的反击、佯袭和格挡术；还有这历史上最古老武器的单手、双手握法。 　　 次日清晨，堂亲两人直面彼此，再没有哪对斗士的入场氛围差异比他们更一边倒了。安达斯侧入口传来阵阵欢呼，这不仅是因为这位“瑞多然家的希望”人人敬畏，还因为谁都知道这场决斗已成定局，因此绝大多数人都想要和他搞好关系。他铮亮闪烁的铠甲和剑刃引得无数钦佩和敬畏。相较之下，阿辛恩只博得惊讶的倒抽冷气和零散的礼节性掌声。他打扮得就像个武装起来的野蛮人。 如莎蒂忠告那样，阿辛恩请安达斯先攻。“瑞多然家的希望”渴望直接结束战斗，尽快取得他当之无愧的权力。安达斯那孔武有力的壮臂挥舞起剑刃划过阿辛恩的胸口，好在伤势轻微，而在剑刃回攻前，阿辛恩挥起自己的武器将之击回。在阿辛恩展开攻势并击伤安达斯时，“瑞多然家的希望”因生平首度负伤而大惊失色，他的武器摔落在地。 此战结果不必多说。就是阿辛恩挥舞着一根朴素的棍棒，将安达斯活活打死却滴血不流。 此后，阿辛恩承袭了他父亲的议员之席。随即便有人说，其实预兆所述的“希望”指的是阿辛恩而非安达斯。说到底，要是安达斯没有企图夺走他堂亲议员席位，而阿辛恩的雄心也没那么大，也不会尝试夺回它的话，当然是可以这么说的。反正我是这么想的。

"It is time for you to leave your apprenticeship here," said the Great Sage to his students, Taksim and Vonguldak. "So soon?" cried Vonguldak, for it had been but a few years since the training began. "Are we such poor pupils?" "We have learned much for you, master, but you have no more to teach us?" Taksim asked. "You have told us so many tales of great enchanters of the past. Can't we continue to learn until we have reached some level of their power?" "I have one last story for you," smiled the Great Sage. Many thousands of years ago, long before the Cyrodilic Dynasty of Reman and even longer before the Septim Dynasty ruled Tamriel, and before there was a Mages Guild, and when the land called Morrowind was known as Resdayn, and the land of Elsweyr was called Anequina and Pellitine, and the only law of the land was the cruel ways of the Alessian Doctrines of Marukh, there lived a hermetic enchanter named Dalak who had two apprentices, Uthrac and Loreth. Uthrac and Loreth were remarkable students, both equally assiduous in their learning, the pride of their Master. Both excelled at the arts of the cauldron, mirror castings, the infusion of spiritas into mundus, and the weaving of air and fire. Dalak was very fond of his boys, and they of him. On a springtide morn, Dalak received a message from another enchanter named Peothil, who lived deep in the forests of the Colovian heartland. You must remember that in the dark days of the First Era, mages were solitary practitioners with the only organized consortium being the Psijics of Artaeum. Away from that island, mages seldom saw one another and even more rarely corresponded. Thus, when Dalak received Peothil's letter, he gave it his great attention. Peothil was greatly aged, and he had found the peace of his isolation threatened by the Alessian Reform. He feared for his life, knowing that the fanatical priests and their warriors were close at hand. Dalak brought his students to him. "It will be an arduous and perilous journey to the Colovian Estates, one that I would fear partaking even in my youth," Dalak said. "My heart trembles to send you two forth to Peothil's cave, but I know that he is a great and benevolent enchanter, and his light must continue to burn in the heart of the continent if we are to survive these dark nights." Uthrac and Loreth pled with their teacher not to order them to go to Peothil. It was not the priests and warriors of the Alessian Reform they feared, but they knew their Master was aged and infirm, and could not protect himself if the Reform moved further westward. Finally, he relented and allowed that one would stay with him, and the other would journey forth to the Colovian Estates. He would let them decide which of them would go. The lads debated and discussed, fought and compromised, and at last elected to let fate make the choice. They threw lots, and Loreth came up short. He left early the next morning, miserable and filled with fear. For a month and a day, he tramped through the forests into the midst of the Colovian Estates. Through some planning, some skill, and much assistance for sympathetic peasants, he managed to avoid the ever-tightening circle of the Alessian Reform by crossing through unclaimed mountain passes and hidden bogs. When at last he found the dark caverns where Dalak had told him to search for Peothil, it was still many hours before he could find the enchanter's lair. No one appeared to be there. Loreth searched through the laboratory of ancient tomes, cauldrons and crystalline flutes, herbs kept alive by the glow of mystic circles, strange liquids and gasses caught in transparent membranes. At last, he found Peothil, or so he presumed. The desiccated shell on the floor of the study, clutching tools of enchantment, scarcely seemed human. Loreth decided that he could do nothing further for the mage, and began at once the journey back to his true master Dalak and his friend Uthrac. The armies of the Reform had moved quickly since he passed. After more than one close near encounter, the young enchanter realized that he was trapped on all sides. The only retreat that was possible was back in the caves of Peothil. The first thing to be done, Loreth saw, was to find a means to keep the army from finding the laboratory. That, he found, was what Peothil himself had been trying to do, but by a simple error even an apprentice enchanter could recognize, he had only succeeded in destroying himself. Loreth was able to take what he had learned from Dalak and apply it to Peothil's enchantments, quite successfully. The laboratory was never found or even detected by the Reform. Much time passed. In the 480th year of the First Era, the great Aiden Direnni won many battles against the Alessian horde, and many passages and routes that had once been closed were now open. Loreth, now no longer young, was able to return to Dalak. When at last he found his way to his Master's old hovel, he saw candles of mourning lit in all the trees surrounding. Even before he knocked on the door and met his old fellow student Uthrac, Loreth knew that Dalak had died. "It was only a few months ago," said Uthrac, after embracing his friend. "He talked of you every day of every year you were away. Somehow he knew that you had not preceded him to the world beyond. He told me that you would come back." The gray-haired men sat before the fire and reminisced of the old days. The sad truth was that they both discovered how different they had become. Uthrac spoke of carrying on the Master's work, while Loreth described his new discoveries. They left one another that day, each shaking his head, destined to never see one another again. In the years ahead, before they left the mortal world to join their great teacher Dalak, they both achieved their desires. Uthrac went on to become respected if minor enchanter in the service of Clan Direnni. Loreth took the skills he had learned on his own, and used them to fashion the Balac-thurm, the Staff of Chaos. My boys, the lesson is you have to learn from a teacher to avoid those small but essential errors that claimed the life of such self-taught enchanters as Peothil. And yet, the only way to become truly great is to try all the possibilities on your own.

“该是时候让你二人从学徒生涯毕业了，”大贤者向他的两名学徒，塔克西姆和冯高达克言道。 “这么快？”冯高达克喊着，因为训练才刚刚开始几年。“我们就这么不堪造就吗？” “大师，我们从您那里学到了很多东西，但您没有别的可以传授我们了吗？”塔克西姆问道，“您曾为我等讲述过去许多伟大附魔师的故事。难道我们不能学习到他们那种境界吗？” “我有最后一个故事要讲给你们。”大贤者笑道。 　　 数千年前，远在雷曼的希罗帝尔王朝建立以前，自然也远在一统泰姆瑞尔的塞普汀王朝以前，那时还没有法师公会，晨风还被叫做“瑞斯戴恩”，艾斯维尔还叫做“安内奎那”和“佩里庭”，而大地上仅有的法律仍是马鲁克所订阿莱西亚教义的残酷法则，当时生活着一位名唤达拉克的附魔师隐士。他有两个学徒，乌斯拉克和洛瑞斯。 乌斯拉克和洛瑞斯都很优秀，二人同等刻苦勤勉，都是老师的骄傲。二人精通药釜之术、镜影映射、召灵至世和交风布火。达拉克极为爱惜他的弟子，而他们待他亦如是。 一个春日清晨，达拉克收得另一位深居于科洛文腹地林间深处的、名唤佩奥蒂尔的附魔师所传来的讯息。要知道，在那第一纪元的黑暗时代里，法师们都是孑然一身的专业修艺者，唯一具组织性的结社便是阿塔姆的赛伊克。在那岛屿之外，法师们极少碰面，甚至罕有书信往来。由是，当达拉克收得佩奥蒂尔来函时，他对此极度重视。 佩奥蒂尔年事已高，他发现自己与世隔绝的清静生活正受阿莱西亚改革派所威胁。他忧心自家性命，深知那些狂信的祭司及其战士们已近在咫尺。达拉克遂将他的学生唤至面前。 “前往科洛文自治领将是一趟艰难险峻之旅，就是我年轻时也不敢轻涉，”达拉克道，“让你们俩去佩奥蒂尔的洞穴，我也感觉心颤，但我知晓他是一位伟大而仁慈的附魔师，若我等在这黑暗长夜中生还，他的光辉必将在大陆腹地继续熊熊燃烧。” 乌斯拉克和洛瑞斯央求老师莫要命令他们去找佩奥蒂尔。他们并非畏惧阿莱西亚改革派的祭司和战士们，而是他们心知若改革派进一步西进，年高体弱的老师无力自保。最终，他妥协并准许其中一人驻留相伴，而另一人则踏上前往科洛文自治领的旅途。他将让他们自行决定谁将动身。 两个小伙子经历一番争辩和讨论、比拼和妥协后，最终选择让命运作出抉择。他们掷出许多签，而洛瑞斯抽得短签。次日大清早，他便怀着哀戚和满心恐惧离去。 一月又一日的行程间，他漫步穿越森林进入科洛文自治领中心。通过一些筹划、各般技巧又得到心怀同情的农夫们充分援助之下，他穿行于无人问津的山脉隘口和隐秘幽深的沼泽，设法躲开阿莱西亚改革派日益缩紧包围圈。当他终于寻获达拉克告知他要搜索的佩奥蒂尔所居昏暗洞穴时，他又花了数小时方才找到附魔师的隐居处。 里面似乎空无一人。洛瑞斯在实验室内翻查着古老巨著、坩埚和水晶长笛、因神秘圆环光照而保持生机的药草、承载怪异液体和气体的透明膜体。最终，他找到了佩奥蒂尔，或者说，他推断应是找到了佩奥蒂尔。书房地板上有具干尸，紧握着附魔工具组，几近不成人形。 洛瑞斯知道他无法再为这位附魔师做任何事了，于是立即启程返回他真正的老师达拉克和好友乌斯拉克处。改革派大军自他离开后便迅速行动。经过不止一次的近距离接触后，年轻的附魔师意识到他已陷于四面受敌之境。唯一的退路便是返回佩奥蒂尔的洞穴之中。 洛瑞斯发现，首先要做的便是探索出一种能让敌军无法发现实验室的方法。他随后发现，佩奥蒂尔本人也曾尝试过，但却出于一处甚至连学徒都能意识到的简单错误，只让他成功毁灭了自己。洛瑞斯成功将他自达拉克处习得的知识应用于佩奥蒂尔的附魔之中。实验室从未被改革派发现，甚至未曾察觉分毫。 时光荏苒。于第一纪元480年，伟大的艾登·迪伦尼在对抗阿莱西亚部众的多次战斗中取胜，许多曾被封闭堵塞的道路和航线再度开通。已不复年轻的洛瑞斯总算能返回达拉克之处。 当他终于寻得那通往大师老旧茅舍的道路时，他只见其周围所有树木皆燃满哀悼之烛。甚至在他敲响门与老同窗乌斯拉克重逢前，洛瑞斯便已知晓达拉克的身故。 “就是几个月前的事，”拥抱老友后的乌斯拉克道，“你离去的每年每天，他都在谈论你。不知何故，他知晓你并未先他一步而去。他告诉我，你一定会回来。” 两名头发花白的老人坐在炉火前追忆往昔时光。可悲的是，他们都发现对方已然变化得如此不同。乌斯拉克说将再续老师的工作，而洛瑞斯则描述起他的新发现。那日他们皆摇着头彼此各自踏上歧路，注定从此再无相见。 在未来岁月里，在他们舍弃尘世追随他们伟大的先师达拉克而去前，他们都达成了自己的愿望。乌斯拉克后来选择为迪伦尼家族效劳，成了受人尊敬的附魔师。而洛瑞斯以他自身习得的技能制造了巴拉克-图姆，“混沌之杖”。 我的孩子们，在这一课中你等要从老师处习得的，便是要规避那些细微却紧要的错误，这些错误足可夺去如佩奥蒂尔那般无师自通的附魔师的性命。然而，成就真正伟大业绩的唯一方法，便是亲身尝试所有可能性。

was in the Rat and the Pot, a foreigner cornerclub in Ald'ruhn, talking to my fellow Rats when I first saw the woman. Now, Breton women are fairly common in the Rat and the Pot. As a breed, they seem inclined to wander far from their perches in High Rock. Old Breton women, however, are not so migratory, and the wizened old biddy drew attention to herself, wandering about the room, talking to everyone. Nimloth and Oediad were at their usual places, drinking their usual stuff. Oediad was showing off a prize he had picked up in some illicit manner -- a colossal diamond, large as a baby's hand, and clear as spring water. I was admiring it when I heard the creaking of old bones behind me. "Good day to you, friends," said the old woman. "My name is Abelle Chriditte, and I am in need of financial assistance to facilitate my transportation to Ald Redaynia." "You'll want to see the Temple for charity," said Nimloth curtly. "I am not looking for charity," said Abelle. "I'm looking to barter services." "Don't make me sick, old woman," laughed Oediad. "Did you say your name was Abelle Chriditte?" I asked, "Are you related to Abelle Chriditte, the High Rock alchemist?" "Closely related," she said, with a cackle. "We are the same person. Perhaps I could prepare you a potion in exchange for gold? I noticed that you have in your possession a very fine diamond. The magical qualities of diamonds are boundless." "Sorry, old woman, I ain't giving it up for magic. It was trouble enough stealing this one," said Oediad. "I've got a fence who'll trade it for gold." "But your fence will demand a certain percentage, will he not? What if I could give you a potion of invisibility in exchange? In return for that diamond, you could have the means to steal many more. A very fair exchange of services, I would say." "It would be, but I have no gold to give you," said Oediad. "I'll take what remains of the diamond after I've made the potion," said Abelle. "If you took it to the Mages Guild, you'd have to supply all the other ingredients and pay for it as well. But I learned my craft in the wild, where no Potion-makers existed to dissolve diamonds into dust. When you must do it all by hand, by simple skill, you are blessed with remnants those fool potion-makers at the Guild simply swallow up." "That sounds all very nice," said Nimloth, "But how do we know your potion is going to work? If you make one potion, take the rest of Oediad's diamond, and leave, we won't know until you've gone whether the potion works or not." "Ah, trust is so rare these days," sighed Abelle. "I suppose I could make two potions for you, and there'd still be a little bit of the diamond left for me. Not a lot, but perhaps enough to get me to Ald Redaynia. Then you could try the first potion right here and now, and see if you're satisfied or not." "But," I interjected. "You could make one potion that works and one that doesn't, and take more of the diamond. She could even give you a slow-acting poison, and by the time she got to Ald Redaynia, you'd be dead." "Bleedin' Kynareth, you Dunmer are suspicious! I will hardly have any diamond left, but I could make two potions of two doses each, so you can satisfy yourself that the potion works and has no negative effects. If you still don't trust me, come along with me to my table and witness my craft if you'd like." So it was decided that I would accompany Abelle back to her table where she had all her traveling bags full of herbs and minerals, to make certain that she was not making two different potions. It took nearly an hour of preparation, but she kindly allowed me to finish her half-filled flagon of wine while I watched her work. Splintering the diamond and powdering the pieces required the bulk of the time; over and over again, she waved her gnarled hands over the gem, intoning ancient enchantments, breaking the facets of the stone into smaller and smaller pieces. Separately she made pastes of minced bittergreen, crushed red bulbs of dell'arco spae, and driblets of ciciliani oil. I finished the wine. "Old woman," I finally said with a sigh. "How much longer is this going to take? I'm getting tired of watching you work." "The Mages Guild has fooled the populace into thinking alchemy is a science," she said. "But if you're tired, rest your eyes." My eyes closed, seemingly of their own volition. But there had been something in that wine. Something that made me do what she asked. "I think I'll make up the potion as cakes. It's much more potent that way. Now, tell me, young man, what will your friends do once I give them the potion?" "Mug you in the street afterwards to retrieve the rest of the diamond," I said simply. I didn't want to tell the truth, but there it was. "I thought so, but I wanted to be certain. You may open your eyes now." I opened my eyes. Abelle had made a small presentation on a wooden platter: two small cakes and a silver cutting knife. "Pick up the cakes and bring them to the table," said Abelle. "And don't say anything, except to agree with whatever I say." I did as I was told. It was a curious sensation. I didn't really mind being her puppet. Of course, in retrospect, I resent it, but it seemed perfectly natural at the time to obey without question. Abelle handed the cakes to Oediad and I dutifully verified that both cakes were made the same way. She suggested that he cut one of the cakes in half, and she would take one piece and he'd take the other, just so he would know that they worked and weren't poisoned. Oediad thought it was a good idea, and used Abelle's knife to cut the cake. Abelle took the piece on the left and popped into her mouth. Oediad took the piece on the right and swallowed it more cautiously. Abelle and all the bags she was carrying vanished from sight almost instantly. Nothing happened to Oediad. "Why did it work for the witch and not for me?" cried Oediad. "Because the diamond dust was only on the left-hand side of the blade," said the old alchemist through me. I felt her control lessening as the distance grew and she hurried invisibly down the dark Ald'ruhn street away from the Rat and the Pot. We never found Abelle Chriditte or the diamond. Whether she completed her pilgrimage to Ald Redaynia is anyone's guess. The cakes had no effect, except to give Oediad a bad case of droops that lasted for nearly a week.

当初头一回见着这女人那会，我正在奥德'鲁恩一家外地人汇聚的街角吧“鼠与罐”里头跟我的耗子老友们聊天。如今，布莱顿女人在鼠与罐里相当常见。他们这混血种族似乎有行脚四方而远离他们在高岩里栖息地的倾向，然而布莱顿老太太可不常外出，那个干瘪的老太婆在屋子里走来走去，和每个人说话，引起了大家的注意。 尼姆罗斯和奥迪亚德待在他们的老地方灌着平日里的老玩意儿，奥迪亚德正炫耀他那凭某些非法手段搞到的战利品——一枚硕大的钻石，大得跟婴儿小手似的，跟泉水一样清澈。我正羡慕着呢，就听到我后头有把老骨头嘎吱嘎吱响。 “你们好啊，朋友们。”老妪说，“我名叫阿贝尔·克利蒂特，需要些经济援助好动身前往奥德·瑞达尼亚。” “去搞善堂的神殿看看吧。”尼姆罗斯随口敷衍道。 “我不是寻求施舍，”阿贝尔道，“只是想用服务来交换。” “别恶心人，老太婆。”奥迪亚德笑道。 “你说你叫阿贝尔·克利蒂特？”我问道，“你跟高岩炼金术师阿贝尔·克利蒂特什么关系？” 　 “很有关系，”她嘎嘎笑着，“我们就是同一个人。或许我可以为阁下调制一服药水来换钱？我留意到您有一枚很不错的钻石。而钻石的魔法特性可谓无穷无尽。” “对不住啊老太婆，我可不会为了什么魔法放弃它。光是偷到手就已经够麻烦了，”奥迪亚德道，“我早找好能把它变现的销赃人了。” “但阁下的销赃人也要分上一杯羹，不是吗？倘若我予您一剂隐形药水作交换呢？只需付出那颗钻石，阁下还可以偷到更多钻石。要我说，这可真是一次非常公平的交易服务啊。” “这倒是，不过我可没钱付你。”奥迪亚德道。 “调配好药水后，我将会取走钻石的剩余部分，”阿贝尔道，“若阁下将之交予法师公会，则须提供其他原料并支付费用。但我是在外面习得这一手技艺，荒郊野岭可没有炼药师能把钻石溶解成粉末。当您必须仅凭简单技能来手工完成这一切时，您便能走运拿走剩余部分了，公会那群愚钝炼药师光会将它囫囵用个干净而已。” “那些啥听着都挺不错。”尼姆罗斯道，“可我们怎么知道你的药水管不管用？你要做了一瓶药水，拿走奥迪亚德剩下的钻石，然后离开，我们却只能在你走后才去验证药水的效果。” “啊，信任在如今居然这么罕见，”阿贝尔嗟叹道，“依我看，可为阁下调配两服药水，这样我还能得到丁点钻石。虽然不多，但可能足以让我前往奥德·瑞达尼亚。届时阁下大可马上在此试饮第一服药水，且看您满意与否。” “不过，”我插上一嘴，“你能做个一份有用的和一份没用的，然后拿走更多钻石。说不定还能下个慢性毒，等你到了奥德·瑞达尼亚那会儿他就死透了。” “凯娜瑞丝在上啊，你们丹莫真是多疑！我都快剩不下什么钻石了，但我可做两剂药水，每剂两份，这样你们便可确信药水有效且无负面效果，如果仍不信任我，则若阁下愿意，大可一同往我桌旁，亲自见识我手艺。” 我决定陪同阿贝尔返回她的桌旁，她在那放的几个旅行包给草药和矿物塞得满满当当，我得确保她并未调配两种不同的药水。准备工作费去将近一小时，但她亲切地允许我在监视她工作时喝掉她那半瓶酒。切割钻石并将制成粉末需要大量时间；她反复在宝石上方挥舞着粗糙的双手，咏唱古老的魔法，将宝石研磨成越来越细的碎屑。她分别以绞碎的苦绿草、捣碎的赤色戴尔'阿可·斯帕鳞茎和微量希西连尼油制成糊状物。这时酒也被我喝完了。 “老太婆，”我最后叹着气道，“还需要多久？我这么看你干活已经看累了。” “法师公会愚弄大众，使之认为炼金术是一门科学。”她道，“但如果你真累了，就让眼睛休息一下吧。” 我的眼帘像有自己的意志一样闭合了。但那酒里有些什么东西不对劲。让我乖乖听她话办事。 “我会将药水制成蛋糕模样，如此效用更佳。现在，告诉我吧，年轻人，一旦我将药水交予你的好友们，他们将如何做？” “之后到大街上打劫你扒回剩下的钻石块儿。”我简单直白地说道。我并不想道出实言，但却就这么吐露了。 “我也是这么猜的，只是想再确认一下。现在可以睁开眼睛了。” 我睁开眼。阿贝尔已在木盘子上摆下两块小蛋糕及一柄银切刀。 “拿起蛋糕，送往他们那桌，”阿贝尔道，“除却赞同我所言以外，什么也不要说。” 我照她说的做了，这感觉太异样了。我并非当真介意成为她的傀儡。当然在回想起来时，我对此很反感，但在彼时，毫无疑问地顺从听命好像很自然。 阿贝尔把蛋糕递给奥迪亚德，而我也尽职尽责地证实两份蛋糕皆以同样的手法制成。她建议奥迪亚德将其中一份蛋糕切作两半，他们二人各食其一，由此他便可知晓它们有效且无毒。奥迪亚德认为这主意不错，便用阿贝尔的餐刀切开蛋糕。阿贝尔拿起左半块一下子塞进口中。奥迪亚德则更谨小慎微地拎起右半块咽下。 阿贝尔及其携带的所有包裹几乎立刻从视线中消隐无踪。奥迪亚德却毫无变化。 “怎么只对巫婆管用，而我啥变化没有？”奥迪亚德高号。 “只因钻石粉尘独在刀刃左侧罢了，”炼金术士老太婆用我的嘴说道。随着距离增远，我感觉到她的控制力越发弱化，她在隐形下匆匆沿着昏暗的奥德'鲁恩街道远离了鼠与罐。 我们再未找到阿贝尔·克利蒂特或是钻石。谁也说不准她是否完成了前往奥德·瑞达尼亚的朝圣之旅。蛋糕没什么别的效果，只是让奥迪亚德严重虚弱了差不多一周。

ith his god destroyed, Wulfharth finds it hard to keep his form. He staggers out of Red Mountain to the battlefield beyond. The world has shaken and all of Morrowind is made of fire. This Numidium is what he needs to conquer the world. It is his destiny to have it. He contacts the Underking and says he was right all along. They should kill the Tribunal, and they need to get together and make a plan. While the Underking was away he realized the true danger of Dagoth-Ur. Something must to be done. Still, there are conflicting reports of what really happened, and this is why there is such confusion over such questions as: Why does Alcaire claim to be the birthplace of Talos, while other sources say he came from Atmora? Why does Tiber Septim seem to be a different person after his first roaring conquests? Why does Tiber Septim betray his battlemage? In truth, he's a little nervous with all these provinces. Then an advisor shows up. "I was friends with your grandfather," the Underking says, "He sent me to help you run the Empire."

随着他的神被摧毁，武夫哈斯发现自己的形态难以维系。他晃荡荡走出红山，走向远方的战场。此时世界动摇，整个晨风一片火海。一阵强风刮来，将他的骨灰吹回了天际。 武夫哈斯回归，并被诺德人接纳。“灰风”伊斯米尔、凯娜的风暴。但因为洛克汗的缘故，他失去了自己民族的身份。他想让诺德人去杀死审判席。他掀起风暴，派遣族人，却被审判席的大军击溃。丹莫现在实在太强了。武夫哈斯只得回归幽域等待，并重新加强改造自己的身体。奇怪的是，阿玛莱西亚搅扰了他的休息，召唤出王与审判席一起对抗阿卡维尔恶魔，艾达’苏姆·迪尔-卡玛尔。武夫哈斯在打败艾达’苏姆之后便消失了，三百年都未曾现身。 而灰胡子的轰鸣吵醒了他。虽然帝国已经崩溃，但传言天命之子会重新复兴。这位新皇将击败精灵，统辖一个统一的泰姆瑞尔。武夫哈斯自认就是预言的化身。他径直到霍斯加修道院聆听灰胡子的话。结果伊斯米尔在灰胡子的话语中再次炸成了灰烬。他并非天命之子，高岩的一个年轻战士才是那个人。当灰风前往寻找预言之子时，他听到了灰胡子的告诫：武夫哈斯王，切勿忘记背叛的颜色。 此时西瑞驰地区正处于战乱。西希罗帝尔的佛克瑞斯王库勒凯恩的处境相当糟糕。为了统一科洛文，他需要保证北部边境的安全，但诺德人和瑞驰人已经在那里互相攻伐了几百年。他在古霍尔丹战役中选择与天际结盟。此时领军的正是“早髯”亚尔提。亚尔提来自高岩岛国阿尔凯瑞，后来成为了泰姆瑞尔的开国皇帝—泰伯·塞普汀。 亚尔提精于战术，他的科洛文部队和诺德的狂战士打破了瑞驰人的防线，迫使他们退守古霍尔丹。围攻似不可行，亚尔提缺乏来自佛克瑞斯的增援。是夜，一场风暴光顾亚尔提的军营，并与他在大帐中交谈。拂晓时分，亚尔提走到城门口，风暴在其头顶紧紧跟随。连箭矢也不能穿透他周围的风。他的吼声冲垮古霍尔丹的城墙，部下蜂拥而入。胜利后诺德人把亚尔提称为“塔洛斯”，或者“风暴王冠”。 库勒凯恩与他新晋的战无不胜之将，在不到一年时间就统一了希罗帝尔西部。无人能当亚尔提的风暴。幽域之主明白，亚尔提想要成为泰姆瑞尔的皇帝，就必须向东攻占腹地。亚尔提利用了他们二者。他需要库勒凯恩坐镇科洛文地区，因为外邦人不可信任。至于他需要伊斯米尔的原因更是显而易见。他们向东进发，战斗法师们军前投降，他们随即占领了都城。在库勒凯恩加冕前，亚尔提暗中谋杀了他及其亲信。而出于政治因素考量，此次暗杀被归咎于库勒凯恩在西瑞驰的敌人。首席战斗法师祖林·阿克图斯（不是幽域之主）随即加冕亚尔提为全希罗帝尔的新皇，泰伯·塞普汀。泰伯·塞普汀夺权后，发现统治整个希罗帝尔的起步工作极为耗费时间。于是派遣幽域之主主持帝国向天际和高岩方向的扩张。此时的伊斯米尔使得主持幕后工作的泰伯·塞普汀像是同时身在两地一般。这也就是此时的泰伯为何从塔洛斯征服故事中咆哮雷霆之人变成冷静沉着的政治家外交家的未解之谜的原因所在。（所谓的刺杀不过是捏造罢了，外界普遍以为是塔洛斯的喉咙被割断了。） 人类诸国此时悉数被征服，哪怕被视为难以成功的落锤也未例外。此时幽域之主希望主导一场彻底的入侵战争，创造和异国神亲自一战的机会，但泰伯·塞普汀却拒绝了他。因为他已经制定了更好的计划，一个似乎能让他的统治更加合法化的计划。希罗帝尔支持了落锤内战的输家，并被邀请入驻落锤。帝国终于可以把目光转向精灵了。 幽域之主继续向泰伯·塞普汀施压，要求他发兵晨风。皇帝却以此甚不明智。他听说过审判席的力量。幽域之主想要达成复仇，提醒泰伯，他注定要征服精灵，其中自然包括审判席。阿克图斯则谏言此时不宜如此，不过塞普汀也确实觊觎晨风的黑檀，他急需资金重建历经四百年战乱的希罗帝尔。幽域之主说，随着审判席之死，塞普汀有可能窃取他们的神力，并用来对付高精灵（他们是洛克汗最古老的敌人，甚至远在审判席之前就已结怨）。夏暮岛是泰伯·塞普汀心中最遥远的目标。即便如此，他仍然计划派遣祖林·阿克图斯去见艾琳诺王讲和。最后，黑檀的需求胜出了。帝国入侵晨风，审判席投降。可停战协议的条件不仅包括对审判席统治的不干涉政策，而且在幽域之主的眼里，这还意味着对他们宗教信仰的承认，伊斯米尔暴怒了。他彻底抛弃了帝国。这就是灰胡子们所说的背叛吧。至少他是这么想的。 没有了幽域之主的力量，征服全泰姆瑞尔的想法也随之搁置了。塞普汀却想，如此也好，而且我们也需要担心希罗帝尔和其他人类王国了。此时落锤已经开始爆发叛乱了。 尽管如此，努米迪安的碎片被逐步运来了。泰伯·塞普汀始终痴迷矮人，令祖林·阿克图斯研究这件伟大的器物。在此期间，阿克图斯偶然发现了一些关于红山之战的记载。他发现了制造努米迪安的目的和其真正的潜力。更重要是，他知道了幽域之主在大战中的地位。但祖林·阿克图斯的计划还未完成。他认为洛克汗之心可以为努米迪安供能。 当祖林·阿克图斯大谈自己的发现之时，泰伯·塞普汀终于明白了预言的内涵。他需要用努米迪安征服世界。这就是他的命运。他联系幽域之主，承认他始终是对的。他们应该杀掉审判席，请幽域之主回来商议计划，自从幽域之主离开，他才明白达格斯·乌尔的真正危险所在，必须要采取行动。不过他需要军队，所以请老朋友回来。陷阱就此设下。 幽域之主刚刚抵达就遭受了帝国卫队的伏击。当他与伏兵大战时，祖林·阿克图斯对他使用了灵魂石。幽域之主在咽下最后一口气前，把战斗法师的胸膛吼出一个大洞。最后，所有人都死了，幽域之主变成了灰烬，泰伯·塞普汀踱步而来拿走了灵魂石。当元老院抵达时，他宣布自己遭遇了第二次刺杀，这次是他最信任的战斗法师祖林·阿克图斯企图发动政变。他把那些战死的护卫称为英雄，尤其是其中一人甚至被炸成了灰烬……他警告此时希罗帝尔急需安内，但他已经找到了攘外之法。曼特拉。 努米迪安虽然没成为泰伯·塞普汀和锻莫期望中的神（毕竟幽域之主不是完整的洛克汗），但它确实开始运转了。就在它完成了对夏暮岛的作战后，新的威胁出现了—一个操纵漫天腐烂的不死巫师。他打散了努米迪安。不过努米迪安的最后一击也把他击飞，变成了天边的一个黑点。曼特拉掉进海里，似乎永远遗失了。 与此同时，泰伯·塞普汀加冕为泰姆瑞尔的开国皇帝。他活到108岁，是史上最长寿的人类。他早期统治的方方面面都被篡改了。然而，关于真相仍然众说纷纭，这就是为什么在阿尔凯瑞号称是塔洛斯的出生地时，其他消息则说他来自阿特莫拉？为什么泰伯·塞普汀在他第一次吼声征服之后似乎变了个人？为什么泰伯·塞普汀背叛了他的战斗法师？曼特拉究竟是战斗法师的心脏还是泰伯·塞普汀的心脏？ 泰伯·塞普汀的孙子佩拉吉奥斯一世继承了皇位。事实上，他确实对各省感到压力。随后一位顾问出现了。 幽域之主说道：“我是你祖父的朋友，他让我来帮你管理帝国。”

Spirit of Nirn

[pagebreak]

orkhan is the Spirit of Nirn, the god of all mortals. This does not mean all mortals necessarily like him or even know him. Most elves hate him, thinking creation as that act which sundered them from the spirit realm. Most Humans revere him, or aspects of him, as the herald of existence. The creation of the Mortal Plane, the Mundus, Nirn, is a source of mental anguish to all living things; all souls know deep down they came originally from somewhere else, and that Nirn is a cruel and crucial step to what comes next. What is this next? Some wish to return to the original state, the spirit realm, and that Lorkhan is the Demon that hinders their way; to them Nirn is a prison, an illusion to escape. Others think that Lorkhan created the world as the testing ground for transcendence; to them the spirit realm was already a prison, that true escape is now finally possible.

or three hundred years I have been a priestess of Azura, the Daedric Princess of Moonshadow, Mother of the Rose, and Queen of the Night Sky. When my grandmother died in an attempt to poison the heir of Firewatch, I re-examined my faith in the cult. My brother was a wizard of the cult of Boethiah-and from what he told me, the Dark Warrior was closer to my spirit than the treacherous Molag Bal. Boethiah is a Warrior Princess who acts more overtly than any other Daedroth. After years of skulking and scheming, it felt good to perform acts for a mistress which had direct, immediate consequences. Besides, I liked it that Boethiah was a Daedra of the Dark Elves. Our cult would summon her on the day we called the Gauntlet, the 2nd of Sun's Dusk. Bloody competitions would be held in her honor, and the duels and battles would continue until nine cultists were killed at the hands of other cultists. Boethiah cared little for her cultists-she only cared for our blood. I do think I saw her smile when I accidentally slew my brother in a sparring session. My horror, I think, greatly pleased her. I left the cult soon after that. Boethiah was too impersonal for me, too cold. I wanted a mistress of greater depth. For the next eighteen years of my life, I worshipped no one. Instead I read and researched. It was in an old and profane tome that I came upon the name of Nocturnal-Nocturnal the Night Mistress, Nocturnal the Unfathomable. As the book prescribed, I called to her on her holy day, the 3rd of Hearth Fire. At last I had found the personal mistress I had so long desired. I strove to understand her labyrinthine philosophy, the source of her mysterious pain. Everything about her was dark and shrouded, even the way she spoke and the acts she required of me. It took years for me to understand the simple fact that I could never understand Nocturnal. Her mystery was as essential to her as savagery was to Boethiah or treachery was to Molag Bal. To understand Nocturnal is to negate her, to pull back the curtains cloaking her realm of darkness. As much as I loved her, I recognized the futility of unraveling her enigmas. I turned instead to her sister, Azura. Azura is the only Daedra Princess I have ever worshipped who seems to care about her followers. Molag Bal wanted my mind, Boethiah wanted my arms, and Nocturnal perhaps my curiosity. Azura wants all of that, and our love above all. Not our abject slavering, but our honest and genuine caring in all its forms. It is important to her that our emotions be engaged in her worship. And our love must also be directed inward. If we love her and hate ourselves, she feels our pain. I will, for all time, have no other mistress.

三百年来，我作为祭司侍奉统治月影的迪德拉君主，玫瑰之母，夜空女王--阿祖拉。每到初种月第二十一天，我们庆祝霍吉萨姆日，召唤她以求指引，并向我们的女王献上珍贵而美丽的祭品。她是严酷却明断的主母。如若霍吉萨姆日起了雷雨，我们不会向她祈唤，雷雨之夜属于疯子谢尔格拉，即使恰逢霍吉萨姆日也一样。在这样的时日里，阿祖拉理解我们的顾忌。 对阿祖拉的祈唤与个人息息相关。我曾担任过另外三位迪德拉君王的祭司，但只有阿祖拉看重崇拜者的品质，看重我们的敬爱之情所蕴含的赤诚。当我还是一位十六岁的暗精灵少女时，我加入了祖母的女巫集会，集会崇拜莫拉格·巴尔，阴谋女王。对于莫拉格·巴尔的女巫来说，讹诈，勒索，行贿是和黑魔法并重的武器。莫拉格·巴尔的祈唤在夜星月20日举行，除非雷雨天气，仪式极少失期，但莫拉格·巴尔也常在其他日子里以凡人的形象现身于教徒面前。当我的祖母死于她毒杀火望城继承人的图谋以后，我反思了我在教团中的信仰。 我的兄弟是波耶西亚教团的巫师--据他所说，黑暗战士比狡诈的莫拉格·巴尔更契合我的精神。波耶西亚是位战士女王，行事之公开是其余迪德拉所不能及的。为这位女主人效力所得到的结果直接了当。经过了多年的蛰伏和密谋之后，如此行事让我感觉甚好。我们教团会在日暮月2日召唤她，那一天我们称为试炼日。我们以她的名义举行血腥的竞赛，对决和战斗一直持续到九名教徒死于其余人之手。波耶西亚不在乎她的教徒--她只在乎我们的血。当我在一次对决中意外杀死了我的兄弟时，我很确定我看到了她的微笑。我猜，我的惊恐令她感到了极大的愉悦。 之后不久我就离开了教团。波耶西亚对我来说太过不近人情，太过冷酷。我想要一个更深邃的主人。在我人生接下来的十八年里，我不崇拜任何神明。我只做研读。最后我在一册古老亵渎的书卷中见到了诺克图娜尔这个名字—“黑夜女神”、“深不可测者”。按照这本书所指明的那样，我在她的圣日炉火月3日呼唤她。最终我找到了长久一来我一直渴求的关心我的主母，我努力去理解她迷宫一般的哲学，她神秘苦痛的根源。与她有关的一切都笼罩在黑暗中，包括她对我言说的方式和她叫我所行的事。我花了好几年才理解了这个简单的事实，那就是我永远也无法理解诺克图娜尔。神秘之于她就像野蛮之于波耶西亚或者奸诈之于莫拉格·巴尔一样必要。试图理解诺克图娜尔就是在试图否定她，试图扯下笼罩她黑暗领域的帷幕。尽管我爱她，但我意识到想要解开她的谜题终是徒劳。我转而信仰她的姐妹，阿祖拉。 阿祖拉是我崇拜过的唯一一个会关心自己追随者的迪德拉女王。莫拉格·巴尔要的是我的心智，波耶西亚要的是我的臂膀，诺克图娜尔要的也许是我的好奇心。阿祖拉要所有这一切，而在这之上，她要的是我们的爱。要的不是我们奴颜婢膝的谄媚，而是我们诚实而真挚的一切关怀。对于她来说，在我们崇拜中的真情实感非常重要。我们的爱必须发自真心。如果我们爱她却怨恨自己，她也将感受我们的痛苦。从此以后，我将不会再有别的主人。

Chronicles of Nchuleft

This is a chronicle of events of historical significance to the Dwemer Freehold Colony of Nchuleft. The text was probably recorded by an Altmer, for it is written in Aldmeris. [pagebreak] 23. The Death of Lord Ihlendam t happened in Second Planting (P.D. 1220) that Lord Ihlendam, on a journey in the Western Uplands, came to Nchuleft; and Protector Anchard and General Rkungthunch met him there, and Dalen-Zanchu also came to the meeting. They talked together long by themselves; but this only was known of their business, that they were to be friends of each other. They parted, and each went home to his own colony. Bluthanch and her sons came to hear of this meeting, and saw in this secret meeting a treasonable plot against the Councils; and they often talked of this among themselves. When spring came, the Councils proclaimed, as usual, a Council Meet, in the halls of Bamz-Amschend. The people accordingly assembled, handfasted with ale and song, drinking bravely, and much and many things were talked over at the drink-table, and, among other things, were comparisons between different dwemer, and at last among the Councilors themselves. One said that Lord Ihlendam excelled his fellow Councilors by far, and in every way. At this Councilor Bluthanch was very angry, and said that she was in no way less than Lord Ihlendam, and that she was eager to prove it. Instantly both parties were so inflamed that they challenged each other to battle, and ran to their arms. But some citizens who were less drunk, and more understanding, came between them, and quieted them; and each went back to his colony, but nobody expected that they would ever meet in peace again together. But then, in the fall, Lord Ihlendam received a message from Councilor Bluthanch, inviting him to a parlay at Hendor-Stardumz. And all Ihlendam's kin and citizens strongly urged him not to come, fearing treachery, but Lord Ihlendam would not listen to counsel, not even to carrying with him his honor guard. And sadly, it came to pass that, while traveling to Hendor-Stardumz, in Chinzinch Pass, a host of foul creatures set upon Lord Ihlendam and killed him, and all of his party. And many citizens said thereafter that Bluthanch and her sons had conjured these beasts and set them upon Lord Ihlendam, but nothing was proven. Lord Ihlendam lies buried at a place called Leftunch.

此为一篇关于锻莫长久居住地尼楚莱福特历史性大事件的历代记。由于原文为奥德莫文，所以很可能出自某傲特莫之手。 [pagebreak] 23.伊伦达姆勋爵之死 该事起于P.D.1220年次种节，伊伦达姆勋爵在西部高地旅行时，来到了尼楚莱福特；保护人安夏德与将军里昆图奇前往迎接，达伦-赞楚亦随行。他们会谈良久，但内容不详，他们成为彼此的朋友。随后他们分别，各自回到自己的居住地。 布鲁萨奇及其儿子们听闻了此次会面，并在此次密会中察觉到了背叛议会的阴谋，他们彼此经常谈论此事。春天来临，议会一如既往在巴姆泽-阿姆斯森德的大厅里召开会议。于是人们聚集一起，喝酒唱歌，互相斗酒。在酒桌上，人们谈论着很多事，其中就有酒鬼们的互相吹嘘，甚至还对议员们进行品评。 有人说伊伦达姆勋爵在各方面远胜其他议员同僚。布鲁萨奇议员为此言论大为光火，声称她一点不比伊伦达姆勋爵差，而且她十分急于证明这一点。双方立刻都十分恼怒，互相挑战，拔出了武器。但一些尚未醉过头且比较机敏的公民挡在他们中间，劝说他们冷静。他们各自返回自己的居住地，没人看好他们还能再和平共处了。 但就在秋天，伊伦达姆勋爵收到了布鲁萨奇议员的信，邀请他到亨多-斯塔杜姆兹参加聚会。伊伦达姆的所有亲朋和公民都极力劝阻，担心恐遭背叛，但伊伦达姆勋爵不听劝告，甚至连仪仗队都没带。不幸的是，在前往钦津奇山口的亨多-斯塔杜姆兹途中，一群邪恶生物袭击了伊伦达姆勋爵，杀死了他们一伙。许多公民后来都说，是布鲁萨奇和她的儿子们召唤了这些怪兽，指使它们攻击了伊伦达姆勋爵，可惜没有什么证据。伊伦达姆勋爵最终被葬在了一个叫莱福特恩齐的地方。

The Charwich-Koniinge Letters Book IV

8 Sun's Dawn, 3E 412 Amiglith, Summurset Isle My Good Friend, Lord Gemyn, You must forgive me for not meeting you at the palace personally, but I've been unavoidably, tragically detained. I've left the front gate and door unlocked, and if you're reading this, you must have made it at least as far the antechamber to the east drawing room. Perhaps you've already wandered the estate and seen some of its delights before coming to this chamber: the seven fountains of marble and porphyry, the reflecting pool, the various groves, the colonnades and quincunx. I don't think you would have already gone to the second floor suites and the west wing as you would have had to pass this room first, and picked up this letter. But believe me, they're beautifully appointed with magnificent balustrades, winding staircases, intimate salons, and bedchambers worthy of your affluence. The price of this property is exorbitant, certainly, but for a man like you who seeks only the best, this is the villa you must have. As you undoubtedly noticed as you arrived through the gates, there are several smaller buildings ideally suited to be guard stations. I know you are concerned with security. I am an intensely greedy man, and there is nothing I would have liked more than to meet you here today, show you the grounds, fawn on you obsequiously, and collect a fat percentage of the cost of the sale when you bought this marvelous palace, as I'm sure you would have. My dilemma that caused my inexcusable absence began shortly after I arrived here early to make certain the villa was well-cleaned for your inspection. A man named Koniinge crept up behind me, and gripped me by the throat. Clamping his left hand over my mouth and nose, and throttling me with his right hand, crushing the soft spot on my throat just below the thyroidal cartilage, he effectively strangled me in a few quick but very painful minutes. I am currently buried in a pile of leaves in the north statuary parterre, close to the exceptional sculptural representation of the Transformation of Trinimac. It should not be too long before I am discovered: someone at my bank will surely notice my absence in due time. Koniinge might have buried me deeper, but he wanted to be ready for the arrival of his old partner, Charwich. Perhaps part of you thinks it best to stop reading now, Lord Gemyn. You are looking around the antechamber and seeing nothing but doors. The large one you took to come in from the garden is locked now behind you, and without a better knowledge of the layout of the estate, I could not recommend you attempt to flee down a corridor that might easily come to a dead end. No. Much better to keep reading, and see where this is going. Koniinge, it seems, was in a partnership with his friend Charwich to try to recover Azura's Star. They understood it to be in the possession of someone named Hadwaf Neithwyr, a man who conjured up the Daedra Prince Azura herself to acquire it. As Neithwyr originally haled from High Rock, Charwich went there to look for him, while his partner searched Morrowind. They planned to communicate their findings by letters sent through couriers. Charwich's first letter stated that he had found information that Neithwyr had a mysterious patron named Baliasir, a fact he had learned at a cemetery with a gravestone of Neithwyr's sister Peryra and a lycanthropic caretaker. Koniinge replied back that he could find nothing about Baliasir, but believed that Neithwyr had returned to High Rock with Peryra after getting the Star. Charwich's last letter was a written on his deathbed, having sustained mortal wounds from his battle with Baliasir, who it seemed had been a mighty daedra lord. Koniinge grieved for his friend, and traveled the span of the Empire to Wayrest, to pay his call of condolences on Lady Moorling, the woman at whose house Charwich had been staying. After making some inquiries, Koniinge learned that her ladyship had left the city, quite suddenly. She had been entertaining a guest named Charwich, and it was understood that he had died, though no one ever saw the body. Certainly no healers had been sent to her house on the 13th of Last Seed of last year. And no one in Wayrest, just like no one in Tel Aruhn, had ever heard of Baliasir. Poor Koniinge was suddenly unsure of everything. He retraced his late partner's path through Boriane and Grimtry Gardens, but found that the Neithwyr family crypt was elsewhere, in a small town in the barony of Dwynnen. There was indeed a lycanthropic caretaker, fortunately in human form at the time. When questioned (using the technique of strangulation, release, strangulation, release), he told Koniinge the story that he had told Charwich many months before. Hadwaf and Peryra Neithwyr had returned to Dwynnen, intent on settling old business. As the Star requires potent spirits for power, they thought they would begin small by capturing the spirit of the werewolf they knew of in the family graveyard. Sadly, for them, their grasp exceeded their reach. When the poor caretaker resumed his human form one morning, he found himself lying next to the shredded, bloody bodies of the Neithwyr siblings. Distressed and fearful, he brought the corpses and all their possessions down into the crypt. They were still there when Charwich came, and so too was Azura's Star. Koniinge now saw things clearly. The letters he had received from Charwich were lies, intended to keep him away. Undoubtedly with the assistance of Lady Moorling, his new partner, he had concocted stories, including one of his own demise, to trick Koniinge into abandoning the quest for the Star. It was clearly a sad statement on the nature of friendship, and one that needed immediate correction. It took the better part of six months for Koniinge to find his old partner. Charwich and Lady Moorling had used the power of the Star to make themselves very wealthy and powerful. They assumed a number of different identities in their travels through High Rock and Skyrim, and then down to Valenwood and the Summurset Isle. Along the way, of course, the Star itself disappeared, as great daedric artifacts always do. The couple still had much wealth, but their love sadly fell on troubled times. When they reached Alinor, they parted ways. One must assume that during their months together, Charwich must have told Lady Moorling about Koniinge. It's pleasant to think of the loving couple laughing over the stories they were telling him about the mythical and dangerous Baliasir. Charwich must not have given his former beloved a very accurate physical description, however, because when Lady Moorling (then under the identity of the Countess Zyliana) met Koniinge, she had no idea who he was. It came as quite a surprise to her when he began strangling her and requesting information about her former paramour. Before she died, she told Koniinge what Charwich's new name and title was, and where he was looking for a new palace. She even told him about me. Given all the twists and bends the last months' chase took him on, it was not difficult to find which palace Charwich was looking to buy, and what time his appointment was to view it. Then he had merely to arrive early, dispose of me, and wait. There our story must sadly end. I look forward to seeing you soon. Yours, Syrix Goinithi, Former Estate Banker P.S.: Charwich -- Turn around now, or don't. Your choice. Your friend, Koniinge.

3E412年，日晓月8日 夏暮岛 阿米格利斯 我的好友，杰米恩大人： 请原谅我不能亲自到宫中见您，但不幸的是，我不可避免地被耽搁了。我没有锁前门和屋门，如果你正在读这封信，那您肯定至少已经从前厅走到东客厅了。也许在来到这个房间前，你已经在庄园里漫步了一阵，看到了里面的一些景致，七块大理石和斑岩组成的喷泉、反射池、各式树木、立柱连廊和梅花。您应该没到二楼的套房和西翼，因为这个房间是必经之路，您会先拿到这封信。但相信我，那边布置得很漂亮，栏杆华美、楼梯蜿蜒，还有私密的沙龙和与您的富贵相称的寝室。 当然，这所宅院价格肯定不菲，不过像您这种追求极致享受的人来说，这里还是物超所值的。您穿过大门时肯定注意到了，这里有几座较小的建筑很适合当做警卫站。我知道您很担心安全问题。 我很贪心的，我很希望今天能在这里见到您，带您参观，好好奉承您，当您买下这座美妙的宫殿时，从售价中拿一笔丰厚的提成，因为我相信您肯定会出手拿下的。但我的困境使我不可被原谅地失约了，就在我提前到达这里，来确定您来参观的别墅是否已经打扫干净了。有个叫科宁吉的人蹑足潜踪走到我背后，扼住了我的喉咙。他左手捂住我的口鼻，用右手掐住我的脖子，摁住了我喉咙里甲状软骨下面最柔软的部位，短短几分钟，我就被他勒死了。 我现在就被埋在北面花坛下面的一堆树叶里，靠近“崔尼玛克的转化”那尊杰出雕像。用不了多久，我就会被发现，我所在银行的某人肯定会及时发现我失踪了。科宁吉本来想把我埋得更深，但他想在老搭档查维治来到前做好准备。 杰米恩大人，也许您现在正打算停止阅读。您环顾前厅，只看到了一扇门。从花园进来的那扇大的现在已经上锁了。如果您对庄园布局不大了解，我劝您还是顺着很容易走到头的连廊逃跑吧。不对，最好还是继续读吧，看看下文如何。 科宁吉似乎是和自己的朋友查维治合作，打算夺取阿祖拉之星。他们打听到东西正在哈德沃夫·内斯维尔的手里，他召唤了迪德拉君王阿祖拉。查维治顺着内斯维尔的足迹到高岩寻访，而搭档科宁吉则搜查晨风。他们打算通过信件来交流发现。 查维治在第一份信中说，他发现内斯维尔有个神秘的后台，叫做巴里亚瑟。他从一个墓地得知了这个情报，还在那里发现了内斯维尔的妹妹佩蕾拉的墓碑还有一个狼人守墓人。科宁吉回信说没有找到任何关于巴里亚瑟的信息，相信内斯维尔在得到了星之后就带着佩蕾拉回高岩了。查维治最后一封信写于临终前，他在和巴里亚瑟的战斗中受了致命伤，巴里亚瑟似乎是个强大的迪德拉领主。 科宁吉为朋友之死悲痛不已，横跨帝国赶到了途歇城，打算拜访收留查维治的莫林女士，向她致哀。但当科宁吉打探一番之后，得知女士突然离城。她是接待了一个叫查维治的客人，据了解他已经死了，可没人见过尸体。而去年末种月13日，也确实没有医生到过她家。正如泰尔·阿鲁恩一样，途歇城也没人听说过巴里亚瑟。可怜的科宁吉顿时对一切都丧失了信心。他从博理安到格里姆特里花园一路追溯已故搭档的足迹，却发现内斯维尔的家族墓地另有他处，在杜维能男爵领的某个小镇上。也确有一个狼人守墓人，所幸当时他还是人形。在被询问时（技巧是反复勒断气再释放），他告诉科宁吉几个月前见到查维治的事。 哈德沃夫和佩蕾拉兄妹回到杜维能打算解决宿怨。因为阿祖拉之星需要强大的灵魂才能获得力量，所以他们觉得可以从小处着手，先拿家族墓地里拿他们认识的狼人开刀。可惜，他们不知自己能吃几碗饭。等天亮，可怜的守墓人恢复人形时，发现自己倒在兄妹二人血肉模糊的尸体旁。他又愁又怕，把尸体连同所有东西都藏到了墓穴里。查维治来的时候，东西都在，包括阿祖拉之星。 科宁吉现在看清了。他从查维治那里收到的信全是骗人的，为的就是把他支走。毫无疑问，查维治在新搭档莫林夫人的帮助下，编了些故事，伪造了自己的死亡，诱导科宁吉放弃寻找阿祖拉之星。这显然是友谊的可悲反例，需要立即矫正。 科宁吉花了半年多找到了他的老伙计。查维治和莫林夫人利用阿祖拉之星的力量赚的盆满钵满。他们在高岩和天际的旅途中变换了许多身份，之后又去了威伦森林和夏暮岛。当然，在途中，星消失了，和其他强大的迪德拉神器一样。这对夫妻虽仍旧富有，但他们的爱情却陷入了困境。他们在抵达艾琳诺之后就分手了。 在他们相处的数个月中，查维治一定把科宁吉的故事告诉了莫林夫人。想到这贤伉俪因告诉他的那神秘危险的巴里亚瑟的故事而开怀大笑，真是愉快啊。但查维治一定没有给他的前情人仔细描述科宁吉的样貌，因为当莫林夫人（当时叫齐丽安娜伯爵夫人）遇到科宁吉时，压根没有认出来。当他开始勒她并询问她前情人的情况时，她感到相当惊讶。 她去世前，招出了查维治的新名字和头衔，以及他在哪里物色新的宅邸。她甚至跟他提到了我。考虑到他过去几个月追逐中的种种曲折经历，自然不难发现查维治打算买哪处房产，预定何时参观。只要早些抵达，干掉我，然后静候即可。 我们的故事必须悲哀地结束了。期待咱们尽快见面。 您的 前地产银行家 希瑞克斯·格尼锡 又：查维治，要么回头看看，要么就站稳。自己选吧。你朋友，科宁吉。
