n the last dinner in my employ at the palace, the Duchess, quite surprisingly, had invited the mayor of Moliva and Master Hiomaste himself among her other guests. The servants' gossip was manic. The mayor had been there before, albeit very irregularly, but Hiomaste's presence was unthinkable. What could she mean by such a conciliatory gesture? The dinner itself progressed along with perfect if slightly cool civility among all parties. Hiomaste and the Duchess were both very quiet. The Mayor tried to engage the group in a discussion of the Emperor Pelagius IV's new son and heir Uriel, but it failed to spark much interest. Lady Villea, elderly but much more vivacious than her sister the Duchess, led most of the talk about crime and scandal in Eldenroot. "I have been encouraging her to move out to the country, away from all that unpleasantness for years now," the Duchess said, meeting the eyes of the Mayor. "We've been discussing more recently the possibility of her building a palace on Moliva Hill, but there's so little space there as you know. Fortunately, we've come to a discovery. There is a wide field just a few days west, on the edge of the river, ideally suited." "It sounds perfect," the Mayor smiled and turned to Lady Villea: "When will your ladyship begin building?" "The very day you move your village to the site," replied the Duchess of Woda. The Mayor turned to her to see if she was joking. She obviously was not. "Think of how much more commerce you could bring to your village if you were close to the river," said Lady Villea jovially. "And Master Hiomaste's students could have easier access to his fine school. Everyone would benefit. I know it would put my sister's heart to ease if there was less trespassing and poaching on her lands." "There is no poaching or trespassing on your lands now, Your Grace," frowned Hiomaste. "You do not own the jungle, nor will you. The villagers may be persuaded to leave, that I don't know. But my school will stay where it is." The dinner party never really recovered happily. Hiomaste and the Mayor excused themselves, and my services, such as they were, were not needed in the drawing room where the group went to have their drinks. There was no laughter to be heard through the walls that evening. The next day, even though there was a dinner planned for the evening, I left on my usual walk to Moliva. Before I had even reached the drawbridge, the guard held me back: "Where are you going, Gorgic? Not to the village, are you?" "Why not?" He pointed to the plume of smoke in the distance: "A fire broke out very early this morning, and it's still going. Apparently, it started at Master Hiomaste's school. It looks like the work of some traveling brigands." "Blessed Stendarr!" I cried. "Are the students alive?" "No one knows, but it'd be a miracle if any survived. It was late and most everyone was sleeping. I know they've already found the Master's body, or what was left of it. And they also found that girl, your friend, Prolyssa." I spent the day in a state of shock. It seemed inconceivable what my instinct told me: that the two noble old ladies, Lady Villea and the Duchess of Woda, had arranged for a village and school that irritated them to be reduced to ashes. At dinner, they mentioned the fire in Moliva only very briefly, as if it were not news at all. But I did see the Duchess smile for the first time ever. It was a smile I will never forget until the day I die. The next morning, I had resolved to go to the village and see if I could be of any assistance to the survivors. I was passing through the servants' hall to the grand foyer when I heard the sound of a group of people ahead. The guards and most of the servants were there, pointing at the portrait of the Duchess that hung in the center of the hall. There was a single black bolt of ebony piercing the painting, right at the Duchess's heart. I recognized it at once. It was one of Missun Akin's arrows I had seen in his quiver, forged, he said, in the bowels of Dagoth-Ur itself. My first reaction was relief: the Dunmer who had been kind enough to give me a ride to the palace had survived the fire. My second reaction was echoed by all present in the hall. How had the vandal gotten past the guards, the gate, the moat, and the massive iron door? The Duchess, arriving shortly after I, was clearly furious, though she was too well bred to show it but by raising her web-thin eyebrows. She wasted no time in assigning all her servants to new duties to keep the palace grounds guarded at all times. We were given regular shifts and precise, narrow patrols. The next morning, despite all precautions, there was another black arrow piercing the Duchess's portrait. So it continued for a week's time. The Duchess saw to it that at least one person was always present in the foyer, but somehow the arrow always found its way to her painting whenever the guard's eyes were momentarily averted. A complex series of signals were devised, so each patrol could report back any sounds or disturbances they encountered during their vigil. At first, the Duchess arranged them so her castellan would receive record of any disturbances during the day, and the chief of the guard during the night. But when she found that she could not sleep, she made certain that the information came to her directly. The atmosphere in the palace had shifted from gloomy to nightmarish. A snake would slither across the moat, and suddenly Her Grace would be tearing through the east wing to investigate. A strong gust of wind ruffling the leaves on one of the few trees in the lawn was a similar emergency. An unfortunate lone traveler on the road in front of the palace, a completely innocent man at it turned out, brought such a violent reaction that he must have thought that he had stumbled on a war. In a way, he had. And every morning, there was a new arrow in the front hall, mocking her. I was given the terrible assignment of guarding the portrait for a few hours in the early morning. Not wanting to be the one to discover the arrow, I seated myself in a chair opposite, never letting my eyes move away for even a second. I don't know if you've had the experience of watching one object relentlessly, but it has a strange effect. All other senses vanish. That was why I was particularly startled when the Duchess rushed into the room, blurring the gulf for me between her portrait and herself. "There's something moving behind the tree across the road from the gate!" she roared, pushing me aside, and fumbling with her key in the gold lock. She was shaking with madness and excitement, and the key did not seem to want to go in. I reached out to help her, but the Duchess was already kneeling, her eye to the keyhole, to be certain that the key went through. It was precisely in that second that the arrow arrived, but this one never made it as far as the portrait. I actually met Missun Akin years later, while I was in Morrowind to entertain some nobles. He was impressed that I had risen from being a humble domestic servant to being a bard of some renown. He himself had returned to the ashlands, and, like his old master Hiomaste, was retired to the simple life of teaching and hunting. I told him that I had heard that Lady Villea had decided not to leave the city, and that the village of Modiva had been rebuilt. He was happy to hear that, but I could not find a way to ask him what I really wanted to know. I felt like a fool just wondering if what I thought were true, that he had been behind Prolyssa's tree across the road from the gate every morning that summer, firing an arrow through the gate, across the lawn, across the moat, through a keyhole, and into a portrait of the Duchess of Woda until he struck the Duchess herself. It was clearly an impossibility. I chose not to ask. As we left one another that day, and he was waving good-bye, he said, "I am pleased to see you doing so well, my friend. I am happy you moved that chair."

在我受雇于宫殿准备的最后一顿晚宴上，公爵夫人出乎意料地邀请来莫里瓦镇长和希奥马斯特大师本人做客。仆人们议论纷纷。虽说不定期，但镇长好歹曾经来访数次，而希奥马斯特的出席则难以想象。她作如此和解姿态是何意？ 晚宴本身进展得很顺利，各方虽然冷淡，但也算恪守礼节。希奥马斯特和公爵夫人均沉默寡言。镇长试图令这群人参与关于皇帝佩拉吉奥斯四世的新生子和继承人尤瑞尔·塞普汀七世的议论，然而并没引起多大兴趣。与会的薇莉雅夫人年岁较老，但却比身为公爵夫人的妹妹开朗很多，她谈起了很多关于艾尔登之根犯罪与丑闻的话题。 “多年来，我一向鼓励她迁往乡下，远离那些不愉快的事情，”公爵夫人说着，对上镇长双目，“我们近来一直在商议帮她在莫里瓦山上起造宫室的可能性，但如您所知，那里空间狭窄。幸运的是，我们有了一个发现。向西几天路程处有一片沿河的开阔田野，非常合适。” “这听起来很完美，”镇长微笑着转向薇莉雅夫人：“夫人意欲何时破土动工？” “您将您的村镇迁往工地那一天。”沃达公爵夫人答道。 镇长转向她想看看她是否语出玩笑。显然她并非戏言。 “想想看，若您迁到临近河流的地方，您能为村镇带来多大的商贸收益吧，”薇莉雅夫人愉悦地说着，“而希奥马斯特大师的门生们能更容易进入他的名校。人人皆受益。而且如果我妹妹的领地上能少些非法入侵和盗猎，也能让她安心些。” “如今在您的领土上并无盗猎或非法入侵，夫人，”希奥马斯特蹙眉，“您并非丛林的所有者，也不会成为所有者。村民们若是被说服或许会选择离开，但我就两说了。我的学校将留守原地。” 晚宴不欢而散。希奥马斯特和镇长告辞而去，而其余众人所去的会客室里并不需要我侍候。因为他们是去自饮自备酒水的。那夜隔墙不闻丝毫笑声。 次日，尽管当晚安排有一次晚宴，但我仍照常走向莫里瓦。我甚至还未走到吊桥，卫兵已将我拦下：“你去哪儿啊歌尔基科？别是去村子那吧？” “不行吗？” 他指指远方一缕轻烟：“今儿大清早突然起了场火，这会儿还在烧呢。这火明显是从希奥马斯特大师的学校里着起来的。看着像是强盗干的。” “斯坦达尔保佑！”我惊声尖叫，“那学徒们还好吗？” “没人晓得，不过要是有谁能活下来那可真是神迹了。那会儿天太晚了，大多数人还睡着呢。我听说他们已经找着了大师的遗体，或者说是残骸吧。他们还找着了那女孩，就是你朋友，普罗丽莎。” 我一整天都沉沦在满心震惊中。我的本能告知我事有反常：那两位老贵妇，薇莉雅夫人和沃达公爵夫人，一手安排下让触怒她们的村庄和学校化作灰烬。在晚宴上，她们只非常简扼地提及了莫里瓦的失火，好似这根本不算什么新闻。但我第一次看到了公爵夫人的笑容。那是我至死难忘的笑。 次日清晨，我决意前往村庄，看看能不能帮到幸存者。我正穿过仆人堂向大门厅走去，就听闻一群人的声响。卫兵们和绝大多数仆人皆在彼处，对那高悬大厅中央的公爵夫人肖像指指点点。 一杆黢暗的黑檀洞穿了画作，正中公爵夫人的心口。 我一眼就认出了那东西。那是密松·亚金的箭筒里的箭矢，据他所言，其于达格斯·乌尔的腑脏中锻冶而成，我的第一反应是松了口气：那个好心载我到宫殿来的丹莫从大火里活了下来。我的第二反应则得到了厅堂内众人的呼应。破坏者究竟如何越过卫兵、大门、护城河和巨大的城堡铁门呢？ 公爵夫人在我到来后不久便抵达，显然很是生气，不过由于教养极好的缘故，除了微微扬起网薄的眉毛外，没有过于表露自己的怒火。她毫不犹豫地给所有仆人分配了新职责，从而令宫殿保持全天候警备。我们也被安排了非常规律的轮班和精密频繁的巡逻。 次日早晨，虽有这一切预防措施，仍有另一杆黑矢刺穿了公爵夫人肖像。 如此持续一周。公爵夫人确保至少有一人常驻于门厅中，但不知何故，每当守卫双目暂且移开之时，箭矢总能命中她的画作。 他们为此设计了一系列繁复的信号，因而每支巡逻队皆可汇报他们在守夜期间遭遇的任何声响和骚动。起初，公爵夫人安排她的城堡执事接收白天传来的所有骚动记录，而卫兵长则在夜间接任。然而当她发现这样扰得自己不得安枕时，她又安排把消息直报自己。 宫殿内的氛围从阴郁变成了噩梦。一尾蛇溜过了护城河，而夫人就会突然从东翼冲出来大加调查。一阵强风吹皱了草坪上为数不多的数棵树的叶子，也被算成了紧急情况。一位不走运的独步旅者行走在宫殿前的道路上，结果只是一名彻头彻尾清清白白之人，却引发了如此强烈的反应，他一定是觉得自己无意中遇到了一场战争。某种程度上，确实是。 而每日清晨，皆有一发新矢钉在前厅嘲讽着她。 我被分配了糟糕的任务，那就是在大清早数小时内看守画作。我可不想发现箭矢，于是我坐在正对面的一把椅子上，眼神不敢稍错开一秒。我不知晓您是否有目不转睛紧盯什么东西的经历，但这有种古怪的效果。其他一切感官都静默了。这就是为何我在公爵夫人冲进室内时特别吃惊，还恍惚间没分清她和自己的画像。 “大门外道路对侧的树林背后有些什么在移动！”她咆哮着将我推搡到一边，拿着她的钥匙在那金锁上摸索着。 她激动得浑身发抖，而钥匙似乎不大想进去。我伸出援手想要相助，但公爵夫人已是跪倒在地，眼睛盯着锁孔，以确定钥匙能不能插进去。 箭矢恰在那一秒射来，但，这回却并没有射到画像那么远的地方。 数年后在晨风招待贵族时，我与密松·亚金重逢了。他对于我自从卑微的仆人一跃成为小有名气的吟游诗人感到惊奇。他本人也返回了灰地，并如他的往日恩师希奥马斯特那样，在退休后过着教授和狩猎的朴素生活。 我告知他，我听闻薇莉雅夫人已决定不离开城市，而莫里瓦村也已重建。他很高兴听到这些，但我找不到方法询问他我真正欲知之事。我觉得这样像是个傻瓜，但我只想知道自己所想是否确凿无误，他是否在那夏日的每天清晨藏身在门外道路对面普罗丽莎曾经攀爬的树后，张弓射出一发箭矢飞越大门、草坪、护城河，穿透锁孔、并钉入沃达公爵夫人的肖像画上，直至他袭杀了公爵夫人本人。这显然绝无可能。我选择不问。 那天我们分别时，他挥手告别，道：“能看到你过得不错我很高兴，朋友。多亏你那天搬来那把椅子。”

Father of the Niben Translated and With Commentary by Florin Jaliil

[pagebreak] [pagebreak]

Introduction: Writing the biography of anyone is a challenge. Usually the problem lies in assessing one's sources, comparing the prejudices of one chronicle versus another versus another. Waughin Jarth, I have been told, in writing his well-regarded series on the Wolf Queen of Solitude used over a hundred contemporary narratives. I cannot complain about my task having a similar issue. There is but one record of the man called Topal the Pilot, the earliest known Aldmer explorer of Tamriel. Only four short verse fragments of the epic "Father of the Niben" have survived to present day, but they offer an interesting if controversial look at the Middle Merethic Era when Topal the Pilot may have sailed the seas around Tamriel. Though "Father of the Niben" is the only written record of Topal the Pilot's voyages, it is not the only proof of his existence. Among the treasures of the great Crystal Tower of Summerset Isle are his crude but fascinating maps, his legacy to all Tamriel. The translation of the Aldmeri Udhendra Nibenu, "Father of the Niben," is my own, and I accept that other scholars may disagree with some of my choice of words. I cannot promise my translation lives up to the beauty of the original: I have only strived for simple coherence. Fragment One: Second ship, the Pasquiniel, manned by pilot Illio, was to follow the southern pointing Waystone; and the third, the Niben, manned By pilot Topal, was to follow the north-east Pointing waystone; the orders from the Crystal Tower, they were to sail forth for Eighty moons and then return to tell. Only Niben returned to Firsthold, laden high with Gold and spice and fur and strange creatures, Dead and live. Though, alas, Old Ehlnofey Topal never found, he Told the tales of the lands he had visited to the Wonderment of all. For sixty-six days and nights, he sailed, over crashing Waves of dire intent, past whirlpools, through Mist that burned like fire, until he reached the Mouth of a great bay and he landed on a Sun-kissed meadow of gentle dells. As he and his men rested, there came a fearsome howl, And hideous orcs streamed forth from the murky Glen, cannibal teeth clotted with gore For centuries, strange crystalline balls were unearthed at the sites of ancient Aldmer shipwrecks and docks, peculiar artifacts of the Merethic and Dawn Eras that puzzled archeologists until it was demonstrated that each had a tendency to rotate on its axis in a specific direction. There were three varieties, one that pointed southward, one that pointed northeast, and one that point northwest. It is not understood how they work, but they seemed attuned to particular lines of power. These are the "waystones" of the fragment, which each of the pilots used to point their craft in the direction they were assigned to go. A ship with a name not mentioned in the fragment took his vessel north-west, towards Thras and Yokuda. The Pasquiniel took the southern waystone, and must have sailed down toward Pyandonea. Topal and his north-east waystone found the mainland of Tamriel. It is clear from this fragment what the three ships were assigned to do - find a passage back to Old Ehlnofey so that the Aldmer now living in Summerset could learn what became of their old homeland. As this book is intended to be a study of Topal the Pilot, there is scarcely room to dedicate to different theories of the Aldmeri exodus from Old Ehlnofey. If I were using this poem as my only source, I would have to agree with the scholars who believe in the tradition that several ships left Old Ehlnofey and were caught in a storm. Those who survived found their way to Summerset Isle, but without their waystones, they did not know what direction their homeland was. After all, what other explanation is there for three ships heading in three opposite directions to find a place? Naturally, only one of the ships returned, and we do not know if either or both of the other two found Old Ehlnofey, or perished at sea or at the hands of the ancient Pyandoneans, Sload, or Yokudans. We must assume, unless we think the Aldmer particularly idiotic, that at least one of them must have been pointing in the right direction. It may well have even been Topal, and he simply did not go north-east far enough. So, Topal setting sail from Firsthold heads north-east, which coincidentally is the longest one can travel along the Abecean Sea without striking land of any kind. Had he traveled straight east, he would have struck the mainland somewhere in what is now the Colovian West of Cyrodiil in a few weeks. Had he traveled south-east, he might have reached the hump of Valenwood in a few days. But our pilot, judging by his own and our modern maps, sailed in a straight line north-east, through the Abecean sea, and into the Iliac Bay, before touching ground somewhere near present day Anticlere in two months time. The rolling verdant hills of southern High Rock are unmistakable in this verse, recognizable to anyone who has been there. The question, of course, is what is to be made of this apparent reference to orcs occupying the region? Tradition has it that the orcs were not born until after the Aldmer had settled the mainland, that they sprung up as a distinct race following the famous battle between Trinimac and Boethiah at the time of Resdayn. It is possible that the tradition is wrong. Perhaps the orcs were an aboriginal tribe predating the Aldmeri colonization. Perhaps these were a cursed folk -- "Orsimer" in the Aldmeris, the same word for "Orc" - of a different kind, whose name was to be given the orcs in a different era. It is regrettable that the fragment ends here, for more clues to the truth are undoubtedly lost. What's missing between the first fragment and the second is appreciable. It must be more than eighty months that have passed, because Topal is on the opposite side of mainland Tamriel now, attempting to sail south-west to return to Firsthold, after his failure at finding Old Ehlnofey. Fragment Two: No passage westward could be found in the steely cliffs That jutted up like giant's jaw, so the Niben Sailed south. As it passed an sandy, forested island that promised Sanctuary and peace, the crew cheered in joy. Then exultation turned to terror as a great shadow rose From the trees on leathered wings like a unfurling Cape. The great bat lizard was large as the ship, but good pilot Topal merely raised his bow, and struck it in its Head. As it fell, he asked his Bo 'sun, "Do you think it's dead?" And before it struck the white-bearded waves, he Shot once more its heart to be certain. And so for another forty days and six, the Niben sailed south We can see that in addition to Topal's prowess as a navigator, cartographer, survivalist, and raconteur, he is a master of archery. It may be poetic license, of course, but we do have archeological proof that the Merethic Aldmer were sophisticated archers. Their bows of layers of wood and horn drawn by silver silk thread are beautiful, and still, I have heard experts say, millennia later, very deadly. It is tempting to imagine it a dragon, but the creature that Topal faces at the beginning of this fragment sounds like an ancestor of the cliffracer of present day Morrowind. The treacherous cliff coastline sounds like the region around Necrom, and the island of Gorne may be where the nest of the "bat lizard" is. No creatures like that exist in eastern Morrowind to my knowledge at the present day. Fragment Three: The fetid, evil swamp lands and their human lizards Retreated to the east, and Topal and his men's Hearts were greatly gladdened by the sight of Diamond blue, pure, sweet ocean. For three days, they sailed in great cheer north-west Where Firsthold beckoned them, but hope died In horror, as land, like a blocking shield rose Before them. Topal the Pilot was sore wroth, and consulted he The maps he had faithfully drawn, to see Whether best to go south where the Continent must end, or take the river that Snaked through a passage north. "North!" cried he to his sad men. "North we go Now! Fear not, north!" Tracing Topal's movements, we see that he has skirted the edge of Morrowind and delved into southern Blackmarsh, seemingly determined to follow his waystone as best as he can. The swamp he is leaving is probably near present day Gideon. Knowing what we now know about Topal's personality, we can understand his frustration in the bay between Black Marsh and Elsweyr. Here is a man who follows his orders explicitly, and knows that he should have been going south-east through river ways to reach Firsthold. Looking at his maps, we can see that he attempted to find passages through, as he has mapped out the Inner Sea of Morrowind, and several of the swampy tributaries of Black Marsh, no doubt being turned away by the disease and fierce Argonian tribes that dissuaded many other explorers after him. With a modern map of Tamriel in hand, we can see that he makes the wrong choice in electing to go north-east instead of pushing southward. He could not have known then that what he perceived to be the endless mainland was only a jutting peninsula. He only knew that he had traveled too far southward already, and so he made a smart but incorrect decision to go up the river. It is ironic that this great miscalculation would today bear his mark of history. The bay he thought was an endless ocean is now known as Topal Bay, and the river that took him astray shares the name of his boat, the Niben River. Fragment Four: The cat demons of four legs and two ran the river's Length, always keeping the boat in their Green-eyed sight, hissing, and spitting, and Roaring with rage. But the sailors never had to brave the shores, for Fruit trees welcomed them, dropping their Arms down to the river's edge as if to Embrace the mer, and the men took the Fruit quickly before the cats could pounce. For eleven days, they traveled north, until they came To a crystalline lake, and eight islands of Surpassing beauty and peace. Brilliant flightful creatures of glorious colors Greeted them in Aldmeri language, Making the mer wonder, until they Understood they were only calling back The word they were speaking without Understanding it, and then the sailors Laughed. Topal the Pilot was enchanted with the islands And the feathered men who lived there. There the Niben stayed for a moon, and the bird Men learned how to speak their own words, And with taloned feet, to write. In joy for their new knowledge, they made Topal Their lord, giving him their islands for the Gift. Topal said he would return someday, but first he Must find the passage east to Firsthold, so Far away. This last fragment is bittersweet for a number of reasons. We know that this strange, friendly feathered people the Pilot encounters will be lost - in fact, this poem is the only one where mention is made of the bird creatures of Cyrodiil. The literacy that Topal gives them is evidently not enough to save them from their eventual fate, likely at the hands of the "cat demons," who we may assume are ancient Khajiiti. We know that Topal and his crew never find a route from the eight islands which are the modern day Imperial City through to the Iliac Bay. His maps tell the tale where this lost poem cannot. We see his hand as he traces his route up the Niben to Lake Rumare; and, after attempting a few tributaries which do not lead him where he wants to go, we can imagine Topal's frustration -- and that of his long-suffering crew -- as they return back down the Niben to Topal Bay. There, they evidently discovered their earlier mistake, for we see that they pass the peninsula of Elsweyr. Eventually they traveled along its coastline, past the shores of Valenwood, and eventually home. Usually epic tales end with a happy ending, but this one begins with one, and the means to which it was accomplished is lost. Besides the extraordinary bird creatures of present day Cyrodiil, we have caught glimpses of ancient orcs (perhaps), ancient cliff-racers, ancient Argonians, and in this fragment, ancient Khajiit. Quite a history in a few lines of simple verse, all because a man failed to find his home, and took all the wrong turns to retrace his steps back.

简介： 为人作传是一项挑战。问题通常在于评估资料来源，比较史料中存在的各种偏见。有人告诉我，瓦辛·贾斯在他广受好评的《独孤城狼后传》系列中加入了上百种当代传说。我不能抱怨说我的工作中存在类似问题。 有且仅有一份对“领航员”托帕——已知最早探索泰姆瑞尔的奥德莫探险家的记录。史诗《尼本之父》有四段诗篇保存至今，但它们提供了一个趣味与争议并存的视角来看待精灵纪元中期，那时的“领航员”托帕可能正在环游泰姆瑞尔。 虽然《尼本之父》是“领航员”托帕航行的唯一书面记录，但他存在过的证据不止于此。夏暮岛水晶塔的宝藏中就有他粗略但迷人的地图，那是他留给全泰姆瑞尔的遗产。 奥德莫语Udhendra Nibenu的译名“尼本之父”出自我本人。可能其他学者不认同我对某些字词的选择，我也不保证译文达到原文的美感，但求力保简单的行文连贯性。 片段一： 第二艘船，帕斯奎尼尔号，由领航员伊里奥掌舵，沿着南向的指路石； 第三艘船，尼本号，由领航员托帕掌舵，沿着东北向的指路石， 依水晶塔之令，他们须航行八十个月相方可回返。 仅有尼本号回到了首堡，满载着黄金、香料、毛皮与或死或生的珍稀生物。 虽然，唉，托帕一直没找到古伊诺菲大陆，但他讲述的那些曾到土地的故事，扣人心弦。 海航了六十又六个日夜，他驶过滔天巨浪，逃出漩涡，穿过火烧般的海雾，直至抵达大海湾的入口，登上一片沐浴日光的山谷草地。 当他和部下们休息时，传来一声可怕的嚎叫，面目狰狞的兽人自幽谷中鱼贯而出，食人利齿上血块凝结。 几个世纪以来，在古奥德莫沉船与码头遗迹常发掘出奇异水晶球。这些黎明纪元及精灵纪元的文物一直困扰着考古学家们，直到它们被证明有沿着轴线向特定方向旋转的趋势。目前已发掘出三种，分别指向南、东北和西北。 目前不知道它们如何运作，但似乎与特定能源线路相协调。这些即是片段中提及的“指路石”，每位领航员都用来指引船驶向被派往的特定方向。片段中未提及名字的船航向西北，朝瑟拉斯和尤库达驶去，帕斯奎尼尔号携带南向的指路石，想必是驶向派安多尼亚。托帕和他的东北指路石则发现了泰姆瑞尔大陆。 从这个片段可以清楚了解到三艘船分配到的任务--找到回归古伊诺菲的道路，以便居于夏暮岛的奥德莫知晓祖地后来如何。由于本书的目的是研究领航员托帕，没有空间来讨论奥德莫出走古伊诺菲大陆的不同理论。 如果我将这首诗作为唯一资料来源，就不得不同意学者们的传统观点：几艘船离开了古伊诺菲大陆，后受困于风暴。幸存者找到了通往夏暮岛的路，但在遗失指路石的情况下，他们不知祖地在何方。毕竟还有什么能解释三艘船朝着不同方向驶去呢？ 当然，只有一艘船得以回归，我们不知道另外两艘是找到了古伊诺菲，或是毁于海航，死于古派安多尼亚人、斯洛德或是尤库达人之手。除非我们认定奥德莫愚昧至极，否则就必须假设他们至少有一位指明了正确的方向。甚至可能是托帕，或许他只是航行得不够远罢了。 所以，托帕自首堡朝东北起航，这恰好是一条沿着阿贝希恩海，而不遭遇任何陆地的最长航线。若他径直往东，就会在几周以内发现大陆，即今天的希罗帝尔西部的科洛文某地。若他往东南，几天内就会抵达威伦森林丘陵。但是，据他自己的和我们当今的地图，我们的领航员笔直地沿着东北驶去，穿越阿贝希恩海进入髂骨湾，两月后在如今的安提克利尔附近某地登陆了。 这段诗里有南高岩连绵青山，任何曾到访者都不会将其认错。问题显然在于我们该如何理解兽人占领该地的说法？传说中兽人是在奥德莫定居大陆后，瑞斯戴恩时代中著名的崔尼玛克与波耶西亚之战后，突然涌现出的独特种族。 传说或许是错的，也许兽人在奥德莫殖民前就已经是一个土著部族。或许这些是另一个被诅咒的种族，故此在奥德莫语里是“奥辛莫”，这个与“兽人”同义的词语被赋予了另一个时代的兽人。遗憾的是，片段到此为止，更多找寻真相的线索已经丢失。 第一个和第二个片段间的缺失十分明显，肯定已经过去了八十多个月，因为托帕现在在泰姆瑞尔大陆对岸。在未能找到古伊诺菲后，他决定向西南返航，回到首堡。 片段二： 坚岩峭壁上找不到西向通道，如巨人下颌般突出， 所以尼本号向南航行。 当它经过一个森林茂盛的沙岛时，船员们欢呼雀跃，因其带来了庇护与安宁。 当巨大阴影升起时，欢欣化作恐惧，树林上的皮翼如斗篷般舒张开。 这巨大的蝙蝠蜥蜴和船一般大，但称职的领航员托帕一箭射中了它的头颅。 当它坠落，他问水手长：“你觉得它死了吗？” 在它卷起白浪之前，托帕再次射中它的心脏确保已死。 于是尼本号又向南航行了四十又六天 我们可以得知，托帕除了作为领航员、制图师、生存专家和健谈者，还精通箭术。当然这可能是一种诗意的描写，但我们确实有考古证据证明精灵纪元的奥德莫是技艺高超的弓箭手。他们的弓由多层木制配上银丝裹角，非常漂亮，而且我听专家说，这些弓几千年后仍然致命。 人们容易把开头托帕面对的生物想象成一条龙，但听来像是今日晨风峭壁行者的先祖。危险的峭壁海岸线听起来像死灵城周边地区，而戈恩岛可能就是所谓“蝙蝠蜥蜴”的巢穴。据我所知，东晨风目前还没有这种生物。 片段三： 恶臭可憎的沼泽地以及其中的人形蜥蜴消失在了东边， 而托帕和他的船员们为看到了那纯净、亲切的钻石蓝海洋而十分喜悦。 三天以来，他们欢呼雀跃地向着西北，即首堡向他们招手的方向航行 然而希望在陆地如屏障般阻拦在前时破灭了。 领航员托帕怒不可遏，查阅了他准确绘制的地图， 想了解是否向大陆尽头的南方，还是取一条北方的蜿蜒通道。 “北边！”他朝着那些悲伤的人们大喊。 “现在往北走！别害怕，往北走！” 追寻托帕的行踪，我们得知他绕过晨风边界，深入黑沼泽南部，似乎决心尽其所能地跟随他的指路石。他要离开的沼泽很可能是今天的吉迪昂附近。据我们当今对托帕性格的了解，可以理解他在黑沼泽与艾斯维尔之间海湾的沮丧。 他是一个明确遵照命令的人，知道该沿水路向东南抵达首堡。通过看他的地图，我们可以得知他试图找到通过其间的航道，因为他已经绘制出晨风内海，以及几条黑沼泽的沼泽支流。毫无疑问的是，疾病与激烈反抗的阿尔贡部族阻止了许多其他追随其后的探险家。 手中这份泰姆瑞尔现代地图表明，他选择向东北而不是向南推进是个错误选择。可能当时他不清楚，眼见那一望无际的大陆不过是一个突出的半岛。他只知道已经向南走得太远了，所以做了一个明智但错误的决定，逆流而上。 讽刺的是，这次重大误判让他明标史册。他认为的那望不到头的海洋，现在叫做托帕湾，而把他引入歧途的河流分享了船的名字，尼本河。 片段四： 四腿与两腿的猫妖在河上奔跑，碧眼盯着船， 口中吞吐唾沫，嘶嘶作响，怒气冲冲地咆哮着。 但水手们从来都不需要冒险上岸，因为就像要拥抱这些莫一般 臂膀垂到河边的果树欢迎他们，而水手们在猫扑过来前就迅速摘走了果子。 往北走了十一天后，来到了一个澄澈的湖泊和八个美丽宁静的岛屿。 色彩斑斓的飞行生物用奥德莫语向他们致意，使他们惊奇 直到水手们明白了，他们只是不加理解地回喊水手们所说的词语，之后笑了。 领航员托帕为这些岛屿与居于此的羽毛人着迷 尼本号在此呆了一个月相，鸟人们学会了如何说话，和用脚上的爪子写字 他们为新知识而欢欣鼓舞，立托帕为他们的主，将岛屿送给托帕作为礼物 托帕说他总有回来的一天，但首先必须要找到，那遥远的通往首堡的水道。 这最后的片段是苦乐参半的，原因众多。 我们知道领航员遇到的这些奇异、友好而带羽毛的人将会消失，事实上这是唯一一首提到希罗帝尔鸟类生物的诗歌。托帕给他们的识字能力显然不足以挽救他们的最终命运，很可能是落入“猫妖”之手，可以假设它们就是古卡吉特。 我们知道托帕和他的船员没有找到一条从八岛（即今帝都）到髂骨湾的路线。他的地图补充了这首缺失的诗歌没讲的部分。 我们可以看到他沿着自己的路线上溯尼本河到了卢玛瑞湖，在尝试了几条支流仍不能去到所想之地后，我们可以想象托帕和他的坚忍船员们沿尼本河返回托帕湾时的沮丧。 他们显然在那里发现了早先的错误，因为我们知道他们经过了艾斯维尔半岛。最后沿着海岸线航行，经过威伦森林海岸，最终返回家园。通常史诗都有一个好结局，但这首以一个好的开头，而结尾片段则丢失了。 除了对现今希罗帝尔而言的非凡鸟类，我们还瞥见了古兽人（存疑），古峭壁行者，古阿尔贡，以及这个片段里的古卡吉特。几行简单的诗句就讲述了一段历史，这一切都是因为一个找不到故乡的，拐错了弯不得不走回头路的人。

VERNACCUS AND BOURLOR By Tavi Dromio

[pagebreak] [pagebreak]

allgerd walked into the King's Ham that Loredas evening, his face clouded with sadness. While he ordered a mug of greef, his mates Garaz and Xiomara joined him with moderately sincere concern. "What's wrong with you, Hallgerd?" asked Xiomara. "You're later than usual, and there's a certain air of tragedy you've dragged in with you. Have you lost money, or a nearest and dearest?" "I haven't lost any money," Hallgerd grimaced. "But I've just received word from my nephew than my cousin Allioch has died. Perfectly natural, he says, just old age. Allioch was ten years younger than me." "Aw, that's terrible. But it goes to show that it's important to savor all of life's possibilities, 'cause you never know when your time is coming," said Garaz, who had been sitting at the same stool at the smoky cornerclub for the last several hours. He was not one cursed with self-awareness. "Life's short all right," agreed Xiomara. "But if you'll pardon a sentimental thought, few of us are aware of the influence we'll have after our deaths. Perhaps there's comfort there. For example, have I told you the story about Vernaccus and Bourlor?" "I don't believe so," said Hallgerd. Vernaccus was a daedra (said Xiomara, throwing a few dribbles on flin on the hearth to cast the proper mood), and though our tale took place many, many years ago, it would be fair to say that Vernaccus still is one. For what after all is time to the immortal daedra? "Actually," Garaz interrupted. "I understand that the notion of immortality--" "I am trying to offer our friend an inspirational tale in his hour of need," Xiomara growled. "I don't have all bloody night to tell it, if you don't mind." You wouldn't have heard of Vernaccus (said Xiomara, abandoning the theme of immortality for the time being) for even at the height of his power and fame, he was considered feeble by the admittedly high standards of the day. Of course, this lack of respect infuriated him, and his reaction was typical of lesser daedra. He went on a murderous rampage. Soon word spread through all the villages in the Colovian West of the unholy terror. Whole families had been butchered, castles destroyed, orchards and fields torched and cursed so nothing would ever grow there again. To make things even worse for the villagers, Vernaccus began getting visitations from an old rival of his from Oblivion. She was a daedra seducer named Horavatha, and she delighted in taunting him to see how angry she could make him become. "You've flooded a village and that's supposed to be impressive?" she would sneer. "Try collapsing a continent, and maybe you'll get a little attention." Vernaccus could become pretty angry. He didn't come very close to collapsing the continent of Tamriel, but it wasn't for lack of trying. A hero was needed to face the mad daedra, and fortunately, one was available. His name was Bourlor, and it was said that he had been blessed by the goddess Kynareth. That was the only explanation for his inhuman accuracy with his bow and arrow, for he never missed a target. As a child he had driven his marksmanship tutors wild with frustration. They would tell him how to plant his feet, how to nock a bolt, the proper grip for the cord, the best method of release. He ignored all the rules, and somehow, every time, the arrow would catch a breath of wind and sail directly to his target. It did not matter if the quarry was moving or still, at very close range or miles away. Whatever he wanted to strike with his arrow would be struck. Bourlor answered the call when one of the village mayors begged him for help. Unfortunately, he was not as great a horseman as he was an archer. As he rode through the forest toward the mayor's town, a place called Evensacon, Vernaccus was already murdering everyone there. Horavatha watched, and stifled back a yawn. "Murdering a small town mayor isn't going to put you in famous company, you know. What you need is a great champion to defeat. Someone like Ysgramor or Pelinal Whitestrake or--" she stared at the figure emerging from the forest. "That fellow!" "Who's he?" growled Vernaccus between bites of the mayor's quivering body. "The greatest archer in Tamriel. He's never missed." Bourlor had his bow strung and was pointing it at the daedra. For a moment, Vernaccus felt like laughing -- the fellow was not even aiming straight -- but he had a well-honed sense of self-preservation. There was something about the man's look of confidence that convinced the daedra that Horavatha wasn't lying. As the bolt left the bow, Vernaccus vanished in a sheet of flame. The arrow impaled a tree. Bourlor stood and stared. He had missed a target. In Oblivion, Vernaccus raged. Fleeing before a mortal man like that -- not even the basest scamp would have been so craven. He had exposed himself for the weak, cowardly creature he was. As he considered what steps to take to salvage the situation, he found himself face-to-knee with the most fearsome of the Daedra Princes, Molag Bal. "I never thought anything much of you, Vernaccus," the giant boomed. "But you have more than proven your worth. You have shown the creatures of Mundus that the daedra are more powerful than the blessings of the Gods." The other denizens of Oblivion quickly agreed (as they always did) with the view of Molag Bal. The daedra are, after all, always very sensitive about their various defeats at the hands of mortal champions. Vernaccus was proclaimed The Elusive Beast, The Unpursuable One, He Who Cannot Be Touched, The Bane of Kynareth. Shrines devoted to him began to be built in remote corners of Morrowind and Skyrim. Bourlor meanwhile, now found flawed, was never again called to rescue a village. He was so heartbroken over his failure to strike his target that he became a hermit, and never restrung his bow again. Some months later, he died, unmourned and unremembered. "Is this really the tale you thought would cheer me?" asked Hallgerd incredulously. "I've heard the King of Worms told more inspirational stories." "Wait," smiled Xiomara. "I'm not finished yet." For a year's time, Vernaccus was content to watch his legend grow and his fledging worship spread from his home in Oblivion. He was, in addition to being cowardly and inclined toward murderous rages, also a very lazy creature. His worshippers told tales of their Master avoiding the bolts of a thousand archers, of moving through oceans without getting wet, and other feats of avoidance that he would rather not have to demonstrate in person. The real story of his ignominious retreat from Bourlor was thankfully forgotten. The bad news, when it came, was delivered to him with some relish by Horavatha. He had delighted in her jealousy at his growing reputation, so it was with a cruel smile she told him, "Your shrines are being assaulted." "Who dares?" he roared. "Everyone who passes them in the wilderness feels the need to throw a stone," Horavatha purred. "You can hardly blame them. After all, they represent He Who Cannot Be Touched. How could anyone be expected to resist such a target?" Vernaccus peered through the veil into the world of Mundus and saw that it was true. One of his shrines in Colovian West country was surrounded by a large platoon of mercenary soldiers, who delighted in pelting it with rocks. His worshippers huddled inside, praying for a miracle. In an instant, he appeared before the mercenaries and his rage was terrifying to behold. They fled into the woods before he even had a chance to murder one of them. His worshippers threw open the wooden door to the shrine and dropped to their knees in joy and fear. His anger melted. Then a stone struck him. Then another. He turned to face his assailants, but the air was suddenly filled with rocks. Vernaccus could not see them, but he heard mercenaries in the woods laugh, "It's not even trying to move out of the way!" "It's impossible not to hit him!" guffawed another. With a roar of humiliation, the daedra bounded into the shrine, chased by the onslaught. One of the stones knocked the door closed behind him, striking him in the back. His face broke, anger and embarrassment disappearing, replaced by pain. He turned, shaking, to his worshippers who huddled in the shadows of the shrine, their faith shattered. "Where did you get the wood to build this shrine?" Vernaccus groaned. "Mostly from an copse of trees near the village of Evensacon," his high-priest shrugged. Vernaccus nodded. He dropped forward, revealing the deep wound in his back. A rusted arrowhead buried in a whorl in the wood of the door had jolted loose in the assault and impaled him. The daedra vanished in a whirlwind of dust. The shrines were abandoned shortly thereafter, though Vernaccus did have a brief resurgence as the Patron Spirit of Limitations and Impotence before fading from memory altogether. The legend of Bourlor himself never became very well known either, but there are still some who tell the tale, like myself. And we have the advantage of knowing what the Great Archer himself didn't know on his deathbed -- his final arrow found its target after all.

哈尔杰德在周六晚上踏进国王火腿酒馆，他脸色因悲伤而愁云密布。待他坐下点了杯格雷夫酒之后，老朋友加拉兹和肖玛拉与他坐到一起。 “出什么事了，哈尔杰德？”肖玛拉问。“你来得比平日晚，看着还一脸悲剧相。你是丢了钱还是…死了至亲好友？” 　　 “没丢钱，”哈尔杰德一脸苦相，“但我刚接到外甥来信，得知我表弟阿利奥齐去世了，他说他死得很自然，就是岁数大了。可阿利奥齐比我小十岁。” “噢，那真糟…不过这也是表明享受生活的一切可能是有多重要，毕竟你永远无法预知大限什么时候就到了。”加拉兹说，此前他在街角烟馆里同一把凳子上数小时没挪过屁股。他并非那种自我意识强烈的人。 　　 “人生苦短啊，”肖玛拉附议，“但如果你别想得这么伤感，我们中没几个人知晓人死后有何影响。这样说也许你会感觉宽慰点。说起来…我有没有跟你讲过维纳科斯和波罗尔的传说？” 　　 “应该是没说过。”哈尔杰德说。 　　 “维纳科斯是个迪德拉。”肖玛拉边说边在壁炉炉床处滴了些飞令来营造理想的气氛，“虽这是个多年前的传说，但维纳科斯当下肯定还在，毕竟于永生不死的迪德拉而言，时间又算什么？” 　　 “事实上，”加拉兹打岔，“我理解永生的概念是…” 　　 “我正尝试给咱们需要安抚的朋友讲个激励精神的故事，”肖玛拉低吼，“不介意的话请别打断，我可没打算花他妈一整晚来念叨这个故事。” 　　 你多半没听过维纳科斯这名字，”肖玛拉暂且搁置不朽这个主题，“就算在他攀上力量和名望的巅峰后，当年的高标准，他还是被视为软弱的存在。显然，人们对他毫无敬畏这点深深激怒了他，接续的反应和那种典型的'低等迪德拉'毫无二致。他开始暴戾地散播怒火。 　　 不久邪恶恐怖的消息传遍了科洛文西部每座村庄。灭门惨案、城堡毁灭，果园与田地受到焚烧诅咒，再也长不出庄稼。 为了让村民的处境雪上加霜，维纳科斯在湮灭时的旧敌前来拜访，她是个黑暗诱惑者，名唤哈拉瓦萨。她很爱嘲弄他，然后看能把他激怒到什么程度。 　　 “淹了个村就觉得自己行了？”她讥讽道，“怎么不试试毁掉整片大陆啊，说不定那时你会有点热度。” 　　 维纳科斯陷入极端狂怒了。虽说他并没有毁掉泰姆瑞尔大陆，但这不代表他没有尝试过。 　　 世界需要英雄与这疯狂的迪德拉正面对决。幸亏确有一位。 　　 他叫波罗尔，人们说他曾蒙凯娜瑞丝女神赐福，唯一能解释他箭术超凡，百发百中的原因了。在他幼年时曾令其箭法导师们懊丧欲疯。他们教授他如何摆正双脚，怎样认扣搭弦，何时撒手放箭。而他无视了所有规则，但他的箭却不知为何，每次都能乘风而去，直中目标。无论猎物或岿然不动或健步如飞，或远在天边或近在眼前。他的箭都能凭心意射中。 　　 波罗尔响应了一位镇长的求援。然而非常不幸，他骑术的造诣远不如箭术。当他骑越森林到那镇长所辖，一个叫做艾文斯康的小镇时，那里的人已被维纳科斯杀得一干二净。哈拉瓦萨在旁看得强忍哈欠。 　　 “杀个小村长怎可能让你更有名，你不会不知道吧？你起码得击破一位强大的勇士。比如伊斯格拉默或‘白轮’佩林纳尔什么的，或者——”她凝视正穿林而来的人影说，“那家伙！” 　　 “他是谁？”维纳科斯一边啃着镇长还在颤抖的尸体，一边咆哮。 　　 “泰姆瑞尔最强的弓箭手，百发百中。” 波罗尔引弓指向迪德拉。那一瞬间，维纳科斯甚至想笑——这小子甚至都没瞄准——但他有一种久经磨练的自我保护意识。这人自信的神情令他确信哈拉瓦萨绝无虚言。箭矢离弦之时，维纳科斯于火炎帷幕中匿去身形。 　 箭刺穿了一棵树。波罗尔止步凝望。他竟然错过了目标。 　　 在湮灭中，维纳科斯怒火中烧。在凡人面前逃跑——就是最低劣的邋遢鬼都不会这么胆怯。他已充分暴露出他自己是个怯懦没用的脆弱生物。当他正考虑如何挽救局面时，他发现自己面前是迪德拉君王中最可怕的莫拉格·巴尔，而自己刚好面向他的膝盖。 “我从未看重过你，维纳科斯，”巨神开口如轰鸣，“但你已证明自己的价值远不止于尔尔。你向梦达思的众生表明，我迪德拉比众圣灵的祝福更胜一筹。” 　　 湮灭的其他居民也迅速附议（他们总是这样）莫拉格·巴尔的观点。迪德拉们长久以来都对他们在凡人勇士之手的各种失败深为敏感。维纳科斯被赞颂为难以捉摸的狂兽，不可追寻者，无法触及者，凯娜瑞丝之祸。敬奉他的神殿开始在晨风和天际的偏远地区修建起来。 　　 同一时间，被发觉有缺陷的波罗尔，再没有呼唤他去拯救村镇的请求了，他因未能射中目标伤心欲绝，索性洗手归隐，此后再不上弦。数月后他逝世了，无人哀悼也无人追忆。 　　 “你竟然认为讲这种故事能让我打起精神？”哈尔杰德难以置信，“蠕虫之王讲故事都比这鼓舞人心。” “稍安勿躁”肖玛拉莞尔。“我还没讲完。” 　　 下面的一年，维纳科斯满意地看着他的传奇传播得越来越广，他的崇拜自湮灭蔓延开来。但他除了懦弱、暴戾外，还是个非常懒惰的家伙。他的信徒诉说着他们的主能闪避足足一千个弓箭手的万箭齐发、能不沾滴水穿行大洋，及众多他不肯亲自表现的回避技艺。谢天谢地，他在面对波罗尔时的耻辱逃窜已无人知晓。 　　 但哈拉瓦萨津津有味地传给他一个坏消息。他乐于见到她嫉恨他日益名扬这点，因而她邪笑着告诉他，“你家神殿给攻击咯。” 　　 “谁敢？”他咆哮。 　　 “每个郊外路人都想着得朝它砸点石头，”哈拉瓦萨愉快地轻声说。“也难怪啊。它们象征‘无法触及者’。哪有人能忍住不打这样的靶子呢？” 　　 维纳科斯透过帷幕窥向梦达思，确信这都是事实。一座在科洛文西部郊外供奉他的神殿外围着一大排佣兵，他们不亦乐乎地向它投掷石块。信众躲在里面瑟瑟发抖，祈愿奇迹发生。 刹那间，他就出现在雇佣兵面前，展现自己暴虐的狂怒。但他还来不及杀死其中一个，人就都逃到树林里去了。信徒们敞开神殿木门，又敬又怕地叩拜。他感到火气渐渐平息。然后又有块飞石砸到他。 然后又一块。他转身面向冒犯者处，但空中顿时充满了飞石。 维纳科斯根本看不到他们，但他听到林中佣兵们在狂笑， “它压根不躲！” 　　 “这有什么打不到的！”另一个人狂笑。 　　 随着一声饱含耻辱的咆哮，迪德拉跳进神殿里躲避着追赶他的猛袭。有枚石块砸到了他背后的大门，大门撞击了他的背。他的脸被打破了，剧痛取代了愤懑和尴尬。他颤抖着转身，面对在神殿阴影下蜷缩一团的、信仰已然崩坏的信众。 　　 “你们建神殿是从哪里弄来的木材？”维纳科斯呻吟。 　　 “大多是从艾文斯康村附近的树林。”他的大祭司耸肩。 维纳科斯点点头。他向前俯身，展露他背上深创的伤口。深埋于木门年轮内一枚生锈箭镞在攻击引发的震动中掉了出来并刺透了他。迪德拉消失在一股旋流涡风刮起的尘埃内。 　　 那些神殿随后很快就被荒废了。尽管维纳科斯在完全消失于众人记忆前，确实有被当成局限与虚弱之神短暂复兴过。而波罗尔的传说也从未广为人知，但仍有些人像我一样在述说这故事。且重点是我们知道传说弓箭手到死都不知道的事——他的最后一箭还是射中目标了。

"Soap! The forest will eat love! Straight ahead! Stupid and a stupid cow!" The voice boomed out so suddenly that Decumus Scotti jumped. He stared off into the dim jungle glade from which he only heard animal and insect calls, and the low whistling of wind moments before. It was a queer, oddly accented voice of indiscriminate gender, tremulous in its modulations, but unmistakably human. Or, at very least, elven. An isolated Bosmer perhaps with a poor grasp of the Cyrodilic language. After countless hours of plodding through the dense knot of Valenwood jungle, any voice of slight familiarity sounded wondrous. "Hello?" he cried. "Beetles on any names? Certainly yesterday yes!" the voice called back. "Who, what, and when, and mice!" "I'm afraid I don't understand," replied Scotti, turning toward the brambled tree, thick as a wagon, where the voice had issued. "But you needn't be afraid of me. My name is Decumus Scotti. I'm a Cyrodiil from the Imperial City. I came here to help rebuild Valenwood after the war, you see, and now I'm rather lost." "Gemstones and grilled slaves ... The war," moaned the voice and broke down into sobs. "You know about the war? I wasn't sure, I wasn't even sure how far away from the border I am now," Scotti began slowly walking toward the tree. He dropped Reglius's satchel to the ground, and held out his empty hands. "I'm unarmed. I only want to know the way to the closest town. I'm trying to meet my friend, Liodes Jurus, in Silvenar." "Silvenar!" the voice laughed. It laughed even louder as Scotti circled the tree. "Worms and wine! Worms and wine! Silvenar sings for worms and wine!" There was nothing to be found anywhere around the tree. "I don't see you. Why are you hiding?" In frustration born of hunger and exhaustion, he struck the tree trunk. A sudden shiver of gold and red erupted from a hollow nook above, and Scotti was surrounded by six winged creatures scarcely more than a few inches long. Bright crimson eyes were set on either side of tunnel-like protuberances, the animals' always open mouths. They were legless, and their thin, rapidly beating, aureate wings seemed poorly constructed to transport their fat, swollen bellies. And yet, they darted through the air like sparks from a fire. Whirling about the poor clerk, they began chattering what he now understood to be perfect nonsense. "Wines and worms, how far from the border am I! Academic garnishments, and alas, Liodes Jurus!" "Hello, I'm afraid I'm unarmed? Smoken flames and the closest town is dear Oblivion." "Swollen on bad meat, an indigo nimbus, but you needn't be afraid of me!" "Why are you hiding? Why are you hiding? Before I begin to friend, love me, Lady Zuleika!" Furious with the mimics, Scotti swung his arms, driving them up into the treetops. He stomped back to the clearing and opened up the satchel again, as he had done some hours before. There was still, unsurprisingly, nothing useful in the bag, and nothing to eat in any corner or pocket. A goodly amount of gold (he smiled grimly, as he had done before, at the irony of being financially solvent in the jungle), a stack of neat blank contracts from Lord Vanech's building commission, some thin cord, and an oiled leather cloak for bad weather. At least, Scotti considered, he had not suffered rain. A rolling moan of thunder reminded Scotti of what he had suspected for some weeks now. He was cursed. Within an hour's time, he was wearing the cloak and clawing his way through mud. The trees, which had earlier allowed no sunlight in, provided no shelter against the pounding storm and wind. The only sounds that pierced the pelting of the rain were the mocking calls of the flying creatures, flitting just above, babbling their nonsense. Scotti bellowed at them, threw rocks, but they seemed enamored of his company. While he was reaching to grab a promising looking stone to hurl at his tormentors, Scotti felt something shift beneath his feet. Wet but solid ground suddenly liquefied and became a rolling tide, rushing him forward. Light as a leaf, he flew head over feet over head, until the mudflow dropped and he continued forward, plunging down into a river twenty-five feet below. The storm passed quite as instantly as it had arrived. The sun melted the dark clouds and warmed Scotti as he swam for the shore. There, another sign of the Khajiiti incursion into Valenwood greeted him. A small fishing village had stood there once, so recently extinct that it smoldered like a still-warm corpse. Dirt cairns that had once housed fish by the smell of them had been ravaged, their bounty turned to ash. Rafts and skiffs lay broken, scuttled, half-submerged. All the villagers were no more, either dead or refugees far away. Or so he presumed. Something banged against the wall of one of the ruins. Scotti ran to investigate. "My name is Decumus Scotti?" sang the first winged beast. "I'm a Cyrodiil from? The Imperial City? I came here to help rebuild Valenwood after the war, you see, and now I'm rather lost?" "I swell to maculate, apeneck!" agreed one of its companions. "I don't see you. Why are you hiding?" As they fell into chattering, Scotti began to search the rest of the village. Surely the cats had left something behind, a scrap of dried meat, a morsel of fish sausage, anything. But they had been immaculate in their complete annihilation. There was nothing to eat anywhere. Scotti did find one item of possible use under the tumbled remains of a stone hut. A bow and two arrows made of bone. The string had been lost, likely burned away in the heat of the fire, but he pulled the cord from Reglius's satchel and restrung it. The creatures flew over and hovered nearby as he worked: "The convent of the sacred Liodes Jurus?" "You know about the war! Worms and wine, circumscribe a golden host, apeneck!" The moment the cord was taut, Scotti nocked an arrow and swung around, pulling the string tight against his chest. The winged beasts, having had experience with archers before, shot off in all directions in a blur. They needn't have bothered. Scotti's first arrow dove into the ground three feet in front of him. He swore and retrieved it. The mimics, having likewise had experience with poor archers before, returned at once to hovering nearby and mocking Scotti. On his second shot, Scotti did much better, in purely technical terms. He remembered how the archers in Falinesti looked when he pulled himself out from under the hoarvor tick, and they were all taking aim at him. He extended his left hand, right hand, and right elbow in a symmetrical line, drawing the bow so his hand touched his jawline, and he could see the creature in his sight like the arrow was a finger he was pointing with. The bolt missed the target by only two feet, but it continued on its trajectory, snapping when it struck a rock wall. Scotti walked to the river's edge. He had only one arrow left, and perhaps, he considered, it would be most practical to find a slow-moving fish and fire it on that. If he missed, at least there was less of a chance of breaking the shaft, and he could always retrieve it from the water. A rather torpid, whiskered fish rolled by, and he took aim at it. "My name is Decumus Scotti!" one of the creatures howled, frightening the fish away. "Stupid and a stupid cow! Will you dance a dance in fire!" Scotti turned and aimed the arrow as he had done before. This time, however, he remembered to plant his feet as the archers had done, seven inches apart, knees straight, left leg slightly forward to meet the angle of his right shoulder. He released the last arrow. The arrow also proved a serviceable prong for roasting the creature against the smoking hot stones of one of the ruins. Its other companions had disappeared instantly after the beast was slain, and Scotti was able to dine in peace. The meat proved to be delicious, if scarcely more than a first course. He was picking the last of it from the bones, when a boat sailed into view from around the bend of the river. At the helm were Bosmer sailors. Scotti ran to the bank and waved his arms. They averted their eyes and continued past. "You bloody, callous bastards!" Scotti howled. "Knaves! Hooligans! Apenecks! Scoundrels!" A gray-whiskered form came out from a hatch, and Scotti immediately recognized him as Gryf Mallon, the poet translator he had met in the caravan from Cyrodiil. He peered Scotti's direction, and his eyes lit up with delight, "Decumus Scotti! Precisely the man I hoped to see! I want to get your thoughts on a rather puzzling passage in the Mnoriad Pley Bar! It begins 'I went weeping into the world, searching for wonders,' perhaps you're familiar with it?" "I'd like nothing better than to discuss the Mnoriad Pley Bar with you, Gryf!" Scotti called back. "Would you let me come aboard though first?" Overjoyed at being on a ship bound for any port at all, Scotti was true to his word. For over an hour as the boat rolled down the river past the blackened remnants of Bosmeri villages, he asked no questions and spoke nothing of his life over the past weeks: he merely listened to Mallon's theories of merethic Aldmeri esoterica. The translator was undemanding of his guest's scholarship, accepting nods and shrugs as civilized conversation. He even produced some wine and fish jelly, which he shared with Scotti absent-mindedly, as he expounded on his various theses. Finally, while Mallon was searching for a reference to some minor point in his notes, Scotti asked, "Rather off subject, but I was wondering where we're bound." "The very heart of the province, Silvenar," Mallon said, not looking up from the passage he was reading. "It's somewhat bothersome, actually, as I wanted to go to Woodhearth first to talk to a Bosmer there who claims to have an original copy of Dirith Yalmillhiad, if you can believe it. But for the time being, that has to wait. Summurset Isle has surrounded the city, and is in the process of starving the citizenry until they surrender. It's a tiresome prospect, since the Bosmeri are happy to eat one another, so there's a risk that at the end, only one fat wood elf will remain to wave the flag." "That is vexing," agreed Scotti, sympathetically. "To the east, the Khajiiti are burning everything, and to the west, the High Elves are waging war. I don't suppose the borders to the north are clear?" "They're even worse," replied Mallon, finger on the page, still distracted. "The Cyrodiils and Redguards don't want Bosmer refugees streaming into their provinces. It only stands to reason. Imagine how much more criminally inclined they'd be now that they're homeless and hungry." "So," murmured Scotti, feeling a shiver. "We're trapped in Valenwood." "Not at all. I need to leave fairly shortly myself, as my publisher has set a very definite deadline for my new book of translations. From what I understand, one merely petitions to the Silvenar for special border protection and one can cross into Cyrodiil with impunity." "Petition the Silvenar, or petition at Silvenar?" "Petition the Silvenar at Silvenar. It's an odd nomenclature that is typical of this place, the sort of thing that makes my job as a translator that much more challenging. The Silvenar, he, or rather they are the closest the Bosmeri have to a great leader. The essential thing to remember about the Silvenar --" Mallon smiled, finding the passage he was looking for, "Here! 'A fortnight, inexplicable, the world burns into a dance.' There's that metaphor again." "What were you saying about the Silvenar?" asked Scotti. "The essential thing to remember?" "I don't remember what I was saying," replied Mallon, turning back to his oration. In a week's time, the little boat bumped along the shallow, calmer waters of the foaming current the Xylo had become, and Decumus Scotti first saw the city of Silvenar. If Falinesti was a tree, then Silvenar was a flower. A magnificent pile of faded shades of green, red, blue, and white, shining with crystalline residue. Mallon had mentioned off-hand, when not otherwise explaining Aldmeri prosody, that Silvenar had once been a blossoming glade in the forest, but owing to some spell or natural cause, the trees' sap began flowing with translucent liqueur. The process of the sap flowing and hardening over the colorful trees had formed the web of the city. Mallon's description was intriguing, but it hardly prepared him for the city's beauty. "What is the finest, most luxurious tavern here?" Scotti asked one of the Bosmer boatmen. "Prithala Hall," Mallon answered. "But why don't you stay with me? I'm visiting an acquaintance of mine, a scholar I think you'll find fascinating. His hovel isn't much, but he has the most extraordinary ideas about the principles of a Merethic Aldmeri tribe the Sarmathi --" "Under any other circumstances, I would happily accept," said Scotti graciously. "But after weeks of sleeping on the ground or on a raft, and eating whatever I could scrounge, I feel the need for some indulgent creature comforts. And then, after a day or two, I'll petition the Silvenar for safe passage to Cyrodiil." The men bade each other goodbye. Gryf Mallon gave him the address of his publisher in the Imperial City, which Scotti accepted and quickly forgot. The clerk wandered the streets of Silvenar, crossing bridges of amber, admiring the petrified forest architecture. In front of a particularly estimable palace of silvery reflective crystal, he found Prithala Hall. He took the finest room, and ordered a gluttonous meal of the finest quality. At a nearby table, he saw two very fat fellows, a man and a Bosmer, remarking how much finer the food was there than at the Silvenar's palace. They began to discuss the war and some issues of finances and rebuilding provincial bridges. The man noticed Scotti looking at them, and his eyes flashed recognition. "Scotti, is that you? Kynareth, where have you been? I've had to make all the contacts here on my own!" At the sound of his voice, Scotti recognized him. The fat man was Liodes Jurus, vastly engorged.

斯科提被这些模仿者激怒了，挥舞起胳膊，试图用力去够树梢。随后，正如他几小时前所做那般，他怒气沉重地几步跺回空地，再次打开了背包。他翻遍包里每一个角落或者内袋，不出意料没有找到任何堪用之物或是食物。一大把金币（他露出苦笑，恰如他之前所做那般，嘲笑着荒郊野林中却能有钱还债的讽刺），一叠来自瓦内奇大人建筑委会光洁空白的合同，一些细绳，一件为恶劣天气准备的油性革制斗篷。斯科提思衬着，至少他不用再淋雨了。 一阵滚滚雷鸣般的咆哮让斯科提回想起了数周前他所怀疑的事情。他被诅咒了。 一小时之间，他披上了斗篷，在泥浆中艰难缓行。先前遮天蔽日的树丛却不能地抵御烈风怒雷交相侵伐。那穿透了倾泻而下的雨幕的唯一声音，便是那些飞至前方聒噪喉舌的飞行生物发出的讥嘲之声。斯科提冲着他们怒喝出声，投掷石块，但它们似乎却迷上了和他相伴的感觉。 当他伸手去抓住一块很有可能形似石头的物事，来投石反击折磨着他的生物时，斯科提感到脚下有什么东西在快速移动。湿润却坚固的地面猝然化成液态，接着便翻卷起滚滚浪潮，裹挟着他冲刷而前。在洪波中轻如一叶的斯科提感到上下颠倒，直到泥石流冲势渐竭，而他还在朝前运动着，猛然跌进了下方二十五尺远的一条河里。 风暴来得快去得麻利。日光熔开漫天乌云，为游到岸边的斯科提洒下一身暖意。在那里，斯科提视野中出现了另一处卡吉特入侵威伦森林的迹象。这里曾经伫立着一座渔村，它刚刚覆灭，像一具还在燃烧的尸体。曾用于储存渔获的屋舍毁于一旦，化作火后尘堆，如今只能凭借其残存的鱼腥气味判断出原貌，内中满仓的渔获也尽数燎为余烬。木筏破损、划艇残坏，或沉伏水底、或半浮水面。村中荒无人烟，居民非死即逃，远离此地。他心中所猜测的大抵如是。有物件被猛地砸在废墟中的一面墙壁上。斯科提跑过去一探究竟。 “我的名字是戴奎莫斯·斯科提？”第一头体生双翅的野兽叫嚣如歌。“我是一个希罗帝尔来的？帝都？我来此帮助重建战后的威伦森林，如你所见，而现在我有点迷了路？” “我肿胀得长出了瘢点，猩猩脖！”它的一个同伴表示赞同。“我看不到你。你为什么躲起来？” 在他们陷入饶舌争论时，斯科提开始搜索起了村庄其余的部分。显然，那些大猫们在它们身后遗留下了什么东西，零星的碎肉干、几截鱼肉香肠，或者任何食物。然而它们成功将歼灭战推行到底。在任何地方都搜寻不到食物。在一座坍倒的石屋废墟下，斯科提的确发现了一件可能派得上用场的物件。一把弯弓，两支骨制箭。那弓缺了弦，很有可能是被火焰烧去，但他从雷格利乌斯的背包中取出绳索，为弓重新上好了弦。 那些生物飞过斯科提，在他搜寻时徘徊四周：“圣利奥德斯·朱鲁斯的女隐修院？” “你是知道这战事的！蠕虫和红酒，约束了一位金色的主人，猩猩脖！” 弓弦绷紧的一刻，斯科提一箭搭在弦上，身子一转，将弓弦反引到心口。那些和弓手打过交道的有翼野兽顿时速度一振，四散奔逃，留下残影数道。然而它们也无需费力逃亡。斯科提的第一箭就在他面前入地三尺。他咒骂着拔回了箭。那些善于效仿的生物同样也见识过箭术稀松的弓手，它们立即折返回来，于四周徘徊飞行，句句针对着斯科提不断嘲讽。 仅从技艺角度来看，他的第二箭成效要好得多。他回忆起了自己从食脑虫身下爬出来时，目睹到的法林纳斯提弓手们的姿态，而他们当时正全部瞄准了他自己。他逐次伸出左右手掌，接着是右手肘以一条对称的轨迹反拉弓弦，直到手能刚好接触到他的下颔，此时他能清晰地于视野中看见那生物，且箭矢正如自己指物的手指一般。箭矢仅仅与目标错开两尺，然而箭矢沿着划过的轨迹继续前进，直到叩击在一面石墙上后，脆响一声，断裂开来。 斯科提朝着河岸迈步走了过去。他身上只剩一支箭，并且他认为去找些游速缓慢的鱼并射中它，很有可能更加符合实际。若他错失目标，至少箭杆断裂的机率要小上一些，他还一直能从水中取回箭矢。一条动作相当迟缓，生有鱼须的鱼翻转着身体游过，他便将弓箭对准了它。 “我的名字是戴奎莫斯·斯科提！”那群生物中的一只嗥叫一声，惊走了那条鱼。“蠢货和傻母牛！你会在火中舞蹈着舞步吗？” 斯科提转身将箭对准了目标，恰如向前所做一般。然而这一次，他记住将双脚放置得和那些弓手一样，两脚间隔七寸，膝盖打直，左腿微微前伸，以此匹配右肩的倾斜角度。接着，他开弓射出最后一箭。 这一箭同样建功，它将那生物钉在了废墟中发烟的灼烫岩石上，让那生物惨遭炮烙。那生物的其它同伙在这头野兽遭到屠戮后立即消失不见，斯科提则终于得以安静下来用餐。那些肉尝起来甚为美，但量却没比一道开胃小菜多得了多少。在一艘小艇从河弯处周围驶入视野中时，他正从骨头上剥下最后一块肉。船舵上立着波斯莫水手们。斯科提挥动着手臂趋向河岸。他们目光闪躲着继续驾船驶过了斯科提。 “你们这些天杀的冷血杂碎！”斯科提大喊大叫。“无赖！流氓！猩猩脖！恶棍！” 一个须发灰白的人影从舱口走出，斯科提立即认出了这是格兰夫·马伦，这位诗歌翻译家曾与他在来自希罗帝尔的车队有过一面之缘。 他朝着斯科提的方向瞥了眼，眼中亮起了愉悦的光芒，“戴奎莫斯·斯科提！这不就是我要找的人嘛！我正想问问你是怎么理解《穆恩莱德·普利·巴尔》里那段莫名其妙的话呢！它的开头就是‘我于世界中垂泪，寻觅奇迹，’你可能对这段蛮熟悉？” “我也很想和你一起探讨《穆恩莱德·普利·巴尔》，格兰夫！”斯科提回答道。“不过，你可以让我先登上船吗？” 登上了一艘驶会向任何港口的船，斯科提都倍感喜出望外，遵守了他的诺言。在船随波荡漾、沿河顺流而下穿过波斯莫村落一片焦黑的废墟期间，斯科提没有问任何问题，也对自己这几周以来的生活只字未提，他只是听着马伦讲述着关于精灵纪元奥德莫语秘笈的理论，如此持续了一小时有余。这位翻译家对他的听众没有太多学术造诣的要求，将斯科提的点头和耸肩看作礼貌对话的表征。他甚至拿来了一些红酒和鱼肉冻，一边全心全意阐述着他浩繁的论文，一边漫不经心地和斯科提分享食物。 最终，在马伦寻找着他笔记里某一次要论点的参考资料时，斯科提发问道：“请允许我打个岔，但我很想知道，这次我们的船将去往何方。” “该行省的中枢腹心之地，希尔维纳，”马伦应道，头也不抬地读着他的文章。“这事情确实有些困扰纠结，因为我现在想去森炉，和那的一位自称有《迪瑞斯·雅密尔希亚德》原抄本的波斯莫先行会谈，虽然真实性不清楚。但目前来看，这事情得先放放。夏暮岛已经包围了那城市，目前正在断绝粮食，通过困得全城百姓不堪饥饿来迫降。这事情的发展会变得相当恼火，因为波斯莫们很乐于同类相食，所以很有可能存在最后仅存一只吃得脑满肠肥的木精灵在那里摇白旗的风险。” “那确实挺闹心的。”斯科提同情地表示赞同。“在东边的卡吉特们焚烧了所有东西，在西边的高精灵们也在发起战争。在北部的边境线还没打通吧？” “它们那只会更糟，”马伦回答道，手指搭在书页上，依然分神顾盼书籍。“希罗帝尔人和红卫人不愿让波斯莫难民们流入他们的省内。这事也合理。想象一下那些难民们现在无家可归、饥肠辘辘的情况，他们的犯罪倾向会有多大。” “所以，”斯科提感受到了一阵战栗，嗫嚅出声：“我们被困在威伦森林了。” “不尽然。我也需要尽快离开，因为我的出版商给我的翻译集著规定了非常严格的交稿期限。就我的理解来说，你只要向希尔维纳申请去进行特殊的边界保护，那么就能不受追咎的渡入希罗帝尔。” “向希尔维纳做申请，还是到希尔维纳做申请？” “到希尔维纳去向希尔维纳做申请。这种奇怪的命名法在这儿很常见，搞得我的翻译工作挑战性上升了不少。希尔维纳，他——或者说他们——是波斯莫当中最接近一位崇高领袖的存在。关于希尔维纳要记住的诀窍是——”马伦微微一笑，于他正在检阅的文章中一阵搜素，“这儿！‘历日十有四，其意难相知，世界焚作舞。’又是这个譬喻。” “你刚才说了什么希尔维纳的东西？”斯科提发问。“记住什么？” “我不记得刚才说了什么，”马伦回答道，又继续着他的说辞。 接下来的一周当中，小舟随波起伏，航行过已然泛沤一片的木河那稍显平静的浅水域，而戴奎莫斯·斯科提也首次目睹到了希尔维纳的城市景貌。若将法林纳斯提比作独木一棵，那么希尔维纳便是花卉一朵。碧赤青白，众采纷葩，其色如洗，耀以残晶。在马伦阐释奥德莫语韵律学的空档，他随口向斯科提说起过，希尔维纳曾经还是一片林间平野上的盛景，但出于某种咒语或者自然的因素，树汁间渗入了透亮的酒浆。树汁流经万色缤纷的森林并将其硬化的过程塑造了这座城市的网络。尽管马伦的描述听上去富于吸引力，但它基本上未能让斯科提先行领略这座城市之美。 “这里服务质量最上乘、最奢华的酒馆是哪家？”斯科提朝一个波斯莫船员问。 “普瑞萨拉之厅，”马伦回答道。“但你为何不住我这呢？我要去见我的一位熟人，一个我私以为你可能会觉得十分吸引人的学者。他那间陋室恐怕难以容下太多空间，但他有着极为出众的见解，是关于部落行事准则的，精灵纪元的奥德莫部落萨尔玛西——” “在其它情况下，我会欣然接受，“斯科提语气温和地说道。”但在连着数周过着卧地枕槎而眠、饥不择食的生活后，我迫切感受到需要来点放纵的物质享受。然后嘛，在接下来的一两天，我会向希尔维纳申请安全前往希罗帝尔。” 二人同彼此道别。格兰夫·马伦将自己在帝都的出版商的地址交给了斯科提，那份地址被斯科提收下，并很快抛诸脑后。这位文员在希尔维纳的街头漫步，度过琥珀质地的桥道，欣赏着静静矗立的丛林建筑。就在一处造价不菲、通体银光辉映的水晶宫前，他找到了普瑞萨拉之厅。 他订了一间最优质的房间，又点了一顿上乘食材烹制的饕餮盛宴。他在邻桌看见了两个身材肥硕的家伙，一个人类和一个波斯莫，对那里的食物如何胜过希尔维纳宫廷膳食评头论足。他们的话题开始转向战争以及经济上的问题与省内桥梁重修。那个男人注意到了斯科提正盯着他，眼中流露出一瞬间的会意。 “是你吗，斯科提？凯娜瑞丝在上，你去哪了？现在这里所有联系人的事，都只能全凭我自己！” 一听他的声音，斯科提就认出了他。那个大胖子正是利奥德斯·朱鲁斯。

n that early springtime morning, pale sunlight flickered behind the morning mist floating through the trees as Templer and Stryngpool made their way to the clearing. Neither had been back in High Rock, let alone in their favorite woods for four years. The trees had changed little even if they had. Stryngpool had a handsome blond moustache now, stiffened and spiked with wax, and Templer seemed to be a completely alien creature to the young lad who searched for adventure in the ancient grove. He was much quieter, as if scarred within as well as without. They each carried their bows and quivers with extra care as they maneuvered their way through the clusters of vine and branch. "This is the path that used to lead to your house, isn't it, old boy?" asked Stryngpool. Templer glanced at the overgrowth and nodded, before continuing on. "I thought so," said Stryngpool and laughed: "I remember it because you used to run down it every time you got a bloody nose. I know I can't offend you, but I have to say, it's hard to believe that you ended up a soldier." "How's your family?" asked Templer. "The same. A bit more pompous, if that's possible. It's obvious they wish I'd come back from the academy, but there's nothing much for me here. At least not until I collect my inheritance. Did I you see I got a gold ribbon of merit in archery?" "How could I miss it?" said Templer. "Oh yes, I nearly forgot that the family's put it in the Great Hall. Very ostentatiously. I suppose you can actually see it through the picture window. Silly, but I hope the peasants are impressed." The clearing opened up before them, where the mist settled on the grass, enveloping it in an opaque, chilly vapor. Burlap targets were arranged around in a semi-circle, several meters apart, like sentinels. "You've been practicing," observed Templer. "Well, a bit. I've only been back in town for a few days." said Stryngpool with a smile. "My parents said you got here a week ago?" "That's right. My unit's camped a few miles east, and I thought I'd visit the old haunts. A lot's changed, I could hardly recognize anything at all." Templer looked down at the valley below, to the vast empty tilled ground, stretching out for miles around. "It looks like a good planting." "My family's rather spread out since yours left. There was some discussion I think about keeping your old house up, but it seemed a little sentimental. Especially as there was fertile ground beneath." Stryngpool strung his bow carefully. It was a beautiful piece of art, darkest ebony and spun silver filigrees, hand-crafted for him in Wayrest. He looked over at Templer stringing his bow, and felt a twinge of pity. It was a sad, weathered utensil, bound together with strips of fabric. "If that's how they taught you to string your bow, you need some advisors from the academy in that army of yours," said Stryngpool as gently as he could. "The untightened loop is supposed to look like an X in an O. Yours looks like a Z in a Y." "It works for me," said Templer. "I should tell you, I won't be able to make an afternoon of this. I'm supposed to join my unit this evening." Stryngpool began to feel annoyed by his old friend. If he was angry about his family losing their land, why couldn't he just say it? Why did he come back to the valley at all? He watched Templer nock his first arrow, taking aim at a target, and coughed. "I'm sorry, but I can't in good faith send you back to the army without a little new wisdom. There are three types of draw, three-fingers, thumb and index, thumb and two fingers. Then there's the thumb draw which I like, but you see," Stryngpool showed Templer the small leather loop fastened on the cord of his bow, "You need to have one of these thingies or you'll tear your thumb right off." "I think I like my stupid method best." "Don't be pigheaded, Templer. They didn't give me the gold ribbon of merit for nothing. I had demonstrated shooting from under a shield, standing, sitting, squatting, kneeling, and sitting on horseback. This is practical information I'm imparting for the sake of our friendship which I, at least, haven't completely forgotten. Sweet Kynareth, I remember when you were just an oily little squirt, begging for this kind of honest guidance." Templer looked at Stryngpool for a moment, and lowered his bow. "Show me." Stryngpool relaxed, shook away the tensions that had been building. He did his exercise, drawing the bow back to his eyebrow, his moustache, his chest, his earlobe. "There are three ways of shooting: snatching and releasing in one continuous motion, like the Bosmer do; holding with a short draw and a pause before releasing like the Khajiit; and partial draw, pause, final draw," Stryngpool fired the arrow into the center of the target with cool precision, "And release. Which I prefer." "Very nice," said Templer. "Now you," said Stryngpool. He helped Templer select a grip, nock his arrow correctly, and take aim. A smile grew on Templer's face -- the first time Stryngpool had seen such a childlike expression on the war-etched visage all afternoon. When Templer released the arrow, it rocketed high over the top of the target and into the valley below where it disappeared from sight. "Not bad," said Templer. "No, not bad," said Stryngpool, feeling friendly once again. "If you practice, you should be able to focus your aim a little bit." The two shot a few more practice bolts before parting ways. Templer began the long trek east to his unit's camp, and Stryngpool wound his way down through the woods to the valley and his family's mansion. He hummed a little tune he learned at the academy as he passed the great lawn and walked up to the front door, pleased with himself for helping his old friend. It entirely escaped his attention that the large picture window was broken. But he noticed right away when he came into the Great Hall, and saw Templer's wild-shot bolt sticking in his gold ribbon of merit.

早春的清晨，微弱的阳光在树间飘荡的晨雾后闪烁，坦普勒跟斯特林普尔前往那片林间空地。四年以来他们二人都没有回过高岩，更别提回到他们最喜欢的树林了。四周的林木几乎看不出变化。如今斯特林普尔蓄起了漂亮的金色小胡子，用蜡定了型。而坦普勒则和以前那个喜欢在古老丛林寻求奇遇的少年判若两人。他沉默寡言，似乎心灵与外表一样都负有伤痕。 他们背着弓和箭袋，小心翼翼地穿越藤蔓和树枝。 “老伙计，这条路以前到你家是吧？” 斯特林普尔问道。 坦普勒瞥了眼郁郁葱葱的植物，点了点头，然后继续行进。 “我就知道，”斯坦林普尔说道，大笑起来，“我记得这儿，因为你每次受委屈的时候，都会顺着它跑回家。我知道我不该冒犯你，但我得说，不能相信你最后竟会去从军。” “你家里怎么样了？”坦普勒问。 “还是一样。如果可能的话，又浮夸了一点儿。他们显然希望我从学院回来，不过这里对我来说已经没什么了。至少在我拿到遗产之前没什么了。你知道我拿到箭术冠军金绸带了吗？” “我怎么会不知道啊？”坦普勒说。 “啊对，我都快忘了，我家里人把它挂大厅里了。特别招摇。你是透过落地窗看见的吧。很蠢，但我希望能给农夫们留下深刻印象。” 空地在他们面前展开，薄雾落在青草上，一切都笼罩在浑浊、冰冷的水汽之中。麻袋做成的靶子像哨兵般围成半圆，之间相隔数米。 “你一直在练习啊。”坦普勒观察道。 “呃，一点点。我才回镇子几天，” 斯坦林普尔微笑着说，“我爸妈说你一周前就来了吧？” “对的。我们部队在东边几里扎营了，我觉得我得拜访拜访老家。变化真大，我差不多什么都认不出来了。”坦普勒俯瞰下方的谷地，大片空阔的耕地延绵数里，“地似乎种得不赖。” “自从你们家走后，我家的土地就不断扩大。关于保留你的老宅还有一场讨论，不过似乎有点多愁善感。尤其是那下面的土壤很肥沃。” 斯坦林普尔小心地给弓上弦。那是一件精美的艺术品，在途歇城由最黑的黑檀和银丝装饰手工制成。他瞧了瞧正在系弓的坦普勒，心生一阵同情。那惨兮兮的破东西就是堆捆在一起的布条。 “如果你们部队是这样教你给弓上弦的，那他们可能得需要几个学院顾问了。” 斯坦林普尔尽量和气地说，“没有系紧的环套应该像X套在O里。你这个像Y套在Z里” “对我来说挺好使的。”坦普勒说，“我应该告诉你，我下午就不能呆了。今晚就得归队。” 斯坦林普尔开始觉得被他的老友惹恼了。要是他对他们家失去土地这件事耿耿于怀，为什么不直说？他为什么还回到谷地？他看着坦普勒瞄准目标射出第一箭，然后咳嗽了几下。 “抱歉，不过如果我没教你点新学问就把你送回部队的话，我可就名声不保了。拉弓的方式有三种，三指拉弓，拇指和食指拉弓，拇指和两指拉弓。然后我喜欢拇指拉弓，但你看，” 斯坦林普尔向坦普勒展示了系在弓上的小皮环，“你需要这么个东西，不然你的大拇指会被划掉的。” “我还是最喜欢我的蠢路子。” “别倔了，坦普勒。我的金绸带不是白拿的。我曾演示过扛盾射，立射，坐射，蹲射，跪射，还有骑射。我是看在我们的友谊上才教给你这些实用的知识的，至少我还没完全忘记这份友谊。亲爱的凯娜瑞丝啊，我还记得你只是一个拍马屁的小屁孩时，还求着要这种真诚的指导呢。” 坦普勒看看斯坦林普尔，然后放下了弓。“给我示范一下。” 斯坦林普尔放松了一下，甩掉一直以来的紧张感。他做了番演示，把弓拉到他的眉毛、胡子、胸部和耳垂。 “有三种射箭方式：像波斯莫那样，拉弓和放箭一气呵成；像卡吉特那样，快速拉弓，在放箭前顿一下；还有拉部分弓，停顿，拉满，” 斯坦林普尔射了一箭，精准地正中靶心，“再放箭。我喜欢这种。” “挺好。”坦普勒说。 “该你了。” 斯坦林普尔说。他帮着坦普了抓住握柄，正确地定好箭，然后找了个目标。坦普勒扬起一丝微笑——整个下午，斯坦林普尔第一次在那张饱经战烽的脸上看到那孩提般的微笑。当坦普勒放箭的时候，它高高地越过了目标上方，飞进了下面的谷地，从视野中消失了。 “不错。”坦普勒说。 “不，是还不坏。” 斯坦林普尔说，又一次感觉到友好的气氛，“如果你勤加练习，你的准头能更好一些。” 二人在分道扬镳前又练着射了几箭。坦普勒开始长途跋涉赶往东边驻军地，而斯坦林普尔蜿蜒穿过树林，回到他家的府邸。他哼着一曲他在学院里学到的小调，穿过草坪来到前门，他对自己帮助老友而感到很高兴。他完全没注意到巨大的落地窗已经破了。 不过当他进入大厅的时候，他立刻发现了，而且还看见坦普勒那发“乱射”的箭矢直直地插在他那冠军金绸带上。

RISLAV THE RIGHTEOUS By Sinjin

[pagebreak] [pagebreak]

ike all true heroes, Rislav Larich had inauspicious beginnings. We are told by chroniclers that the springtide night in the 448th year of the first era on which he was born was unseasonably cold, and that his mother Queen Lynada died very shortly after setting eyes upon her son. If he were much beloved of his father, King Mhorus of Skingrad, who already had plenty of heirs, three sons and four daughters before him, the chroniclers make no mention of it. His existence was so very undistinguished that we hear virtually nothing of him for the first twenty years of his life. His schooling, we can suppose, was similar to that of any "spare prince" in the Colovian West, with Ayleid tutors to teach him the ways of hunting and battle. Etiquette, religious instruction, and even basic statecraft were seldom a part of the training of a prince of the Highlands, as it was in the more civilized valley of Nibenay. There is a brief reference to him, together with his family, as part of the rolls of honor during the coronation of the Emperor Gorieus on the 23rd of Sun's Dawn 1E 461. The ceremony, of course, held during the time of the Alessian Doctrines of Marukh, and so was without entertainment, but the thirteen-year-old Rislav was still witness to some of the greatest figures of legend. The Beast of Anequina, Darloc Brae, represented his kingdom, giving honor to the Empire. The Chieftain of Skyrim Kjoric the White and his son Hoag were in attendance. And despite the Empire's intolerance of all elves, chimer Indoril Nerevar and dwemer Dumac Dwarfking were evidently there as well, diplomatically representing Resdayn, all in relative peace. Also mentioned on the rolls was a young mer in service to the Imperial court of High Rock, who was to have a great history with Rislav. Ryain Direnni. Whether the two young men of about the same age met and conversed is entirely the stuff of historian's fancy. Ryain is spoken of in praising words as a powerful land-owner, eventually buying the island of Balfiera in the Iliac Bay and gradually conquering all of High Rock and large parts of Hammerfell and Skyrim, but Rislav is not heard of again in history's books for another seventeen years. We can only offer supposition based on the facts that follow. Children of kings are, of course, married to the children of other kings to bind alliances. The kingdoms of Skingrad and Kvatch skirmished over common territory throughout the fifth century, until they reached a peace in the year 472. The details of this accord are not recorded, but since we know that Prince Rislav was in the court of Kvatch six years later, as husband to Belene, the daughter of King Justinius, it is fair to make an educated guess that they were married then to make peace. This brings us to the year 478, when a great plague swept through all of Cyrodiil and seemed particularly concentrated in the independent Colovian West. Among the victims were King Mhorus and the rest of the entire royal family in Skingrad. Rislav's only surviving elder brother, Dorald, survived, being in the Imperial City as a priest of Marukh. He returned to his homeland to assume the throne. Of Dorald, we have some history. The King's second son, he was slightly simple-minded and evidently very pious. All the chroniclers spoke of his sweetness and decency, how he saw a vision in his early years that brought him - with his father's blessing - from Skingrad to the Imperial City and the priesthood. The priesthood of Marukh, of course, saw no difference between spiritual and political matters. It was the religion of the Alessian Empire, and it taught that to resist the Emperor was to resist the Gods. Given that, it is scarcely a surprise what Dorald did when he became King of the independent kingdom of Skingrad. His first edict, on his very first day, was to cede the kingdom to the Empire. The reaction throughout the Colovian Estates was shock and outrage, nowhere more so than in the court of Kvatch. Rislav Larich, we are told, rode forth to his brother's kingdom, together with his wife and two dozen of his father-in-law's cavalry. It was surely not an impressive army, no matter how the chroniclers embellish it, but they had little trouble defeating all the guards Dorald sent to stop them. In truth, there was no actual battling, for the soldiers of Skingrad resented their new king's decision to give up their autonomy. The brothers faced one another in the castle courtyard where they had grown up. In typical Colovian fashion, there was no trial, no accusations of treason, no jury, no judge. Only an executioner. "Thou art no brother of mine," Rislav Larich said, and struck Dorald's head from his shoulders in one blow. He was crowned King of Skingrad still holding the same bloody axe in his arms. If King Rislav had no battle experience beforehand, that was shortly to change. Word spread quickly to the Imperial City that Skingrad, once offered, was now being taken back. Gorieus was an accomplished warrior even before taking the throne, and the seventeen years he had as Emperor were scarcely peaceful. Only eight months before Dorald's assassination and Rislav's ascendancy, Gorieus and the Alessian army had faced another of his coronation guests, Kjoric the White, on the fields of the frozen north. The High Chieftain of Skyrim lost his life in the Battle of Sungard. While the pact of chieftains was selecting a new leader, Cyrodiil was busily grabbing back the land of southern Skyrim that it had lost. In short, Emperor Gorieus knew how to deal with rebellious vassals. The Alessian army poured westward "like a flood of death," to borrow the chronicler's phrase, in numbers far exceeding what would be required to conquer Skingrad. Gorieus could not have thought actual battle was likely. Rislav, as we said, had little to no experience at warfare, and only a few days' practice at kingcraft. His kingdom and all of the Colovian West had just been ravaged by plague. The Alessians anticipated that a mere show of arms, and a surrender. Rislav instead prepared for battle. He quickly inspected his troops and drew up plans. The chroniclers who had heretofore ignored the life of Rislav now devote verse after verse describing the king's aspect with fetishistic delight. While it may lack literary merit and taste, we are at least given some details at last. Not surprisingly, the king wore the finest armor of his era, as the Colovian Estates then had the finest leathersmiths - the only type of armor available - in all of Tamriel. The king's klibanion mail, boiled and waxed for hardness, and studded with inch-long spikes, was a rich chestnut red, and he wore it over his black tunic but under his black cloak. The statue of Rislav the Righteous which now stands in Skingrad is a romanticized version of king, but not inaccurate except in the armor represented. No bard of the Colovian West would have gone to the market so lightly protected. But it does, as we will see, include the most important accouterments of Rislav: his trained hawk and his fast horse. The winter rains had washed through the roads to the south, sending much of the West Weald spilling into Valenwood. The Emperor took the northern route, and King Rislav with a small patrol of guards met him at a low pass on what is now the Gold Road. The Emperor's army, it is said, was so large that the Beast of Anequina could hear its march from hundreds of miles away, and despite himself, the chroniclers say, he quaked in fear. Rislav, it was said, did not quake. With perfect politeness, he told the Emperor that his party was too large to be accommodated in the tiny kingdom of Skingrad. "Next time," Rislav said. "Write before you come." The Emperor was, like most Alessian Emperors, not a man of great humor, and he thought Rislav touched by Sheogorath. He ordered his personal guards to arrest the poor madman, but at that moment, the King of Skingrad raised his arm and sent his hawk flying into the sky. It was a signal his army had been waiting for. The Alessian were all within the pass and the range of their arrows. King Rislav and his guard began riding westward as fast as if they had been "kissed by wild Kynareth," as the chroniclers said. He did not dare to look behind him, but his plan went faultlessly. The far eastern end of the pass was sealed by rolling boulders, giving the Alessian no direction to go but westward. The Skingrad archers rained arrows down upon the Imperial army from far above on the plateaus, remaining safe from reprisal. The furious Emperor Gorieus chased Rislav from the Weald to the Highlands, leaving Skingrad far behind, all the while his army growing steadily smaller and smaller. In the ancient Highland forest, the Imperial army met the army of Rislav's father-in-law, the King of Kvatch. The Alessian army likely still outnumbered their opponents, but they were exhausted and their morale had been obliterated by the chase amid a sea of arrows. After an hour's battle, they retreated north into what is now the Imperial Reserve, and from there, further north and east, to slip back to nurse their wounds and pride in Nibenay. It was the beginning of the end of the Alessian hegemony. The Kings of the Colovian West joined with Kvatch and Skingrad to resist Imperial incursions. The Clan Direnni under Ryain was inspired to outlaw the religion of the Alessian Reform throughout his lands in High Rock, and began pushing into Imperial territories. The new High Chief of Skyrim, Hoag, now called Hoag Merkiller, though sharing the Emperor's official xenophobia, also joined the resistance. His heir, King Ysmir Wulfharth of Atmora, helped continue the struggle upon Hoag's death in battle, and also insured his place in history. The heroic King of Skingrad, who faced the Emperor's army virtually alone, and triggered its end, justly deserves his sobriquet of Rislav the Righteous.

正义的瑞斯拉夫 辛金 著

一如所有真英雄般，瑞斯拉夫·拉里奇也有着不甚吉祥的开端。编年史显示，他生于第一纪元448年某个异常寒冷的春潮之夜。其母琳娜达王后只看过孩子一眼后不久就去世了。在他出生前，斯金格勒的莫霍卢斯王的继承人已有三子四女之多，而史书上并未有他独受父王宠爱的记录。 他的存在感稀薄到我们基本不知道他人生头二十年有什么事迹。可以推测，他受的教育训练和西科洛文那些“后备王子”别无二致，即由亚历德宫廷教师教授他狩猎和战斗。社交礼仪、宗教信仰乃至基本的治国之道几乎不会成为一位科洛文高地王子宫廷教育的一部分，这些都是文明程度更高的尼本奈河谷才有的。 有一段史料曾简短提及，他们一家曾出现在第一纪元461年日晓月23日举行的格里乌斯加冕礼的荣耀名册上。当然，该仪典是于马鲁克的阿莱西亚教义统治期间举办的，因而筵席上没什么娱乐活动。不过，时年13岁的少年瑞斯拉夫见证了不少传奇伟人的出席。“安内奎那野兽”达洛克·布瑞代其王国致祝帝国。天际的酋长“白发”柯乔里克及其子霍格也一并出席。另外，即使帝国排斥所有精灵，凯莫领袖因多瑞尔·尼瑞瓦及锻莫的“矮人王”杜马克显然也在嘉宾之列，代表瑞斯戴恩外交礼节性道贺。一切都处在相对的一团和气之中。 另外，名册上还提及一位隶属高岩皇室宫廷的青年精灵：莱恩·迪伦尼，他将与瑞斯拉夫开拓一段伟大的历史。 这两位同龄少年是否在宴会上相遇深谈，史学家们争论许久。于莱恩，后世评价满是溢美之词。他是一位强大的领主，最终购得髂骨湾的巴尔菲拉岛，随后逐步征服全高岩和落锤、天际大片土地。但在接下来的十七年里，瑞斯拉夫却在史书中销声匿迹。我们只可提出基于以下事实的猜想。 国王的子女通常要与其他王室子弟联姻以巩固盟国关系。于第五世纪，斯金格勒和科瓦奇两王国一直在因领土争议而爆发冲突，直至双方于472年停战和解。停战协议的细节并无记载，但我们知道，六年后瑞斯拉夫王子以贾斯汀尼乌斯王之女贝琳妮公主的丈夫身份登临科瓦奇王国宫廷。由此可知，他们的婚姻是此次议和的条件之一。 478年，一次大瘟疫席卷了整个希罗帝尔，而独立的西科洛文地区疫情尤其险恶，受害者就包括莫霍卢斯王及斯金格勒的剩余王室全员。而瑞斯拉夫唯一幸存的兄长，多拉德正在帝都当马鲁克的祭司，所以返回祖国继承了王位。 关于多拉德，我们有些许史料。他是先王次子，有点头脑简单，而同时显然很虔诚。所有的史家均称他和蔼可亲、为人正派，正因此他才于早年带着父王的祝福从斯金格勒出发，到帝都加入神职行列。当然了，在马鲁克的祭司行列里人人平等，不管成员的政治地位如何。而它是阿莱西亚帝国国教，教义里包括反抗皇帝即是反抗诸神。有鉴于此，多拉德在继任独立的斯金格勒王国新王之后的所作所为也就不足为奇了。 他登基首日的第一项法令就是宣布将王国纳入帝国版图。 全科洛文领地的反应都是又惊又怒，但尤其是身处科瓦奇宫廷里那位。据我们所知，瑞斯拉夫·拉里奇携其妻与岳父麾下的两打骑兵奔回兄长的王国。无论记注官们如何美化，但那肯定不是什么能让人印象深刻的部队，可他们几乎毫不费力就击破了多拉德全部遣来阻挠的卫兵队。实际上，根本没有战斗发生。因为斯金格勒的士兵也对新王放弃独立的法令感到不满。 兄弟俩在他们自幼一同长大的城堡庭院中直面彼此。 按科洛文的传统做法，没有审判，没有叛国罪指控，也没有陪审团和法官，只有一位处刑者。 “你不再是我的兄弟。”瑞斯拉夫说完，一斧把多拉德的首级从其肩上斩落。他被加冕为王时，手里还拿着那把斧头。 若此前瑞斯拉夫王毫无作战经验，那这个问题将很快地变化。关于刚刚要并入帝国的斯金格勒要重新独立的消息迅速传入帝都。格里乌斯在继位前已是高超的战士，且登基十七年来他几乎没有停歇，连年征战。就在多拉德被杀、瑞斯拉夫登基的八个月前，格里乌斯才领着阿莱西亚军队在寒冷的北方战场和加冕仪典的贵客“白发”柯乔里克打了一仗。在森加德之战中，天际的至高酋长战死了。当天际的酋长们忙于挑选新头领时，希罗帝尔已经着手夺回它损失的南天际土地了。 简单来说，格里乌斯皇帝很清楚该如何处理反叛的封臣。 借编年史家之语，阿莱西亚军“如死亡洪流般”奔涌西行，数量远远超过征服斯金格勒所需。格里乌斯甚至可能没想过会爆发真正的战斗。如前文所说，瑞斯拉夫基本可说是毫无战争经验，也基本不谙治国之道。他的王国及整个西科洛文才刚刚走出瘟疫的阴霾。阿莱西亚人判断这一次只是过去耀武扬威一番，瑞斯拉夫自然就要投降了。 而瑞斯拉夫却积极备战，迅速检阅了他的军队并完成了战争规划。 一直忽视瑞斯拉夫此前人生的史家们从这里开始满怀迷信的狂喜，用各种华丽辞藻描述这位国王的雄姿英发。也许这些部分缺乏文学价值和品味，但起码让我们知道了一些细节。瑞斯拉夫王毫不令人意外地穿上了在他的时代是最上等的盔甲——皮甲。因为彼时全泰姆瑞尔最佳的制革大师就在科洛文领地，而这也是当年唯一可以打造的盔甲。国王内着黑衣，外罩蒸煮打蜡的红栗寸刺克利巴尼翁铠甲，身披黑斗篷。现今，斯金格勒矗立的正义瑞斯拉夫像仅仅是一位被浪漫化的不准确形象，但甲胄部分除外。毕竟没有哪位西科洛文的吟游诗人会去如此不受保护的市场。不过如我们所见，雕像内容还有瑞斯拉夫至关重要的两项配件：他久经训练的飞鹰和风驰电掣的良驹。 冬雨冲刷着通往南方的道路，穿过希罗帝尔西部莽原流入威伦森林。所以皇帝领军取道北路，瑞斯拉夫王领小股卫队在今天的黄金大道的一处低地迎接了他们。据史载，帝国军庞大到连安内奎那野兽在数百里开外都能听见他们的行进声。就连记载此事的史家都坦承自己会害怕到不由自主发抖。 然而，据说瑞斯拉夫面无惧色。他以完美的礼仪姿态敬告皇帝，说他的军队过于庞大，区区斯金格勒王国根本无法容纳。 　　 “下次来前，”瑞斯拉夫说，“先写封信来。” 格里乌斯和大多数阿莱西亚皇帝很像，都不是有着幽默感的人。他觉得瑞斯拉夫怕不是中了谢尔格拉的邪，他命侍卫擒拿这可悲的狂人。正于此刻，斯金格勒王高举其臂，扬鹰于空。那是他军队久等的信号。阿莱西亚军已全部进入他们的射程之内。 瑞斯拉夫王一行当即策马西奔，如史书所载他们好像“被狂野的凯娜瑞丝亲吻过”。瑞斯拉夫不敢回首确认，但他的计划进行得很顺利。山口最东端被滚落的巨岩封住，阿莱西亚军只能向西。斯金格勒弓兵们远远地自侧近高原上万箭齐发，无需担心遭到反击。极怒的格里乌斯皇帝从莽原到高地一路追赶瑞斯拉夫，把斯金格勒远抛在后，但他的军队却越来越小。 在高地的深山老林内，帝国军遭遇了瑞斯拉夫的岳父科瓦奇王的伏兵。阿莱西亚军貌似在数量上仍超过他们的对手，但他们筋疲力尽，士气也被箭海矢雨消耗殆尽。战斗持续一小时后，他们北撤向至今亦归属帝国的领土，并于继续向东北方败逃，回到尼本奈抚平他们身心的创伤。 而此役正是阿莱西亚霸权由盛转衰的开始。西科洛文的诸王加入了科瓦奇和斯金格勒的同盟，结成反帝国侵略同一阵线。莱恩领导的迪伦尼家族备受鼓舞，宣布于在高岩取缔阿莱西亚改革教派，并开始向帝国领土推进。新任天际至高王霍格，即今人所谓“精灵杀手”，虽然共有着与皇帝一样的仇外情结，却也加入了反帝国阵列。霍格战死后的继承人，阿特莫拉的“伊斯米尔”武夫哈斯，发扬霍格的遗志继续奋战，并开创了他自己名留青史的丰功伟业。 而英勇的斯金格勒王，几乎单枪匹马直面皇帝大军，并首度敲响了帝国的丧钟。理所当然地得到了“正义的瑞斯拉夫王”称号。
